engagement_title: Aurelian Skin first retail season: bring an eight SKU three afternoon shoot to one clinical range, recover the lost mark off a photographed carton, and carry both onto the store pages and the launch set
vertical: Beauty and personal care, clinical skincare actives, direct to consumer plus a twelve door specialty retail rollout (Boston, Massachusetts)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork 'premium clinical skincare brand, logo, label and packaging' launch post quoted in the ledger's grounding_note, which asks for a cohesive credible visual identity across the product line plus explicitly 'print-ready files and editable source files', with a stated aesthetic of clean, minimalist, science-driven, premium but not luxurious, strong typography, whitespace and white-background ecommerce imagery. Co-anchor: the Upwork packaging post (cand_64, db_i 271) asking to 'create premium, visually appealing packaging for our beauty and skincare product line' with 'editable source files' among the deliverables. Both real posts name no client, so the line is laundered to the coined fictional brand Aurelian Skin. The ledger's own repositioning note concedes that from-scratch identity art and free-form layout composition are not connector work; CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) changes what the honest fuller commission is, because HTML authoring now produces a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes and an ink-level trace off photographed printed collateral recovers a real mark. So this is that client's actual job: the identity is RECOVERED rather than invented, and the editable source files they asked for are real.
client_one_liner: Our eight launch products were shot over three afternoons and do not look like one range, our logo file is gone and all that survives is a photo of a carton, and the store goes live in March.
client_brief:
Aurelian Skin, first retail season

We are a two person clinical skincare line in Boston. Eight products, all actives led, sold for a year to a waiting list and through two dermatology practices. In March we open our own store online and go into a specialty chain's twelve doors, so everything a customer sees changes at once.

The honest state of our pictures. A photographer friend shot all eight bottles across three afternoons in her studio on a pale sweep, one at a time. Each is a good photograph. Put them in a row the way a store page does and they are not one range: some read cooler, one sits noticeably brighter than the rest. We need them to read as one line. Clean white behind them, square, the bottle centred, nothing touching the edge, no shadows or reflections invented for them. The chain also wants versions with nothing behind them at all, because their page puts products on a coloured band of their own.

We shot a second set of close ups of the raw actives, the drop on glass, the pipette, the crystal. Those carry the ingredient panel on each product page. They are tighter and they were shot on a different day.

Then the part we are nervous about. We lost our logo file when our first designer's drive failed. What survives is a photograph of an outer carton with the mark printed on it. We need the mark back as artwork we can use at any size on any colour, and it has to still be our mark.

We also need the launch set: a wide one for paid social, a square one and a tall one for stories, all in one working file we can change ourselves, because the date and the featured product will move. In the launch pictures the bottles should sit on something with a soft shadow under them rather than float. The store wants the opposite, so both looks have to exist.

Our products are thirty four to sixty eight dollars. Our customer is twenty six to forty two and she reads the ingredient list before the copy. It should look like a laboratory with good taste: cool, quiet, a lot of white, nothing decorative. Not a spa, and not a discount aisle. And a note on what you did, what type we are on, and anything we should know about using the mark.
price_band_and_audience: Prestige-mass clinical actives at 34 to 68 dollars per SKU, buyer 26 to 42 and ingredient literate. The band is load-bearing: at this price the range must sit on a cool near-clinical white, with restrained type, generous white space, no props and no styling that reads as ritual or spa. The same eight products at a 12 dollar mass band would correctly be shot warm, saturated, prop-heavy and tightly cropped to fill the tile, and shipping that treatment here reads downmarket and kills the clinical claim. Push the other way into near-black grounds, extreme sparseness and cosmetic gloss and it becomes a 200 dollar luxury conserve of a skincare line, which misprices a 34 dollar serum. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,200 to 2,600 dollars fixed.

assets_supplied.name: aurelian_launch_shoot/ (8 frames, 8688 x 5792)
assets_supplied.kind: Product photography shot in-house by a friend across three afternoons, one SKU per frame, pale sweep, fifty megapixel body.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "All eight, same sweep, same corner of her studio. Some read cooler than others and one is brighter, but they are good pictures."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The frames are far larger than anything downstream expects, and the one-call background knockout silently reduces oversized inputs and reports it in no message and no error, only as a downscaled entry inside the returned tradeoffs object with output dimensions below source dimensions. The returned cutout is clean, complete and correct looking at preview scale; the shortfall only appears when the square store tile is cut from it, and by then the only route back to the retailer's tile size is interpolation, which the crop tool will perform up to a two times cap while saying so only inside its own tradeoffs. Separately the 30ml frosted-glass SKU sits at almost the luminance of the sweep at its shoulder, so subject detection has no contrast there and hands back a soft rim on that frame alone.

assets_supplied.name: aurelian_actives_macros/ (8 frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Macro close ups of the raw actives themselves, shot on a later day: a drop on glass, a pipette tip, a crystal, a powder cone.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The ingredient close ups for the product pages. Tighter, different day."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Each frame is a single small element on a near empty ground. A subject-focused crop on that kind of art returns a confident looking result at a plausible size while reporting its uncertainty only as a numeric detection confidence and a detection bounding box buried in the metadata, and on sparse art it can lock onto a specular highlight or a reflection instead of the subject and hand back a crop that clips most of it, at full success. Which of the eight this happens to is a property of each frame's own contrast. Separately there are eight macros for eight products but two of them are the same active shot twice and one launch product has no macro at all, which no filename or column reveals.

assets_supplied.name: aurelian_carton_front.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of an outer carton standing on a bench, the mark printed in one deep ink on pale board: a compound lockup of small-caps type set around a monogram, separated by a hairline rule.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only place our mark still exists. We lost the file when the drive failed."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a compound lockup on a photographed substrate, which behaves nothing like a flat scan. A prompt naming the substrate returns the carton rather than the ink; a compound prompt returns the type ring and silently drops the monogram and the hairline rule while looking entirely plausible; and background removal on the ring returns a solid opaque disc because an enclosed interior cannot be punched. The ink and the board also run close in value on the shadowed right third of the carton face.

assets_supplied.name: aurelian_copy.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text: the eight product names, their INCI lines, the claims cleared by their regulatory reviewer, and the launch prices.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The copy as approved. The INCI lines cannot be edited."

assets_supplied.name: aurelian_reference_page.png
assets_supplied.kind: Screengrab of a store page layout the founders like, from a category-neutral retailer, supplied as a proportion reference.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Roughly how much room we want the product to have."

acceptance_bar: All eight store tiles sit on a clean white ground, square at the retailer's tile size, the bottle optically centred with nothing touching the edge, and the cut edge holds when looked at close up rather than at preview scale.

No delivered file exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions, and no crop's returned tradeoff report carries an upscale entry. A tile that reaches its size by being enlarged fails even if it looks acceptable.

The eight bottles read as ONE range when laid in a row as a store page lays them: one white point, one black point, one crop logic, one height in frame. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is named, not shipped at eighty percent.
Every ingredient close up actually contains the whole of the thing it is a close up of. A tile is not delivered by being filled.
Every launch product has its own ingredient image, and no image stands in for two products.

The mark is placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath it, and it still reads as our mark at the size it actually reproduces and reversed on colour.
In the launch file the mark is live vector shapes and the words are text we can retype, not a picture of a layout.
All three launch canvases are in ONE working file, each keeping its own canvas size, and we also get the self contained source it was built from.
In the launch pictures the bottles read as sitting on a surface rather than floating, on every canvas and not only the first one.
One type system across all three canvases, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the actual weight used.
The note states, per photograph, what was applied and why that frame differs from its neighbours, plus every resize any tool reported and anything about the mark we should know.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted HERE and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_remove_background (transparent and backgroundColor routes), image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor), image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Every raster decision in the commission. It fixes one clinical target from the best lit frame and corrects each of the eight toward it one call at a time, triages the knockout routes between the coherent opaque bottles and the frosted SKU whose shoulder has no contrast, produces both the white-ground store tiles and the genuinely transparent variants the retailer's coloured band needs, crops the sparse macros through explicit selections where the subject-focused route cannot be trusted, and recovers the mark at ink level off a photographed carton with the vector hygiene the tracing tool does not do for you.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The launch set as one native editable document carrying three roots at three canvas sizes, which is the only surface in the connector that does free-form fixed-canvas layout. Every photograph must be pulled down and inlined as image data because a URL renders as an empty grey box at full success, the mark goes in as inline SVG so it stays vector, family and weight are declared on every text element, and the payload goes by uploaded URL because inlined photography passes the inline threshold immediately.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Fonts
adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system for all three launch canvases and the handover. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land on clinical rather than spa. Numeric weights are non-standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, every name must be laundered into canonical PostScript form before the kit call because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug or it falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one frame the founders do not have, a clean laboratory bench atmosphere band for the wide launch canvas, IP-clean and at genuine camera scale with generative-tech candidates excluded. The Boards half persists the shared selects set the two founders sign off from, placed within the twelve-per-call cap, with a partial success read as partial and vector understood to be unacceptable there.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching a pixel.
trajectory.judgement: The store tiles and macros are raster work with a hard spec; the launch set has to be an authored fixed canvas document because the client needs to edit it next season and nothing else in the connector composes free-form layout. The brief already pins the destination, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable, and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline: a manifest keyed by role so that forty artefacts later the agent still knows which URL is which frame.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Preview all eight bottle frames and all eight macros and triage them: which afternoon each belongs to, which sit hot, which subject runs close to the sweep in value, which macro is sparse, and which product each macro actually shows.
trajectory.judgement: The client asserts eight products and eight macros. The pictures are the only thing that can settle whether that is eight different actives, and reading the macros against the product list is slower than counting files and is not the same thing.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering illuminant, tilt, subject contrast against the ground, and macro identity.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes the subject and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix one clinical target off the best lit frame and correct each of the eight toward it with its own call, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a set, not eight good pictures. One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong for frames shot under three different rigs; the agent has to hold one destination and reach it by different routes.
trajectory.produces: Eight graded masters at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Masked corrections where a global grade goes wrong, selecting by the material's own visual properties rather than by the object it sits on.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the whole gate: naming the substrate pulls the selection to the sweep. The amber-glass SKU and the frosted one need confined corrections the other six do not.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a whole-frame move would have taken the glass green or the sweep muddy.

trajectory.action: Knock the eight out: the store's white ground for the listing tiles, and genuinely transparent variants for the retailer's coloured band. Read every returned tradeoffs object rather than the success message.
trajectory.judgement: The tradeoffs array is the only channel that reports what the tool did to the frame's dimensions, and it carries no warning language. The frosted SKU's shoulder will not behave like the other seven.
trajectory.produces: Eight white-ground plates and eight transparent variants, each with its returned tradeoffs recorded.

trajectory.action: Cut the square store tiles at the retailer's spec, product optically centred with clear air at every edge.
trajectory.judgement: Optical centring is not geometric centring on a bottle with a tall cap, and the retailer rejects anything touching the edge.
trajectory.produces: Eight store tiles at spec plus eight on-colour variants.

trajectory.action: Crop the macros to the ingredient panel ratio, reading the detection confidence and detection bounds each crop returns, and grade them as their own family to a target that does not fight the bottle family.
trajectory.judgement: A confident looking crop on sparse art is not evidence. Two families on one page may sit on two targets, but each has to agree with itself and they must not fight where they meet.
trajectory.produces: Ingredient panel tiles with their confidence readings recorded, and a second graded family.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the laboratory bench band, filter to photography, exclude generative-tech results, license and download at full resolution.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to the clinical target, not the prettiest thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP-clean, camera-scale frame.

trajectory.action: Recover the mark off the carton: an ink-level selection naming the mark's own visual properties, correct polarity, a bounds crop from the selection's own bbox, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full-canvas ground path removed.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions the tools do not make: how to word the selection so it takes the ink and not the board, which polarity to trace, and whether the two-colour trace or the colour-accurate knockout plate is the deliverable. Background removal is the wrong instrument on an enclosed ring.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent mark plus a colour-accurate variant.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's, judged against a 34 to 68 dollar clinical band and an ingredient-literate reader. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one-kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self-contained HTML with three roots at three canvas sizes, inline every photograph as image data, place the mark as inline SVG inside an explicitly sized top-left anchored wrapper, declare family and weight on every text element, let each root declare its own canvas, then upload the file and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto-sized right-anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed-size set. The design work is how much air the clinical band takes and how large the mark sits.
trajectory.produces: One export-ready HTML carrying the whole launch set, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at canvas one, and parse the returned per-canvas markup for canvases two and three.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition preview only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at page one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected first canvas, and a per-canvas markup audit for the other two.

trajectory.action: Create the selects board, add the graded set and the licensed frame within the per-call placement cap, re-sending only the entries the response names as failed, then write the handover note.
trajectory.judgement: A 201 is partial success, and the vector mark is not boardable so it belongs in the note instead. The note has to be specific enough that the next freelancer does not repeat the archaeology.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the one-call knockout gives back a picture the store tile can still be cut from. The captures are 8688 x 5792 and the knockout silently reduces oversized inputs, reporting it in no message, no warning and no error: the only trace is a downscaled entry inside the returned tradeoffs object with output dimensions below source dimensions. Nothing in the tool's description mentions a size ceiling and nothing states where it sits. The returned cutout is clean, complete and correct at preview scale. The shortfall appears only when the square tile is cut, and the only route back to the retailer's size is interpolation, which the crop tool performs up to a two times cap while reporting it solely inside its own tradeoffs.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering does not dodge it. The defensible order is straighten, grade, knock out at source scale, then choose the crop, precisely so the crop is chosen after the cut edge is visible; there is no read-ahead for the ceiling and no parameter that controls it. An agent that cropped first would be trading away crop choice for a reason nobody has told it. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for square store pictures and says nothing about resolution; the no-enlargement line in the acceptance bar is the client's standing trade requirement, not a disclosure that a tool shrinks things. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is a different route, decided per frame: crop to the subject's own bounds at native scale so the knockout receives a frame under the ceiling, or abandon the one-call knockout for a material-named sweep selection inverted and filled to white.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-plan the knockout route for all eight frames, re-derive every white-ground plate and every transparent variant through the new route, and re-read both the downscaled and the upscale entries in every returned tradeoffs object before any tile is called delivered.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Eight store tiles that are either short of the retailer's required size and bounced at upload, or brought to size by interpolation and shipped soft, on a clinical line whose entire claim is precision.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the thing the launch look is built on. The client asked for the bottles to sit on a surface with a soft shadow rather than float. Authored the natural way that is a blurred element or a layered shadow, and the importer discards a blur filter outright and truncates a layered shadow to its first layer, with no warning and a successful response. The returned per-canvas markup is the only channel that reports it, and the document's own rendition returns the first artboard only, so the square and tall canvases can be checked no other way. Whether what survives still reads as a bottle sitting on a surface, or as a bottle floating beside a grey smudge, is visible only after the export.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the drop happens at import and the import is the last step; and doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for a look, and the acceptance line about sitting rather than floating is the client's own art direction, not a warning. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to produce a DIFFERENT upstream asset, a bottle composited onto a solid house ground in a single knockout call so the ground is part of the raster, or to reduce the shadow to the single layer the importer keeps and re-judge whether it still reads, and then re-compose the canvas around whichever it is.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the launch masters through a different knockout route or re-cast the shadow as the single surviving layer, re-author the HTML around that decision, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and audit all three canvases from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A launch set delivered as an editable file in which the bottles float on flat white on the two canvases nobody looked at, with the export having reported success throughout.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether a subject-aware crop can find the subject in the ingredient close ups at all. Those frames are one small element on a near empty ground. The crop tool answers a subject-focused request on that kind of art with a confident looking result at a plausible size and reports its uncertainty only as a numeric detection confidence and a detection bounding box buried in the metadata; on sparse art it can lock onto a specular highlight or a reflection and return a crop that clips most of the subject, at full success. Which of the eight this happens to is a property of each frame's own contrast and is not visible by looking at the frame.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) There is no ordering that avoids it and no parameter that prevents it. The safe route, an explicit selection with a returned bounding box driving a bounds crop, costs three calls per frame and is what a competent agent adopts once the cheap route has been seen to fail. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the macros are tighter and were shot on a different day. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the affected frames go through a different chain, not the same chain again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read the detection confidence and bounds on every macro crop, and for each frame below a defensible threshold re-do the crop through an explicit selection of the material by its own visual properties, a returned bounding box and a padded bounds crop, then inspect each result rather than the response.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Ingredient panels showing a third of a droplet and the edge of a pipette, on a line whose customer buys on ingredient literacy and reads that panel before the copy.

deliverables.name: Aurelian store tile set, white ground and on-colour
deliverables.spec: Eight square store tiles at the retailer's tile size on a clean white ground, product optically centred with clear air at every edge and a cut edge that holds under close inspection, plus eight genuinely transparent variants for the chain's coloured band. Every output at or below its source pixel dimensions with the returned tradeoff record for each. This is one set with one cut logic, not one picture at several sizes.

deliverables.name: Aurelian house photography, bottles and actives
deliverables.spec: Eight bottle masters brought to one clinical target (one white point, one black point, one height in frame) plus a separately targeted family of ingredient close ups, one per launch product with none standing in for two, plus one licensed camera-scale bench frame graded into the same world. Per frame parameter log, including one line on why each frame differs from its neighbours.

deliverables.name: Recovered Aurelian mark
deliverables.spec: The compound lockup recovered from a photograph of a printed carton as placeable scalable vector geometry with a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full-canvas rectangle riding along, delivered as both a single-colour mark and a colour-accurate variant, holding its hairline rule and its monogram at the size it actually reproduces on the launch canvases and reversed on colour.

deliverables.name: Launch set, wide, square and tall, as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: One native editable Express document carrying three roots at three canvas sizes, with live editable text in one licensed type system, the mark as real vector shapes, every photograph carried as embedded image data rather than a reference, and the bottles reading as sitting rather than floating on all three canvases. Delivered with the self-contained source HTML, which is the durable half: the client edits the document next season and the source guarantees the design survives regardless.

deliverables.name: Handover note and selects board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording per photograph what was applied and why that frame differs from its neighbours, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight, every resize any tool reported with the frame it applied to, the macro-to-product reconciliation and anything the founders should know about using the recovered mark. Paired with a persistent shareable selects board carrying the graded set and the licensed frame with nothing silently dropped.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are raster work and which need an authored fixed canvas document, given that only one surface here composes free-form layout.
Whether the eight bottle frames are one shoot. The client believes they nearly are; the row is the only place that can be settled.
How far to push the two off-rig frames before they stop being worth saving, versus naming them.
Knockout route per frame: the one-call route for coherent opaque bottles versus a material-named sweep selection inverted and filled for the frosted SKU whose shoulder has no contrast.
Whether to trust a confident looking crop on sparse macro art or to spend three calls per frame on an explicit selection.
Whether eight macro files for eight products is eight actives, and how to say so when it is not.

Selection prompt wording on the carton: naming the substrate takes the board, naming the ink's own visual properties takes the mark, and background removal on an enclosed ring is the wrong instrument entirely.
Which mark variant carries the launch canvases, judged at reproduction size on the actual ground rather than at full canvas.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a clinical band and an ingredient-literate reader, plus the real numeric weight per family.
Whether a licensed bench frame joins the world the eight bottles live in or reads as bought.
How much air the launch canvases carry. At this band restraint is the design; a dense, benefit-led tile is a correct-looking wrong answer.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of skincare bottles. IDENTITY: these are this line's actual eight products with their actual labels and their actual regulatory-cleared claims, and the mark must be RECOVERED off a photographed carton rather than reinvented, because a regenerated mark is a different company's logo. SPEC: the retailer needs eight square tiles at an exact size with nothing touching the edge and no interpolated pixels, plus transparent variants for their own coloured band, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the launch set is defined by being editable, since the date and the featured product will move and the founders explicitly cannot re-commission. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did this knockout come back smaller than it went in, does this crop actually contain the droplet, did the shadow survive the import.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), four surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and detection_confidence, fill_area, remove_background in both the transparent and backgroundColor forms, and vectorize are all verified headless across 27 live calls. The three checkpoints rest on documented findings rather than assumptions: remove_background SILENTLY DOWNSCALES oversized inputs and reports it only as a downscaled tradeoff entry; fit extract with a prompt focus silently mis-crops sparse art (observed at detection_confidence 0.459, clipping 60 percent of the subject while reporting success); and the importer DROPS filter blur entirely and TRUNCATES multi-layer box-shadow to layer one, both at HTTP success. Alpha survives crops at outputFileType png (verified 13,371 partial-alpha pixels preserved), so the on-colour variants are real. VECTOR: the substrate-versus-ink prompt asymmetry, the compound-mark partial selection, the solid-disc failure of remove_background on an enclosed ring, the missing viewBox and the opaque path zero are all live findings, and the acceptance bar scores the hygiene the tool does not perform. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, the product is a genuine editable dcx findable by asset_search, and the rendition preview is documented as PAGE 1 ONLY, which is why verification is split between the rendition and the returned markup. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes the 70 KB threshold immediately. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end including a browser proving licensed faces load. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, license returned a real 7360x4912 JPEG, and boards persist with a hard cap of 12 placements per call and 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no text-to-image, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no fill_text, no animate_design, no batch above 20.

engagement_title: Corner and Cure spring changeover: bring two services of dish photography to one house look, rebuild the printed dish cards from the file that went to press, and hand back the counter screens, the delivery tiles and the insert
vertical: Food and hospitality, independent all-day cafe and counter service, forty covers (Providence, Rhode Island)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork post quoted in the ledger's grounding_note for a food-delivery storefront, whose client says 'we have the assets, they just need to be pulled together so they look like they were shot in the same image ... one cohesive, intentional photo, not a collage'. Co-anchor: the Upwork food photo-editing brief (db_i 1113) asking for 'color correction, white balance, exposure to create a cohesive presentation' across a set 'close to the goal but need tweaking', on a quick turnaround. Third anchor: the Upwork neighbourhood cafe menu brief wanting 'Proficiency in Adobe InDesign', a 'Strong sense of typography, layout, and print design', print-ready files AND editable source, in a warm and elevated register. The real clients name nobody, so the room is laundered to the coined fictional Corner and Cure. The ledger's repositioning note conceded that a from-scratch menu is not connector scope; v3 changes what the honest fuller commission is, because a flat press PDF converts back into a live merge template and HTML authoring produces a native editable document, so the printed cards and the designed collateral are both real here.
client_one_liner: Ten dishes shot across two services look like two kitchens, the printer who built our dish cards has retired and we only have the file that went to press, and the spring menu lands in five weeks.
client_brief:
Corner and Cure, spring menu changeover

We are an all-day place on the west side of Providence. Sandwiches and bowls at lunch, small plates and wine after five, forty covers and a counter. Danny cooks, I run the front. The spring menu lands in five weeks and everything that carries a picture of our food changes with it: the screens over the counter, the printed cards on the tables, the delivery app storefront and our own posts.

We had a photographer in for a day and she shot ten dishes, half at the lunch service and half after the pendants come on at four. They are good pictures. They are not the same picture. Some are warm and some are cold and the marble looks like two different marbles. We need them to look like one kitchen: warm, generous, food that looks like somebody cooked it, not styled to death and not flattened out.

We need them at three shapes, which is where we always come unstuck: wide for the screens over the counter, small and square for the delivery app, and a strip for the printed card.

The printed cards are the awkward part. Our printer ran them last spring, one card per dish, and we do not have whatever she built them in. She has retired. All we have is the file she sent to press. The cards themselves are right and we want them kept, but every dish, every description and every price on them is changing and two dishes are coming off. We also want a proof of each card the two of us can look at before anything goes to print, and a separate file per dish so we can send one card to the printer when we change one thing mid season.

The dish copy comes out of our till and Danny writes it. Please do not reword it or cut it. We have had that done to us and the allergen line matters.

We would also like one wide picture of the counter and the room for the top of the delivery storefront. We have never managed to take one that works.

Everything designed has to come back as something the two of us can open and change prices in. And a short note on what you did to the pictures and what type we are on.

Our mains are sixteen to twenty four dollars and our regulars come twice a week. It should feel like a good neighbourhood room, not a tasting menu and not a chain.
price_band_and_audience: Mid-market all-day cafe, mains 16 to 24 dollars, wine by the glass 11 to 15, regulars 25 to 45 who come twice a week and know the staff. The band is load-bearing. At this price the grade is warm, generous and slightly rustic, the portions read as real portions, the type is large enough to read across a counter, and prices sit plainly inside the run of copy. A 90 dollar tasting-menu treatment (cool, sparse, near-black grounds, food styled into abstraction, prices exiled to a discreet column) misprices the room and reads as pretension on a 19 dollar bowl. Pushed the other way into flat, over-lit, hyper-saturated tiles with a starburst price it becomes the 9 dollar fast-casual chain the owners explicitly rule out. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every merge field binds. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,100 to 2,400 dollars fixed.

assets_supplied.name: service_shots/ (10 frames, 6000 x 4000)
assets_supplied.kind: Dish photography shot in one day across two services, five at lunch and five after four o'clock, on the marble pass.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Ten dishes, one photographer, one day. Some warm, some cold, and the marble looks like two marbles."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two things nobody at the cafe can tell you. Four of the ten are square-on overheads shot at three by two, and the counter screens are sixteen by nine: cropping an overhead to that shape takes away exactly the plate. The crop tool answers that with a requires-expand tradeoff carrying pre-filled arguments rather than a failure, and whether the marble it then generates carries the same grain, warmth and specular as the real marble is a property of each frame and each seed. Separately the burnt-butter gnocchi sits at almost the value of its own plate, so a subject selection on it fringes where a selection on the other nine is clean, and one frame carries the ticket rail and a squeeze bottle in the top corner, which only a crop can lawfully remove and which therefore changes what that frame can carry at the wide shape.

assets_supplied.name: dishcard_2025_print.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's flat press PDF for the table dish cards, 105 x 148 mm portrait, fonts embedded, produced from a real page layout so it converts cleanly. Carries the dish name, a description line, an allergen line, a provenance line and a price, plus a placed photograph of the dish.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What she sent to press last spring. We do not have the working file and she has retired. The cards are right, keep them."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two facts nothing announces. First, the placed photograph splits the copy into TWO text frames rather than the five the printed card implies, and the split falls in an unobvious place, so some of the five lines share one continuous story and must be driven by ordered offset arithmetic inside it while the rest sit alone. Second, the mapping readout of that multi-line story silently omits the run holding the allergen line while KEEPING its line break, so the string still reads as well-formed prose and every character offset after it is short by exactly that run's length. The validator returns valid on the resulting arithmetic, the placeholder step reports success, and two of the five fields never become placeholders. Only an independent reconstruction of the story from the exported document's own concatenated content runs, followed by a round trip and a search of the prepared file, exposes either fact.

assets_supplied.name: dishes.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Export from the till system, one row per dish, with columns for name, description, allergens, provenance, price and a photo filename.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Straight out of the till. Danny writes the copy and it is final, please do not reword or cut it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three faults, none stated. The export carries eleven rows for ten dishes, because a winter special the till still emits has never been retired. The headers are mixed case with trailing spaces and the photo column is a plain header holding bare filenames that neither match the delivered frames nor satisfy the merge's own image-column contract. And two rows carry the takeaway price rather than the dine-in price, because the till exports both columns and the wrong one was pulled, which is visible only by reading the export against the owner's own menu text.

assets_supplied.name: house_words.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Half a page of tone language from the owner: burnt butter, scrubbed oak, the good bread, warm but never orange, plain-spoken.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "How we talk about the room."

assets_supplied.name: spring_menu_draft.txt
assets_supplied.kind: The owner's own draft of the spring menu with the ten dishes in service order and the dine-in prices.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The menu as it will run."

acceptance_bar: The ten dishes read as ONE kitchen when laid together as the counter screens run them: one white point, one warmth in the food, one black point, one crop logic. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is named, not shipped at eighty percent.

No delivered file exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions and no crop's tradeoff report carries an upscale entry. Where a shape could not be reached by cropping, the note says what was done instead and to which frame.
Every wide counter tile is a picture that can hold at counter-screen size. A tile is not delivered by being filled, and any generated surface in it must sit with the real surface beside it.

Exactly one printed card per dish on the spring menu, in menu order, with no extra card and no missing card. If the number shipped is not the number we told you, the note says which row was left out and why.
Every card carries all five lines the 2025 card carried: name, description, allergens, provenance and price. A card missing a line is a failed card even if the file opened fine.
Nothing in the till copy may be reworded, shortened, re-spaced or abbreviated, and the allergen line must be present on every card.
Every card carries its own dish's photograph, and no card repeats another card's photograph.
Each per-dish file actually contains the dish its filename claims, established by opening the file rather than by the order the files came back in.
The proofs are rendered at true print resolution at card trim rather than at screen scale.

The designed collateral comes back as a native editable document the two of us can change prices in, with every photograph actually visible in it, the price list as a real table, and every text element carrying its licensed face at that family's own weight.

A written note: the parameters applied per dish with one line on why that dish differs from its neighbours, the type system by role, every roster row questioned and what was done about it, and every resize any tool reported.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_invert_selection, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor), image_generative_expand, image_apply_auto_tone
adobe_surfaces.role: Fixes one house target off the best lunch frame and corrects each of the ten toward it with its own call, because a single batched call applies one identical parameter set and half the set was lit by pendants. Runs masked corrections where the late-service frames carry two illuminants inside one frame and where one dish sits at the value of its own plate. Derives three families of crop at native scale, and carries the sole sanctioned generative call on the overhead frames that cannot reach the counter-screen shape by cropping, then has to bring the generated surface into the house target before it is usable.

adobe_surfaces.surface: InDesign layout and data merge
adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml (twice, once to read the converted document and once to audit the prepared template), generate_indd_mapping_prompt (as generator and as validator), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout (application/x-indesign and application/pdf, additionalImageFiles, recordRange), document_render_layout (resolution 300, createSeparateFiles, pageRange in N-N form)
adobe_surfaces.role: The print spine. The printer's flat card becomes a live merge template with no working file to start from, the till export becomes the data source, and the run produces the press cards, the per-dish single files and the 300 DPI proofs the owners sign off from. This is the only surface in the connector that does record per page variable data, and the true story text must be reconstructed from the exported document rather than trusted from a convenience readout.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The designed collateral as one native editable document at mixed canvas sizes: the sixteen by nine counter screen, the A5 printed insert page, and the square and four by five posts. Every photograph inlined as image data because a URL renders as an empty grey box at full success, the price list as a genuine table, family and weight declared per text element, each root declaring its own canvas size, and the payload routed by uploaded URL.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Fonts
adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system across the counter screen, the insert and the posts, and the one place the agent's typographic authorship exists at all, since no font from this surface can reach the printed card (there is no font file download, so the card's typography is the retired printer's). The recommender refuses to pair, the numeric weight per family is non-standard, one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the wide counter and room frame the owners have never managed to take, IP-clean and at camera scale, with generative-tech candidates excluded. The Boards half persists the shared set the two owners and the kitchen brief from, placed within the twelve-per-call cap with a partial success read as partial.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle the split: printed cards to the merge surface because they are record per page against a layout the client wants kept, designed collateral to authored fixed canvases because the owners must edit prices, photography to imaging.
trajectory.judgement: Authoring the cards from scratch throws away the layout the client asked to keep; trying to merge the collateral finds that record per page cannot produce four different canvas sizes.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier.

trajectory.action: Upload the press PDF, the till export, the ten dish frames and the menu draft, holding each returned presigned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A manifest keyed by role, so that thirty artefacts later the agent still knows which URL is which dish.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Preview all ten frames and triage: which service each belongs to, which carry more than one illuminant inside the frame, which subject runs close to its own plate, which are overheads, and what is in frame that should not be.
trajectory.judgement: The client says warm and cold; the useful distinction is whether a frame has one light or two, because those need different corrections to reach the same place. Reading each frame against the menu draft also settles which dish it actually is.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note: illuminant count, tilt, subject contrast, native aspect, in-frame distractions and dish identity.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels, and the overheads have the least edge to spare.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed.

trajectory.action: Fix one house target off the best lunch frame and correct each of the ten toward it with its own call, recording parameters.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a set. Six frames need a small move and four need a materially different one to land in the same place, and the agent has to hold one destination rather than optimise each frame.
trajectory.produces: Ten graded masters at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Masked corrections where a global move is wrong: confine the correction to the plate on the late-service frames, and handle the dish that sits at the value of its own plate differently from the nine that behave.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the gate: naming the plate pulls the selection to the china, naming the food's own visual properties pulls it to the food. A fringing mask has to be recognised as fringing rather than accepted because the call succeeded.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a whole-frame move would have taken the marble blue or the food orange.

trajectory.action: Derive the square delivery tiles and the printed strip crops at native scale, reading every returned tradeoffs object rather than the success message.
trajectory.judgement: The tradeoffs array is the only signal that a crop clipped, that a detection was weak, or that an output was interpolated toward the two times cap.
trajectory.produces: Delivery tiles and strip crops with their tradeoff records.

trajectory.action: Derive the wide counter tiles at sixteen by nine, reading confidence and tradeoffs, and decide per frame between a tighter crop that loses the whole plate and expanding the short axis.
trajectory.judgement: On a square-on overhead there is no crop to sixteen by nine that keeps the plate, so the choice is between showing a detail instead of the dish and generating surface. Whichever is chosen has to sit with the real marble beside it.
trajectory.produces: Ten wide counter tiles and a record of which route each frame took.

trajectory.action: Bring any generated surface into the house target and lay the ten counter tiles in a row as the screens run them.
trajectory.judgement: Judging the row rather than the frame, at the only moment the comparison is available.
trajectory.produces: A counter tile row judged as a row, with any frame that will not join it named.

trajectory.surface: Data preparation and Creative Cloud storage
trajectory.action: Reconcile the till export against the owner's menu draft and the triage findings, normalise it into a merge-shaped data file with an at-prefixed image column holding bare filenames, upload the graded card images and build the image map against it.
trajectory.judgement: Real reconciliation work: the row count and the menu do not agree, two prices came from the wrong column, and the agent has to decide what is its call and what is the owners' to confirm, and how to say so.
trajectory.produces: The merge data file, the uploaded card images, the image map and a first list of roster questions.

trajectory.action: Convert the press PDF to a native document, export the interchange file from it, unzip it and read what actually came across: how many text frames, how many graphic frames, the real integer page item ids and the bounds, then reconstruct each frame's true story text by concatenating its content runs.
trajectory.judgement: The mapping strategy is a property of the client's PDF, not of the plan. Per-frame mapping is only available if the lines came across as separate frames; otherwise every field is offset arithmetic inside one story, and the arithmetic has to be computed from the document rather than from any convenience readout.
trajectory.produces: The converted document, its interchange export, a real frame inventory and an independently reconstructed story string.

trajectory.action: Author the mapping against the reconstructed text covering all five copy fields plus the image frame, pass it through the validator, prepare the template, then export the interchange file from the RESULT and search the story for every placeholder the mapping claimed to create.
trajectory.judgement: Not accepting a success message as evidence. Nothing in the chain instructs this verification and nothing warns if it is skipped, and it is the only place the mapping's real yield is visible before pages exist. Rows sharing a uid must be ordered so their positions do not corrupt one another.
trajectory.produces: A prepared merge template whose placeholder inventory has been independently confirmed.

trajectory.action: Merge to a native document with the per-row images bound, then render the press cards and the client proofs at 300 from that document.
trajectory.judgement: Route matters and it is irreversible in practice: merging straight to raster forfeits real resolution and merging straight to press forfeits the ability to render per-record files afterwards. Merging to the native document first keeps both branches open.
trajectory.produces: The press card run at card trim and 300 DPI proofs for sign off.

trajectory.action: Read every rendered card against the menu at trim rather than at proof scale, line by line and photograph by photograph.
trajectory.judgement: Reading the output rather than the log. A missing line and a wrongly bound photograph both look like success at the API boundary and both look fine at screen scale.
trajectory.produces: A card-by-card reconciliation against the menu.

trajectory.action: Produce the per-dish single card files and name each to its dish, verifying identity by opening each file rather than by its position in the returned list.
trajectory.judgement: The order of returned per-record artefacts is not trustworthy on every route, and naming ten files by position is the fast wrong answer that sends the printer the wrong card.
trajectory.produces: Ten single card files, named to dish, each identity-verified by inspection.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the wide counter and room frame, filter to photography, exclude generative-tech results, license and download at full resolution, then grade it toward the house target and lay it against the ten.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose light and whose surfaces can join this room, not the prettiest thumbnail. Two interiors that look equally warm at 240 pixels can be a full grade and a different stone apart at full resolution.
trajectory.produces: One licensed camera-scale frame, in or out, with the reasoning recorded.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit for the whole system.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's and has to land on a good neighbourhood room at sixteen to twenty four dollars, readable across a counter. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name.
trajectory.produces: A one-kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self-contained HTML with four roots at four canvas sizes, inline every photograph as image data, set the price list as a real table, declare family and weight on every text element, anchor from the top left with explicit sizes, then upload it and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto-sized right-anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed-size set. The design work is how much air the band takes and where the prices sit.
trajectory.produces: One export-ready HTML carrying the whole collateral set, retained as the durable source.

trajectory.surface: Adobe Express, then Boards and handover
trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, verify canvas one from the document's rendition and the rest from the returned markup, then build the selects board and write the note.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning and the rendition shows the first artboard only. A 201 on the board is partial success, and the note has to name every roster question and everything that could not be delivered inside the client's own card.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document, a per-canvas audit, a persistent board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the counter screens can carry the overhead dishes at all. Four of the ten are square-on overheads at three by two and the screens are sixteen by nine, so a crop to shape takes away the plate. The crop tool responds not with a failure but with a requires-expand tradeoff carrying pre-filled arguments, which is an invitation to generate marble above and below an overhead frame. Whether the generated surface carries this marble's grain, its warmth and its specular, and whether the seam falls where a diner's eye goes, is a property of each frame and each seed and is not knowable from the frame. It is also not knowable one frame at a time: a generated band that looks convincing alone declares itself the moment the ten tiles are laid in the row the screens actually run them in.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and competence cannot either. The shape is fixed by the client's screens, the frames are fixed by a shoot that is over, and there is no crop that reconciles them; the only other lever is generative and the only way to see its result is to run it and then look at the row. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for wide pictures for the screens and never mentions aspect, expansion or generated surface; the acceptance line that a tile is not delivered by being filled is the client's own standard, not a disclosure. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is a per frame re-decision about what the tile shows: abandoning the whole plate for a tighter detail changes what the counter screen says about that dish, and re-seeding changes the picture, not the pipeline.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Lay all ten counter tiles in a row and judge them as a row. For every frame where the generated band does not sit, either re-run the expansion on a different seed and re-grade the new edge into the house target, or abandon expansion for that frame and re-cut it as a detail, which changes what the screen shows for that dish and therefore what the insert and the delivery tile show too.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A counter screen loop in which four dishes sit on a stretch of marble that is not the cafe's marble, running on a wall above the actual marble, in front of regulars who eat there twice a week.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's card actually becomes as editable structure, and then whether the mapping built against it landed. Two things arrive only by running. First the granularity: whether the five printed lines come across as five addressable frames or as fewer continuous stories, and whether the photograph arrived as a real graphic frame with an integer page item id, which is a property of how a now-retired printer built the 2025 document and is under nobody's control. Second the yield: the mapping readout of the multi-line story silently omits the run holding the allergen line while keeping its line break, so the string still parses as well-formed prose and every offset past it is short by exactly that run's length. The validator returns valid on internally consistent wrong arithmetic, the placeholder step reports success, and two of the five fields never become placeholders.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and diligence alone cannot either. Granularity is not a parameter and has no read-ahead. The yield failure is produced by a lossy readout that presents as complete, so an agent that reads carefully and computes offsets diligently from the readout it was handed produces arithmetic that is internally consistent and wrong, and every downstream tool agrees with it. The defence is a second independent reconstruction of the same text from a different channel, which nothing in any tool description prompts and whose necessity is invisible until the two disagree. (b) Nothing states it. The brief mentions no frames, fields or mappings; it says the cards are right and should be kept. The acceptance line that every card carries all five lines is the client's standing output requirement, not a description of a cause. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. What changes is the mapping STRATEGY and its source of truth, from per-frame replacement against a tool readout to offset arithmetic computed against a reconstructed story with same-frame rows re-ordered. The mapping is re-authored from a different text, not re-fed.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story text by concatenating the exported document's content runs, recompute every field offset against that string, re-order any rows sharing a uid so their positions hold against the original text, rebuild and re-validate the mapping, re-run the template preparation, and re-verify by exporting the interchange file from the prepared template and searching for all five placeholders before any card is merged.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A printed card run that binds the dish name, the description and the price correctly on every card while the allergen line is simply absent, silently, on all ten, with every tool in the chain having reported success. It goes to a printer and onto a table in a room that serves people with allergies.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the per-dish proofs the owners are about to sign off are the dishes they say they are, and whether they are at the resolution they were asked for. The obvious route to a proof image per dish is to merge directly to raster per record. Two things then happen and neither is reported: the resolution requested at merge time is silently ignored, so what comes back is screen scale rather than print scale while looking entirely normal; and the returned links, though labelled row one, row two and row three, come back in a different order from the rows, so naming files by their position attaches the wrong dish to the wrong card. Every file opens, every card looks finished, and nothing in any response is wrong. It surfaces only by opening each returned file and reading the card against the menu.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it. Merging per record to raster is the documented way to get one output per row and the tool's own description says so; the failure is that the description is false in both respects. Care does not help, because both the resolution loss and the reordering present as ordinary success. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for a proof of each card and a separate file per dish. The acceptance lines about identity by inspection and about true print resolution are the client's own standards, not warnings that a route silently violates them. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to abandon the route: merge instead to a native document and render from it with separate files, or loop one record at a time, and re-establish identity by opening each file. The output is produced by a different mechanism, not by re-feeding the same one.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Discard the per-record raster outputs, merge to a native document, render the proofs at true print resolution from that document with separate files (or loop one record per call so identity is guaranteed), open every returned file and read the card against the menu before naming it, and re-issue the whole set of per-dish files under the verified names.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Ten proofs signed off by two owners in which two dishes carry each other's cards, printed at screen resolution and sent to a printer, discovered on the table.
