decision_gates: Which deliverables go to the merge surface and which to authored canvases, given that the client wants the printed card kept and the collateral editable.
Whether a frame has one illuminant or two, and therefore whether a global correction or a confined one is the right instrument.
How far to push the four late-service frames before they stop being worth saving, versus naming them.
On the overheads, whether to show a tighter detail or to generate surface, knowing the generated surface has to sit with the real one in the row.
How to handle the frame carrying the ticket rail, when a crop is the only lawful remedy and the crop costs the wide shape.
The row-count discrepancy and the two prices from the wrong column: what is the agent's call and what is the owners' to confirm, and how to say so.
Whether to trust the mapping tool's readout of the client's text or to reconstruct the story independently from the document.
Whether a success message counts as verification, when nothing instructs the agent to re-export the prepared template and search for its own placeholders.
Which route produces the per-dish proofs and files, and whether identity is established by position in a returned list or by opening the file.
Whether a licensed room frame joins this room or reads as a stock interior, judged at full resolution against the ten.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a counter that has to be read across a room.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns appetising pictures of food. IDENTITY: these are Corner and Cure's actual ten dishes on their actual marble, and a regenerated bowl is a different restaurant's dinner, which is the exact fraud a neighbourhood room cannot survive with regulars who eat there twice a week. SPEC: the client needs one printed card per spring dish at 105 x 148 mm carrying five named fields verbatim from their till, including an allergen line, plus ten separately named single-card files that each contain the dish their filename claims and proofs at true print resolution. EDITABILITY: the collateral is defined by being editable, because prices move mid season and the owners will not pay for a redo. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did this placeholder get created, is this the dish the card says it is, does this generated marble sit with the real marble.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. MERGE SPINE: building a merge template from a bare PDF end to end headlessly is verified (convert to native, export interchange, generate mapping, prepare template, with all six fields confirmed present by unzipping the round trip). One record per page is confirmed for the press branch, per-record named files are confirmed by two routes with order verified, and true 300 DPI at trim is confirmed through the render tool. The three checkpoints rest on documented findings: frame granularity from a PDF is not under your control and interleaved images split a flow into two text frames plus two graphic frames; the mapping readout's text content is LOSSY, dropping a run while keeping its line break so every later offset is short, with the validator returning VALID and the prepare step reporting success while mappings silently fail to land; the merge's own resolution parameter is SILENTLY IGNORED (a Letter page returned 612 x 792); and multi-record raster output URLs COME BACK IN THE WRONG ORDER WITH LABELS THAT LIE (verified reversed on a three row run). Image binding is verified via an at-prefixed column plus an image map with keys matching bare filenames, and the trajectory carries the single-record loop as the identity-guaranteed fallback. IMAGING: straighten, adjustments masked and unmasked, select by prompt with returnBbox, invert, crop to bounds, crop and resize with its tradeoffs and detection confidence, and generative expand (the sole sanctioned generative call, edges only, seedable) are all verified headless. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export, true mm print canvases, real tables with per-cell backgrounds and strokes, and a genuine editable document are verified; the rendition shows PAGE 1 ONLY, so verification is split between the rendition and the returned markup, and the payload goes by uploaded URL because inlined photography passes the 70 KB threshold. FONTS and STOCK and BOARDS as in the verified chains, with short queries, orientation never passed, and the twelve-per-call board cap with 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no upscaling, no object removal, no compositing, no OCR, no bleed or press-preset gate, no variable QR, no fill_text, no animate_design, no batch above 20.

engagement_title: Cedarline and Vale flagship listing: finish a twelve frame shoot so the windows hold their view, rebuild the office window cards from the file that went to press, and hand back the portal set, the feature sheet and the story crops
vertical: Residential real estate, boutique six agent brokerage, architect designed listings (Marin County, California)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Freelancer.com real-estate photo-editing brief quoted in the ledger's grounding_note, whose client hired a freelancer to colour-correct, straighten and lightly retouch a batch of interior listing frames and deliver web-optimised files plus full-resolution ones, to a standard of 'modern, clean, simple, ample lighting, natural' and explicitly 'without making the images look over-processed'. Co-anchor: the Upwork brief from a listing photographer needing a batch editor for bright and airy interiors covering line correction, white balance, WINDOW VIEWS, and a consistent style across the set. Both real clients and the named listing portals are laundered to the fictional Cedarline and Vale and to generic listing portals. The ledger's repositioning note conceded that a true multi-bracket merge is not a connector tool and that the task therefore sat on one surface; the fuller commission that brokerage actually has is the whole listing launch, because the office window card run is a genuine record-per-page job that v3 shows can be rebuilt from a press file, and the feature sheet and portal module are authorable as a native editable document.
client_one_liner: Our photographer shoots single frames so the rooms are right and the windows are white, the house goes live in three weeks, and the office window cards all need reprinting from a file our retired printer sent to press.
client_brief:
Cedarline and Vale, Ridgeway Lane flagship

We are a six agent brokerage in Marin. We have just taken the listing on a nineteen sixties architect house rebuilt by its owners over four years. At two point four million it is the most important thing on our books this year and it goes live in three weeks.

Our photographer shot ten rooms plus the deck and the entry. She is good and she shoots single frames, which means the rooms are right and the windows are not. This house is all glass and the whole reason anybody pays for it is what is outside those windows: the bay through the living room, the oaks off the kitchen. Right now most of them are white. We need the rooms calm and true and the windows actually showing what is there, without the pictures looking cooked. Buyers at this level notice and so do the other agents.

We need the finished rooms in three shapes: the full room files for the listing itself, the four by three the portals crop to, and a taller one of the three best rooms for the story we run on launch day.

Separately, and we always leave this to the last minute, our office window has printed cards in it, one per active listing, and this house joins six that are already there. Our printer runs them. We do not have whatever she built the card in, only the file that went to press, and the six existing cards need new prices anyway because we repriced in January. We want the whole window run done in one go, a proof of each card the vendor can see, and a separate file per listing so we can reprint one without touching the rest.

We also need the printed feature sheet that sits on the hall table at the open house, and the portal module, and both have to be something we can edit ourselves, because the price on this will move and I am not paying for a redo each time.

We have no picture of the house at dusk and no time to get one. If there is something honest we can use on the cover of the feature sheet that is not a picture of the house, use it.

Finally a short note on what you did to each room and what type we are on, for the file.

The buyer is forty to sixty, they read light as build quality, and they will see this next to three other agents' listings. Cool, restrained, true. Not warm and cosy, and nothing that looks retouched.
price_band_and_audience: A 2.4 million dollar architect-designed listing, buyers 40 to 60 with household incomes above 400 thousand who read light and material as proxies for build quality, viewing it alongside three competing agents' listings. The band is load-bearing: at this price the correct treatment is cool, restrained and true, with real neutral whites, deep honest blacks, generous margins on the feature sheet, one photograph doing the work rather than four, and type that does not announce itself. The same brief on a 320 thousand dollar starter home would correctly be warmer, brighter, fuller and more welcoming, with more rooms per page and a friendlier type voice, and shipping that here reads as a volume agency and costs the listing its credibility. Pushed the other way into black grounds, gold rules and heavy serifs it becomes developer marketing, which this vendor and this buyer both distrust. Anything that reads as retouched fails at this band regardless of how well it is executed. A real posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,200 dollars fixed.

assets_supplied.name: ridgeway_rooms/ (12 frames, approx 6000 x 4000)
assets_supplied.kind: Single-frame interior and exterior captures shot in one visit by the brokerage's photographer: ten rooms plus the deck and the entry.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Ten rooms, the deck and the entry, all shot in one visit. She shoots single frames, so the rooms are right and the windows are white."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three frames were shot into the glass, and they are not the same problem. In two of them the sky and the water still carry data and a highlight recovery brings the view back. In the third the glazing is clipped to paper white with nothing behind it at all, so a recovery returns an image that is identical to the one it was given: the call succeeds, the file comes back, and the readout is that nothing has moved. All three look the same as thumbnails. Separately the living room's window is divided by fine glazing bars with a sheer curtain drawn across half of it, and a selection there comes back fully binary with no intermediate values at all, so a masked window pull leaves a stepped seam along the bars and the sheer which is invisible at preview scale and reads as a halo at full resolution. Two frames also sit a degree or so off level, and straightening them eats exactly the edge the portal's four by three crop wants.

assets_supplied.name: windowcard_2025_print.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's flat press PDF for the office window cards, A5 portrait, fonts embedded, produced from a real page layout so it converts cleanly. Carries the address, a description line, the beds and baths line, the price and the agent line, plus a placed room photograph.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The card our printer runs. We only have what went to press and she has retired."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: What the conversion exposes as editable structure is a property of how a retired printer built the 2025 document and is announced nowhere. The five printed lines do not arrive as five addressable frames, and which of them share a story with which is not predictable from looking at the printed card, so some fields must be driven by ordered offset arithmetic inside one flow while others sit alone. The photograph's frame also carries its own bounds and its own placed link, and the aspect it actually holds has to be read out of the converted document rather than assumed from how the card looks in the window.

assets_supplied.name: active_listings.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Export from the office system, one row per active listing, with columns for address, description, beds and baths, price, agent and a photo filename.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The seven cards for the window. The six existing ones have January's prices in them."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three faults, none stated. One of the six existing listings went under contract last week and the office manager has not removed it, so the export carries a row that must not go in the window. The flagship's own row was typed by an agent rather than exported, so its address line uses a different abbreviation convention from the other six and its price is entered with a currency symbol the other six do not carry. And its photo column names a file that does not exist anywhere, because the photograph for that card is the thing this engagement produces.

assets_supplied.name: photographer_notes.txt
assets_supplied.kind: The photographer's shot list with the order the rooms were shot in and the time of day.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Her notes from the visit."

assets_supplied.name: office_style_note.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Half a page from the principal on how the brokerage presents itself and what she means by cooked.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "How we want to look next to the other three agents."

acceptance_bar: The twelve frames read as ONE house shot in one visit: one white point on the plaster, one black point, one crop logic, one degree of window recovery. A room that cannot be brought to the set is named, not shipped at eighty percent.
Every window that has anything behind it shows what is behind it, and any window that does not is named to us in writing before the listing goes live rather than after.
No window pull leaves a visible seam or halo along the glazing or the curtain when the delivered file is viewed at full resolution rather than at preview scale.
Nothing in the delivered set reads as retouched. A room that has been pushed until it stops looking like the room fails even if it looks impressive.
No delivered file exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions and no crop's tradeoff report carries an upscale entry.
The portal crops and the story crops are derived after straightening, and no crop loses a wall or a window edge that the full room file keeps.
Exactly one printed window card per active listing, no extra card and no missing card. If the number shipped is not the number we asked for, the note says which row was left out and why.
Every card carries all five lines the 2025 card carried, and every card's photograph is the listing named on the card.
Each per-listing file contains the listing its filename claims, established by opening it rather than by the order the files came back in.
The proofs are rendered at true print resolution at card trim rather than at screen scale.

The feature sheet and the portal module come back as a native editable document we can change the price in, with every photograph actually visible, the specification block as a real table, and every text element carrying its licensed face at that family's own weight.
Anything on the feature sheet cover that is not a picture of this house is honest about being that, and it sits with the rooms rather than against them.
A written note: what was applied to each room and why that room differs, the type system by role, every listing row questioned and its resolution, and every resize any tool reported.

It levels the off-level frames before any crop is derived, fixes one house target and brings twelve differently lit rooms to it one call at a time, triages the three window frames between those with data behind the glass and the one without, runs the confined window work where a global move would wreck the room, and derives the full room files, the portal crops and the story crops at native scale while reading the tradeoff record on every call. Selections here come back fully binary with no intermediate values, which is the constraint the window work has to be designed around rather than discovered by shipping.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle the split: window cards to the merge surface, feature sheet and portal module to authored canvases, photography to imaging.
trajectory.judgement: The card is record per page against a layout the office wants kept; the feature sheet is free-form and must stay editable, which the merge surface structurally cannot give.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier.

trajectory.action: Upload the twelve frames, the press PDF, the office export and the two notes, holding each returned presigned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A manifest keyed by room and by role, because the same frame will exist in four states before the end.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Preview all twelve frames and triage: which are level, which face glass, what is behind each window, which boundaries a selection would have to follow, and how much edge each frame has to spare.
trajectory.judgement: The three window frames look alike as thumbnails and are not alike. Reading what is behind the glass, and how the glazing and the curtain divide it, is what decides which instrument each room needs.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note: tilt, glass, apparent window content, boundary type and edge margin.

trajectory.action: Straighten the off-level frames before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats the edge the portal's four by three crop wants, so it cannot follow the crop.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix one house target and bring each of the twelve toward it with its own call, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: Twelve rooms lit by different windows at different hours have to arrive at one white point and one black point, which means twelve different routes to one destination rather than one batched move.
trajectory.produces: Twelve graded masters at source scale with a per room parameter log.

trajectory.action: Work the windows: recover the highlights on the glass in the frames that face it, and confine the correction where a global move would take the room with it.
trajectory.judgement: How far a recovery can go before the room stops looking like the room is the whole judgement at this band, and the client has ruled out anything that looks cooked. What a recovery actually returns has to be looked at rather than assumed from the call succeeding.
trajectory.produces: Window-corrected frames and a record of how far each was taken.

trajectory.action: Derive the full room files, the portal four by three crops and the tall story crops of the three lead rooms, reading confidence and tradeoffs on every crop.
trajectory.judgement: One crop logic across twelve rooms, not twelve good crops. The tradeoffs array is the only signal that a crop clipped or that an output was interpolated toward the two times cap.
trajectory.produces: Three families of crop with their tradeoff records.

trajectory.action: Lay the twelve finished rooms together as a listing gallery runs them and judge them as one house.
trajectory.judgement: Judging the set at the only moment the comparison exists, and deciding whether any room has been taken far enough that it now reads as retouched next to its neighbours.
trajectory.produces: A gallery judged as a gallery, with any room that will not join it named.

trajectory.surface: Data preparation and Creative Cloud storage
trajectory.action: Reconcile the office export against the principal's brief, normalise it into a merge-shaped data file with an at-prefixed image column holding bare filenames, upload the room images chosen per listing and build the image map.
trajectory.judgement: Real reconciliation: one row must not go in the window, one row was typed rather than exported and does not match the others' conventions, and one photo reference points at a file that does not exist because this engagement produces it. What is the agent's call and what is the office's to confirm is a decision, and the client asked to be told.
trajectory.produces: The merge data file, the uploaded card images, the image map and a list of listing questions.

trajectory.action: Convert the press PDF, export the interchange file, unzip it and read the real frame inventory and bounds, then reconstruct each frame's true story text from its concatenated content runs.
trajectory.judgement: The mapping strategy is a property of the retired printer's document, and the arithmetic must be computed from the document rather than from any convenience readout. The photograph's frame aspect has to be read out rather than assumed from the printed card.
trajectory.produces: The converted document, its interchange export, a frame inventory with real ids and bounds, and a reconstructed story string.

trajectory.action: Author the mapping covering all five copy fields plus the image frame, validate it, prepare the template, then export the interchange file from the RESULT and search for every placeholder the mapping claimed to create.
trajectory.judgement: Not accepting a success message as evidence, and ordering any rows that share a uid so their positions hold against the original text.
trajectory.produces: A prepared template whose placeholder inventory has been independently confirmed.

trajectory.action: Merge to a native document with the per-row images bound, then render the window cards and the vendor proofs at true print resolution from that document, and produce the per-listing single files, naming each by opening it.
trajectory.judgement: Merging to the native document first keeps both the press branch and the per-record branch open, and identity by position in a returned list is the fast wrong answer that puts the wrong house in the window.
trajectory.produces: The window card run, print-resolution proofs, and per-listing files verified by inspection.

trajectory.action: Read every rendered card against the reconciled roster at trim rather than at proof scale, line by line and photograph by photograph.
trajectory.judgement: A missing line and a wrongly bound photograph both look like success at the API boundary and both look fine on a screen-scale proxy.
trajectory.produces: A card-by-card reconciliation against the roster.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the honest cover frame that is not a picture of this house, filter to photography, exclude generative-tech results, license and download at full resolution.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose light and whose blacks can live beside the graded twelve, not the moodiest thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP-clean, camera-scale cover frame.

trajectory.action: Bring the licensed frame toward the house target and lay it against the twelve graded rooms as one set.
trajectory.judgement: Judging the set as a set at the only moment the comparison is available, and deciding whether the frame joins, gets pushed further, or gets abandoned for a different search.
trajectory.produces: The cover frame, in or out, with the reasoning recorded.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's and has to answer to a 2.4 million dollar listing seen next to three other agents. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one-kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self-contained HTML with the A4 feature sheet at true physical dimensions, the portal module and the story canvas, inline every photograph, set the specification block as a real table, declare family and weight per text element, then upload it and hold the URL.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto-sized right-anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed-size set. The design work is how much air a restrained band takes and which room leads.
trajectory.produces: One export-ready HTML carrying the collateral, retained as the durable source.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, verify canvas one from the document's rendition and the rest from the returned per-canvas markup.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition shows the first artboard only.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document, an inspected first canvas and a markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.action: Build the vendor selects board within the placement cap, re-sending only entries named as failed, then write the note.
trajectory.judgement: A 201 is partial success. The note has to name every window that could not be delivered with a view, before the listing goes live rather than after, under the client's own standard.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which of the three window frames actually has anything behind the glass. Two of them hold sky and water in the highlights and a recovery brings the view back; the third is clipped to paper white with no data at all, and the readout there is that NOTHING MOVES. The call succeeds, a file comes back, and it is the file that went in. All three look identical as thumbnails, because a clipped highlight and a very bright one are the same white on a screen. There is no measurement available anywhere in the connector, no histogram and no eyedropper, so the only way to learn which is which is to apply the recovery and look at what came back against what went in.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no care prevents it. Nothing in the frame, the shot list or the client's account distinguishes a recoverable window from a dead one, and there is no read-ahead: the recovery IS the diagnostic. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says most of the windows are white and asks for the view back, which is the client's goal, not a disclosure that one window has no view left to recover; the acceptance line about naming any window that cannot be delivered is the client's own standing requirement of the same kind they already state about not looking cooked. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is not to re-run anything on that frame, because nothing will change it. It is a judgement and a re-composition: which room leads the feature sheet, which three rooms carry the story crops, which room's photograph goes on that listing's window card, and what gets written to the vendor before the listing goes live.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Confirm the dead frame by comparing the returned file against the input rather than by trusting the call, then re-decide the room order across the feature sheet, the portal module and the story crops so the blown room is not a lead, choose a different photograph for any card that would have used it, and name the room and the reason in writing to the client before launch under their own invitation to be told.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A flagship listing goes live at 2.4 million with a room whose whole selling point is the bay showing a flat white rectangle, presented as finished work to a buyer who reads light as build quality and to three competing agents.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the confined window work leaves a seam on the boundary this particular house has. Selections come back fully binary, with zero intermediate values, so wherever a masked correction meets a soft or finely divided edge the transition is a hard step rather than a blend. In this house the living room's glass is divided by fine glazing bars with a sheer curtain drawn across half of it. Whether the step reads is a property of that boundary, that curtain and the size of the correction applied, and it is invisible at the scale an agent inspects at: the preview looks clean and the seam appears at full resolution as a bright outline along the bars and a hard line where the sheer begins.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it and there is no feather, no blend and no softening control anywhere in the family, so the agent cannot simply do it right first time; nor can it avoid masks, because a global move that pulls the glass takes the room with it. Whether THIS boundary steps visibly can only be seen after the correction, at full resolution. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the windows must show the view and nothing must look retouched, which is the client's standard; no asset note, no earlier step and no deliverable mentions glazing bars, curtains or edges. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is a different instrument: re-word the selection so it lands on a boundary that has contrast (the view beyond the glass rather than the window opening), or abandon confinement on that frame for a smaller global move that costs some recovery, which is a trade the agent has to make and then carry into how that room is cropped and where it sits in the sheet.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Inspect the delivered masters at full resolution rather than at preview scale, and on any frame showing a step re-do the window work through a differently bounded selection or through a reduced global correction, re-judge the room against the other eleven, and re-derive that room's portal and story crops from the corrected master.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The single most important room in the listing ships with a bright halo tracing every glazing bar and a hard line across the curtain, which is the exact tell of retouching at a band where the client has explicitly said nothing may look retouched, visible the moment a buyer opens the full-size file.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the licensed cover frame can live beside the graded twelve. The search returns a 240 pixel thumbnail carrying no usable information about tone, and the frame that reads deep and quiet at that size can, at full resolution, turn out to have lifted milky shadows that were simply not visible in the proxy. Bringing those blacks to the listing set's honest deep neutral either crushes the texture that made the frame worth choosing or leaves it sitting grey on the feature sheet cover above twelve rooms that are not grey. Which of those it is only exists after the frame has actually been licensed, downloaded at full resolution and laid against the finished set.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it, because the comparison needs both the licensed frame and the finished twelve to exist; and care cannot settle it, because a 240 pixel proxy is not evidence about tone, and two frames that look equally deep at that size can be a full grade apart. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says only that if there is something honest that is not a picture of the house, use it. No asset, no earlier step and no acceptance line makes any claim about how a candidate will behave. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The likely response is to abandon this frame and search again on the tone the set actually has rather than on the subject, which is a new licensing decision, a new grade and a new judgement.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Push the licensed frame toward the house target and judge it adjacent to the twelve; if it will not join, return to the search framed by the light and the blacks the set has rather than by subject matter, license a replacement, re-grade, re-lay the set and only then commit it to the feature sheet cover and to the selects board.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A feature sheet on the hall table at the open house whose cover is visibly a bought photograph sitting on top of a house's own pictures, which is the precise tell that undermines a provenance claim in front of a buyer comparing three agents.

decision_gates: Which deliverables go to the merge surface and which to authored canvases, given a card the office wants kept and a feature sheet whose price will move.
Which of the three window frames has anything behind the glass, when all three look alike as thumbnails and no measurement exists anywhere.
How far a recovery can be taken before the room stops looking like the room, at a band where anything that looks retouched fails.
Whether to confine the window work with a mask on a finely divided boundary, or to accept a smaller global move that costs recovery, on a frame where a binary selection cannot blend.
Crop policy for the set as a whole versus per room, and how much edge the two straightened frames can afford to give the portal shape.

The roster: a listing under contract that must not go in the window, a hand-typed row that does not match the others' conventions, and a photo reference that points at a file this engagement produces. What is the agent's call and what is the office's.
Whether to trust the mapping tool's readout of the printer's text or to reconstruct the story independently from the document.
Whether a success message counts as verification of the prepared template's placeholders.
Whether per-listing identity is established by position in a returned list or by opening the file.
Whether a licensed cover frame joins the set at full resolution or reads as bought, and whether to push it or search again on tone rather than subject.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a listing seen next to three other agents.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of a nice house. IDENTITY: these are the actual rooms of the actual property at the actual address, and a regenerated interior is a misrepresentation that a brokerage cannot put in front of a buyer or a vendor. What is outside those windows is the specific bay and the specific oaks, and it must be RECOVERED from the capture, not invented. SPEC: the office needs one A5 card per active listing binding five named fields verbatim, per-listing single files each containing the listing they claim, and proofs at true print resolution. EDITABILITY: the feature sheet is defined by being editable because the price will move. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: does this window have anything behind it, does this mask leave a seam at full resolution, is this the listing the card says it is.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: straighten, apply_adjustments global and masked, auto_tone, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds and crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor are all verified headless. The two imaging checkpoints rest on documented facts rather than invention: there is NO measurement anywhere in the family (no eyedropper, no histogram, no ruler, and metadata.bbox is a mask extent not a tonal reading), so a clipped highlight can only be diagnosed by applying a recovery and comparing; and SELECTION MASKS COME BACK FULLY BINARY, verified as 893,650 pure black plus 154,926 pure white with ZERO intermediate values, with the doc stating explicitly that any edge softness must come from background removal's alpha rather than from a selection, which is unavailable on a window interior. crop_and_resize is documented as interpolating up to a hard 2x cap and reporting it only in the tradeoffs array, which is what makes the no-enlargement bar checkable rather than asserted. MERGE SPINE: building a merge template from a bare press PDF end to end headlessly is verified, one record per page is confirmed for the PDF branch, per-record files are confirmed in correct order by two routes, true 300 DPI at trim is confirmed through the render tool, the merge's own resolution parameter is documented as silently ignored (hence rendering from the merged document), frame granularity from a PDF is documented as not under your control, and the mapping readout's text content is documented as lossy in a way the validator blesses. Image binding through an at-prefixed column plus an image map is verified, with the single-record loop as the identity-guaranteed fallback. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export, true mm print canvases at exactly 96 dpi, real tables, and a genuine editable document are verified; the rendition shows PAGE 1 ONLY so verification splits between the rendition and the returned markup; payload routed by uploaded URL. FONTS, STOCK and BOARDS follow the verified chains, with short queries, orientation never passed, and the twelve-per-call board cap with 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no upscaling, no object or distractor removal, no perspective correction, no HDR merge, no compositing, no OCR, no bleed or press-preset gate, no variable QR, no fill_text, no batch above 20.

engagement_title: Verranza Coastal Retreats direct booking launch: make three separate villas read as one collection, recover the collection mark off the cove gate plate, and rebuild the travel agent rate cards from the file that went to press
vertical: Hospitality and travel, a three villa luxury vacation rental collection going direct, plus a travel agent trade channel (Ligurian coast, Italy)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork rental-portfolio finishing brief quoted in the ledger's grounding_note, from a boutique vacation-rental manager wanting 'a consistent, premium visual identity across the whole portfolio' with a 'natural, realistic look' and an explicit do-not-want list of no fake HDR, no over-saturation and no unrealistically blue pools. The real manager, place and workflow vendor are laundered to the fictional Verranza Coastal Retreats above the fictional cove of Punta Verranza, relocated to the Ligurian coast to sit inside the required Western and European frame. The ledger's own note records that the killed original ran three independent tonal chains and openly conceded that the perspective and cloning work it implied was out of scope, which is exactly why it sat on one surface. The fuller commission that manager actually has is the direct-booking launch: the collection has no logo file, its trade channel runs on printed rate cards from a press file nobody can rebuild, and every rate on them changes for the new season.
client_one_liner: Three houses shot on three different days look like three different holidays, our monogram has only ever existed as an iron plate on the gate, and from January we book direct and sell to agents.
client_brief:
Verranza Coastal Retreats, direct booking launch

We let three houses above the cove at Punta Verranza on the Ligurian coast: Casa Verranza, Casa Oliveto and Casa Scogliera. They sleep six, eight and ten, they go for five hundred and twenty to seven hundred and eighty euros a night in season, and until now we have let them through a marketplace that takes a great deal of money from us. From January we book direct and we sell to a handful of travel agents. Everything a guest or an agent sees is ours to make now, and we have nothing that holds together.

The photography is the heart of it. We have twelve pictures, four of each house, taken on three different days last summer by the same person. Each house looks good on its own. Put the three houses on one page and they are plainly three different holidays: one is green, one is orange, and the three pools are three different blues. A guest choosing between our own houses should not be able to tell they were shot on different days. That is the whole job.

We do not want them cooked. Anders and I have both been on the wrong end of a booking where the pictures were not the house. Nothing lurid, nothing that makes a pool a colour a pool is not, nothing that turns a stone wall into a computer's idea of a stone wall.

We need them as the booking gallery for each house, as a wide header for each house's page, and as a tall one of each house's best room for the stories we run in January.

The mark is the other thing. Verranza's monogram was cut into an iron plate by the smith in the village when my grandfather bought the first house, and it has hung on the gate at the top of the track ever since. There has never been a file. We have a photograph of the gate. We need it back as artwork, on the site, on the cards, at any size, and reversed out of the deep blue we use.

The agents work from printed cards. Our printer ran them last year, one card per house per season, and we have only the file that went to press. All the rates change for twenty twenty seven and the minimum stays change with them. We want the whole run again, a proof of each card, and a file per card.

The collection page and the booking header should be ours to edit, because the rates move.

And a note on what you did to each house, and anything we should know about using the mark.
price_band_and_audience: Three villas at 520 to 780 euros a night in season, guests 35 to 60, American and Northern European families and groups of friends booking a whole house for a week, plus a small trade channel of travel agents working from printed rate cards. The band is load-bearing and it is a restraint band, not a luxury one: at this price the collection must read as a real place honestly photographed, with true stone, true water and true afternoon light, generous white space, one photograph carrying a page, and a mark used quietly. A 110 euro budget rental would correctly be shot bright, literal and full, showing every room and every amenity, and the collection treatment on it would misrepresent the property and invite refund disputes. Pushed the other way into saturated water, orange skin, crushed blacks and a fake evening glow, it becomes the marketplace look the owners are leaving and the one they have explicitly ruled out, and it is the exact thing that produces a guest arriving to a house that is not the pictures. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,300 to 2,800 dollars fixed.

assets_supplied.name: villa_frames/ (12 frames, approx 6000 x 4000)
assets_supplied.kind: Four frames per villa, shot on three different days last summer by the same photographer: terrace, pool, principal bedroom and living room for each house.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Four of each house, same photographer, three different days. One house looks green and one looks orange, and the three pools are three different blues."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The pools are three different blues because they are three different plasters, not three different gradings. The palest, at Casa Scogliera, is a shallow turquoise that will not travel to the deep Mediterranean blue the other two share: pushed toward it, hue and saturation move convincingly for a while and then the water goes grey and dead, and where that threshold sits is a property of this plaster under this light and is not knowable until it is pushed. Nothing reports it and the intermediate results all look plausible. Separately Casa Oliveto's four frames were shot with the terrace shade sail up, which throws a green bounce onto every lime-washed wall in that house; it reads as cool and calm alone and reads as sick next to the other two. And two of the twelve are portrait terrace frames while the booking header is wide, so neither can reach the header shape by cropping.

assets_supplied.name: gate_plate.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of the wrought iron monogram plate bolted to the lime-washed gate pillar at the top of the track, 4032 x 3024, shot square on in mid afternoon raking light.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The plate the smith cut for my grandfather. It is the only place the monogram has ever existed."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The iron and the sunlit lime wash run close in value across the lower half of the plate, and the monogram is a compound lockup, two letters inside an oval rule with a small anchor beneath, so a single selection returns the oval and its type and silently drops the anchor and the inner rule while looking entirely plausible; background removal on the oval returns a solid opaque disc because an enclosed interior cannot be punched. Beyond all that, how much of the oval's hairline and how much of the letters' fine serifs survive this iron, through this trace, at the size the printed card actually reproduces it and reversed out of the collection's deep blue, is a property of this photograph that nothing reports and no earlier step can predict.

assets_supplied.name: agentcard_2025_print.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's flat press PDF for the travel agent rate cards, 148 x 105 mm landscape, fonts embedded, produced from a real page layout so it converts cleanly. Carries the house name, the season, the nightly rate, the minimum stay and the contact line, plus a placed villa photograph and a small placed mark.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What our printer sent to press last year. We do not have the working file."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two things nobody can tell you. The mark's graphic frame is a fraction of the size the printed card suggests, because the printer scaled the plate down inside a larger frame, so the reproduction size the recovered mark has to survive is geometry inherited from a printer nobody can ask rather than a size anyone chose, and it is knowable only by reading the converted document. And the mapping readout of the rate story silently omits the run holding the minimum stay while KEEPING its line break, so the string still reads as well-formed and every character offset after it is short by exactly that run's length; the validator returns valid on the resulting arithmetic and the placeholder step reports success, while two of the fields never become placeholders.

assets_supplied.name: rates_2027.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Export from the owners' booking sheet, one row per house per season, with columns for house, season, nightly rate, minimum stay, sleeps and a photo filename.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The new rates. Nine cards, three houses by three seasons."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three faults, none stated. The export carries ten rows because a fourth house the family sold in 2026 is still on the sheet. The sleeps figure for one house disagrees with the owner's own note. And the season labels in the export do not match the labels the owners use in their note, so the cards would go to agents naming seasons the agents have never been quoted.

assets_supplied.name: owner_note.txt
assets_supplied.kind: A page from the owner: the three houses and what each is for, the do-not-want list in her own words, and how she talks about the coast.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The three houses, and what we do not want done to them."

acceptance_bar: The twelve frames read as ONE collection: a guest comparing the three houses should not be able to tell they were shot on different days. One white point on the lime wash, one black point, one warmth in the stone, one crop logic.

Nothing is cooked. No water is a colour that water is not, no stone is pushed past stone, and any frame taken far enough to stop looking like the house fails even if it looks impressive. Where a house could not be brought fully to the collection without crossing that line, the note says so and says what was done instead.

No delivered file exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions and no crop's tradeoff report carries an upscale entry. Where a shape could not be reached by cropping, the note says what was done to that frame.
Each house has its own booking gallery, its own wide header and one tall crop of its best room, and every canvas carries a picture that can actually hold at that size.

The mark is placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath, and it still reads as our monogram at the size the printed card reproduces it and reversed out of the deep blue.
Exactly one printed card per house per season, no extra card and no missing card. If the number shipped is not the number we asked for, the note says which row was left out and why.
Every card carries all the lines the 2025 card carried, including the minimum stay, and every rate and every minimum stay on every card is the 2027 figure rather than last year's.
Every card carries its own house's photograph and the seasons are named the way we name them to agents.
Each per-card file contains the card its filename claims, established by opening it rather than by the order the files came back in.
The proofs are rendered at true print resolution at card trim rather than at screen scale.

The collection page and the booking header come back as a native editable document we can change the rates in, with every photograph actually visible, the mark as live vector shapes rather than a flattened picture, and every text element carrying its licensed face at that family's own weight.

A written note: what was applied to each house and why each house needed a different correction to arrive at the same place, the type system by role, every rate row questioned and its resolution, every resize any tool reported, and anything we should know about using the mark.

And recovers the monogram at ink level off a photographed iron plate, with the polarity decision and the vector hygiene the tracing tool does not perform.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml (twice), generate_indd_mapping_prompt (as generator and as validator), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout (application/x-indesign and application/pdf, additionalImageFiles, recordRange), document_render_layout (resolution 300, createSeparateFiles, pageRange in N-N form)

The true story text must be reconstructed from the exported document rather than trusted from a convenience readout.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The collection page, the three booking headers and the story canvas as one native editable document at mixed canvas sizes, so the owners can change rates themselves. Every photograph inlined as image data, the monogram inlined as SVG so it stays vector including reversed on the deep blue panel, family and weight declared per text element, each root declaring its own canvas, payload routed by uploaded URL.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Fonts
adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system for the collection page, the headers and the story canvas, and the only place the agent's typographic authorship exists, since no font from this surface reaches the printed agent card. The pairing is the agent's own art direction against a restraint band, the numeric weight per family is non-standard, one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug.

adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one material and texture frame the collection page needs and the houses cannot supply, IP-clean and at camera scale with generative-tech candidates excluded, chosen for a light that can join the collection rather than for a subject. The Boards half persists the shared set the owner and the two property managers brief from, placed within the twelve-per-call cap with a partial success read as partial and vector understood to be unacceptable there.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle the split: agent cards to the merge surface, collection page and headers to authored canvases, photography and mark recovery to imaging.
trajectory.judgement: The cards are record per page against a layout the owners want kept; the collection page must stay editable because the rates move, which the merge surface structurally cannot give.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier.

trajectory.action: Upload the twelve frames, the gate plate photograph, the press PDF, the booking sheet and the owner's note, holding each presigned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A manifest keyed by house and by role, because each frame will exist in several states before the end.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Preview all twelve frames and triage by house: what light each house was shot under, what each house's walls are doing, what colour each pool actually is, which frames are portrait, and which subject boundaries a selection would have to follow.
trajectory.judgement: The client describes green and orange, which is a symptom. The useful question is what is causing each, because a bounce off a shade sail and an afternoon sun are different problems with different remedies, and three pools that differ by plaster are not a grading problem at all.
trajectory.produces: A per house triage note: illuminant, wall cast, water colour, native aspect and boundary type.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels, and the two portrait frames have the least to spare.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed.

trajectory.action: Fix one collection target and bring each of the twelve toward it with its own call, recording parameters per frame and per house.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a collection, and each house needs a different route to reach it. The client has ruled out cooking, so how far each correction goes is the judgement, not how good it can be made to look.
trajectory.produces: Twelve graded masters at source scale with a per house parameter log.

trajectory.action: Confined work where a global move is wrong: the green bounce on Casa Oliveto's lime wash, and the water in each of the three pools, selected by the material's own visual properties rather than by the object it sits in.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the gate: naming the pool takes the pool surround, naming the water's own colour and surface takes the water. How far the water can be moved before it stops being water is the whole do-not-want list in one decision.
trajectory.produces: Confined corrections with the parameters applied recorded per frame.

trajectory.action: Lay the twelve together as a collection page lays them, three houses side by side, and judge them as one collection.
trajectory.judgement: Judging the collection at the only moment the comparison exists, and deciding what one collection is going to mean if one house's water cannot join the other two.
trajectory.produces: A collection contact set judged as a set, with the reasoning recorded.

trajectory.action: Derive the booking gallery crops and the tall story crops at native scale, and take the two portrait terrace frames to the wide header shape, reading confidence and tradeoffs on every call.
trajectory.judgement: A portrait frame cannot reach a wide header by cropping, so the choice is between generating band on the short axis and promoting a different frame to lead that house, and whichever is chosen has to sit with the real coast beside it.
trajectory.produces: Gallery crops, story crops, two wide headers and a record of which route each frame took.

trajectory.action: Recover the monogram off the gate plate: an ink-level selection naming the iron's own visual properties, correct polarity, a bounds crop from the selection's own bbox, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full canvas ground path removed, plus a reversed variant for the deep blue.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions the tools do not make: how to word the selection so it takes the iron and not the lime wash, which polarity to trace, and whether the compound lockup came back whole or came back plausible and incomplete. Background removal is the wrong instrument on an enclosed oval.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent monogram plus a reversed variant.

trajectory.surface: Data preparation and Creative Cloud storage
trajectory.action: Reconcile the booking sheet against the owner's note, normalise it into a merge-shaped data file with an at-prefixed image column holding bare filenames and the seasons named the way the owners name them to agents, upload the chosen card images and build the image map.
trajectory.judgement: Real reconciliation: a sold house is still on the sheet, one sleeps figure disagrees with the owner, and the season labels do not match the ones agents are quoted. What is the agent's call and what is the owners' to confirm is a decision, and it has to be said rather than done silently.
trajectory.produces: The merge data file, the uploaded card images, the image map and a list of rate questions.

trajectory.action: Convert the press PDF, export the interchange file, unzip it and read the real frame inventory, the integer page item ids and the bounds of both graphic frames, then reconstruct each frame's true story text from its concatenated content runs.
trajectory.judgement: The mapping strategy and the mark's true reproduction size are both properties of the retired printer's document rather than of the plan, and the offsets must be computed from the document rather than from any convenience readout.
trajectory.produces: The converted document, its interchange export, a frame inventory with real bounds including the mark's frame, and a reconstructed story string.

trajectory.action: Author the mapping covering every copy field plus both graphic frames, validate it, prepare the template, then export the interchange file from the RESULT and search for every placeholder the mapping claimed to create.
trajectory.judgement: Not accepting a success message as evidence, and ordering any rows sharing a uid so their positions hold against the original text. Choosing which graphic frame is the photograph and which is the mark is settled by bounds and link, not by assumption.
trajectory.produces: A prepared template whose placeholder inventory has been independently confirmed.

trajectory.action: Merge to a native document with the per-row images bound and the mark placed, then render the agent cards and the owners' proofs at true print resolution from that document, and produce the per-card files, naming each by opening it.
trajectory.judgement: Merging to the native document first keeps both branches open, and identity by position in a returned list is the fast wrong answer that quotes an agent the wrong rate.
trajectory.produces: The agent card run, print-resolution proofs, and per-card files verified by inspection.

trajectory.action: Read every rendered card against the reconciled rates at trim rather than at proof scale, line by line, rate by rate and photograph by photograph, and look at the mark where it actually sits on the card.
trajectory.judgement: Reading the output rather than the log. A missing line, a stale rate and a mark that has stopped reading all look like success at the API boundary and all look fine on a screen-scale proxy.
trajectory.produces: A card-by-card reconciliation and a first honest look at the mark at its real reproduction size.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the one material and texture frame the collection page needs, filter to photography, exclude generative-tech results, license and download at full resolution, then grade it toward the collection target and lay it against the twelve.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose light can join this coast, not the most beautiful thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed camera-scale frame, in or out, with the reasoning recorded.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's and has to land on restraint at 520 to 780 euros, not on luxury signalling. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one-kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self-contained HTML with the collection page, the three wide booking headers and the story canvas, inline every photograph as image data, place the monogram as inline SVG inside an explicitly sized top-left anchored wrapper including reversed on the deep blue panel, declare family and weight per text element, then upload and hold the URL.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto-sized right-anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed-size set. The design work is how quietly the mark is used and how much air a restraint band takes.
trajectory.produces: One export-ready HTML carrying the collection set, retained as the durable source.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, verify canvas one from the document's rendition and the rest from the returned per-canvas markup, asserting that every image resolved to real image data and that the monogram arrived as vector paths.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition shows the first artboard only.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document, an inspected first canvas and a per-canvas markup audit.

trajectory.action: Build the shared board within the placement cap, re-sending only entries named as failed, then write the note.
trajectory.judgement: A 201 is partial success and the vector monogram is not boardable, so it belongs in the note. The note has to name every rate row questioned and anything about the mark the owners need to know.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How far the pale pool can actually travel. The three pools are three different plasters, and the collection target the agent fixed off the two deep ones is a colour the third may or may not reach. A confined hue, saturation and lightness move on the water shifts it convincingly for a while, and then it stops being water: the blue goes flat and grey, the surface reads as a painted panel, and the frame crosses precisely the line the owners named when they said nothing that makes a pool a colour a pool is not. Where that threshold sits for this plaster under this light is not published, not reported and not predictable from the frame, and the intermediate results are all plausible. The tool's own range is documented as holding only at moderate moves, so the question is not whether the tool will do it but what the water looks like when it has.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no care prevents it, because the target must be fixed before the frames can be corrected toward it and the third pool's ceiling only exists once the move is attempted; and there is no measurement anywhere in the connector to establish either the target or the distance in advance. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the three pools are three different blues, which is the client's description of a symptom, and the do-not-want list is the client's standing quality requirement, not a disclosure that one pool cannot be reconciled. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to re-decide what one collection means, which changes the target itself and therefore every frame already corrected toward it: either the collection blue is re-set to a blue all three plasters can honestly reach, or the third house keeps its own honest water and the collection consistency is carried by the stone, the sky and the linen instead, which changes what leads each house's page.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-set the collection target to a blue all three pools can reach honestly and re-correct the frames already taken to the old target, or accept the third house's own water and re-carry the collection's consistency on stone, sky and light, re-judging all twelve as a set afterwards and recording in the note why each house needed a different correction to arrive at the same place.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: One house's pool shipped as a flat grey-blue panel that is not the water in that pool, on a direct booking site whose owners have said in writing that a guest arriving to a house that is not the pictures is the thing they are leaving the marketplace to avoid.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered monogram survives being made and being placed. Three facts exist only empirically and only here. How much of the oval's hairline rule and how much of the letters' fine serifs this iron actually yields through this trace, and what path and fill count comes back. What size the card actually reproduces the mark at, which is geometry inherited from a printer nobody can ask and is readable only out of the converted document, not from how the printed card looks. And whether the mark still reads as the monogram at that size and reversed out of the collection's deep blue, which is a question about this trace at this size on this ground that no earlier step can answer and no tool reports. The compound lockup makes it worse: a selection that returned the oval and the type while silently dropping the anchor and the inner rule looks entirely plausible right up until it is placed small.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it. Fidelity is a function of the iron, the raking light, the lime wash and the selection that produced it; the agent chooses the prompt and the polarity but not how much hairline survives, and there is no way to find out short of tracing it and placing the result at the real size on the real ground. The tracing tool takes NO options at all, so there is no parameter to tune and the only lever is the raster preparation, which cannot be chosen before the failure is seen. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for the monogram back as artwork at any size and reversed out of the deep blue, which is the client's requirement, and never mentions traces, path counts or minimum sizes. Crucially it does not ask how small the mark can safely go, which would have made the finding a stated deliverable. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to produce a DIFFERENT asset: re-select with a prompt aimed at a different element of the lockup, prepare the raster differently before tracing, trace the colour-accurate plate instead of the two-colour mask, or re-cast the card and the header around the letters alone with the oval demoted, and then re-author around whichever that is.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-run the recovery with a differently prepared raster and an element-specific selection so the oval rule and the anchor hold, re-place the result at the size the card's own frame actually reproduces it and reversed on the deep blue, and if it still will not hold, re-cast the lockup for small use and re-author both the card mapping and the collection page around that decision before anything is re-rendered.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Nine printed cards go to travel agents carrying a grey smear where the family's monogram should be, its oval gone and its anchor missing, and the same broken mark reversed on the collection page, with every tool in the chain having reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the mapping built against the printer's card actually landed. The mapping readout of the rate story silently omits the run holding the minimum stay while keeping its line break, so the string still reads as well-formed prose and every character offset after it is short by exactly that run's length. The validator returns valid on internally consistent wrong arithmetic, the placeholder step reports success, and two of the fields never become placeholders. The frame granularity that produced the shared story in the first place is itself a property of how the retired printer built the document and is announced nowhere.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and diligence alone cannot either. The failure is produced by a lossy readout that presents as complete, so an agent that reads carefully and computes offsets diligently from what it was handed produces arithmetic that is internally consistent and wrong, and every downstream tool agrees with it. The defence is a second independent reconstruction of the same text from a different channel, which nothing in any tool description prompts and whose necessity is invisible until the two disagree. (b) Nothing states it. The brief mentions no frames, fields or mappings, only that all the rates and the minimum stays change. The acceptance line requiring the minimum stay on every card is the client's own commercial requirement, not a description of a cause. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The mapping strategy and its source of truth change, from replacement against a tool readout to offset arithmetic computed against a reconstructed story with same-frame rows re-ordered; the mapping is re-authored from a different text, not re-fed.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story text by concatenating the exported document's content runs, recompute every offset against that string, re-order any rows sharing a uid, rebuild and re-validate the mapping, re-run the template preparation and verify by exporting the interchange file from the prepared template and searching for every placeholder before any card is merged.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Nine rate cards go out to travel agents carrying last year's minimum stay and one stale rate as static printed text, which is a commercial commitment the owners will be held to for a season.

deliverables.name: Verranza collection photography, twelve frames plus one licensed material frame
deliverables.spec: Twelve frames across three houses brought to one collection target (one white point on the lime wash, one black point, one warmth in the stone, one crop logic) without crossing the owners' do-not-want line, delivered as a booking gallery per house, a wide header per house and a tall story crop of each house's best room, plus one licensed camera-scale material frame graded into the same world. Every output at or below its source dimensions, with a per house parameter log naming why each house needed a different correction to arrive at the same place.

deliverables.name: Recovered Verranza monogram
