decision_gates: Which deliverables go to the merge surface and which to authored canvases, given cards the owners want kept and rates that move.
What is causing each house's cast, since a bounce off a shade sail and an afternoon sun need different remedies.
What the collection blue is going to be, when one pool's plaster cannot reach the other two's, and therefore what one collection means for this portfolio.
How far a confined move on water can go before it stops being water, at a band where the owners have named that failure in writing.
On the two portrait terrace frames, whether to generate band on the short axis or to promote a different frame to lead that house.

Selection prompt wording on the gate plate: naming the pillar takes the lime wash, naming the iron's own visual properties takes the mark, and background removal on an enclosed oval is the wrong instrument entirely.
Whether the compound lockup came back whole or came back plausible and incomplete, which only shows when it is placed small.
Which mark variant carries the card and which carries the reversed panel, decided against how the trace actually reads at the size the printer's own frame reproduces it.
The roster: a sold house still on the sheet, a sleeps figure that disagrees with the owner, and season labels agents have never been quoted. What is the agent's call and what is the owners'.
Whether to trust the mapping tool's readout of the printer's text or to reconstruct the story independently from the document, and whether a success message counts as verification.
Whether per-card identity is established by position in a returned list or by opening the file.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against restraint rather than luxury signalling.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns beautiful pictures of a Mediterranean villa. IDENTITY: these are three specific houses that guests will arrive at, and the owners have said in writing that pictures which are not the house is the exact failure they are leaving the marketplace to escape; a regenerated terrace is a misrepresentation with a refund attached. The monogram is a specific iron plate cut by a specific smith and must be RECOVERED, not reinvented, or it is a different family's mark. SPEC: the trade channel needs one 148 x 105 mm card per house per season binding rates and minimum stays verbatim, per-card files each containing the card they claim, and proofs at true print resolution. EDITABILITY: the collection page is defined by being editable because rates move. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: how far this plaster will travel before it stops being water, whether this trace holds at the size a retired printer's frame reproduces it, whether this placeholder was ever created.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: straighten, apply_adjustments global and masked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and upscale cap, fill_area, generative_expand (edges only, seedable, the sole sanctioned generative call) and vectorize are all verified headless across 27 live calls. The pool checkpoint rests on a documented finding rather than an assumption: HSL RANGE HOLDS AT MODERATE, with a verified 35 degree masked shift moving terracotta to magenta convincingly while a near-complementary swing to a named target is recorded as out of reach, and there is NO measurement anywhere in the family, so both the target and the distance are eye judgements. The mark checkpoint rests on the verified substrate-versus-ink prompt asymmetry, the verified silent partial selection on compound marks (the type ring returned while the inner rule and the central element were dropped), the verified solid-disc failure of background removal on an enclosed ring, image_vectorize TAKING NO OPTIONS AT ALL so the raster preparation is the only lever, and the missing viewBox plus opaque path zero that the acceptance bar scores. MERGE SPINE: building a merge template from a bare press PDF end to end headlessly is verified, one record per page is confirmed for the PDF branch, per-record files are confirmed in correct order by two routes, true 300 DPI at trim is confirmed through the render tool while the merge's own resolution parameter is documented as silently ignored, PDF-derived templates are confirmed to expose real image frames with integer ids and bounds (which is how the mark's inherited reproduction size becomes readable), frame granularity is documented as not under your control, and the mapping readout's text content is documented as lossy in a way the validator blesses and the prepare step reports as success. Image binding through an at-prefixed column plus an image map is verified, with the single-record loop as the identity-guaranteed fallback. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export, inline SVG becoming native editable vector, and a genuine editable document are verified; the rendition shows PAGE 1 ONLY so verification splits between the rendition and the returned markup; payload routed by uploaded URL because inlined photography passes the 70 KB threshold. FONTS, STOCK and BOARDS follow the verified chains, with short queries, orientation never passed, and the twelve-per-call board cap with 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no upscaling, no object removal, no compositing, no OCR, no bleed or press-preset gate, no variable QR, no fill_text, no animate_design, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no batch above 20.

engagement_title: Continental Cup 2026 collector card programme: eight mixed-floodlight pitch-side portraits brought to one house look, each player cut clean for the card hero, the printer's 2025 card rebuilt into a live merge, and the launch set handed back editable
vertical: Sports and event licensing: an officially licensed collector card programme for a fictional continental club football tournament, sold to fans 16 to 45 through the tournament store and specialty card retailers (Western Europe and North America)
real_brief_anchor: Ledger anchor for PHOTO-17 (Freelancer.com, reference null). Its grounding_note, quoted as far as the ledger carries it: 'Adapted from a real Freelancer.com poster brief for a high-impact football-tournament star poster with cinematic, high-contrast floodlit lighting and print+web delivery. Every real element is laundered: the tournament is the fictional Continental Cup 2026, the depicted athletes are eight clearly-fictional players ... with no real likeness, and no real club, nation, flag, emblem, competition, sponsor, camera, editing product or social platform is named anywhere. REPOSITIONED for connector reality: the literal source brief (drawing/AI-compositing named celebrities and a trophy into o' (the ledger note is truncated mid-word at that point). The literal ask, compositing named celebrities into an invented scene, is a banned capability here and would also fail the IP rule. This engagement is the fuller commission that poster client actually had once the compositing fantasy is removed: a licensed card programme, whose photography has to match across two nights of floodlight, whose card artwork survives only as the printer's flat file, and whose crest survives only as a photograph of a stitched sleeve patch. Absorbs AO-29. The eight players are invented Western and Latin-European names with no real likeness: Diego Solano, Marco Ferraz, Theo Rocher, Luka Petrov, Rafael Duarte, Nikolai Ivanic, Callum Reid, Mattias Holm.
client_one_liner: Our eight featured portraits were shot over two nights under different stadium lights and they do not match, we lost the studio that made last year's card, and the whole set has to be with retailers before the group stage.
client_brief:
Continental Cup 2026 collector card programme.

We hold the licence for the tournament's collector cards. This year's featured set is eight players and it has to be with retailers before the group stage, so the print half and the store half need to come from one person and look like one programme.

Our photographer worked two nights at the same ground. The pictures are good but they do not sit together: some are colder, some are greener, and one is much brighter than the rest. We need the eight to read as one shoot, dramatic and floodlit, the way a marquee cup set should look. We also need each player lifted cleanly off the stadium behind him for the card hero, because the hero also has to sit on the retailer's deep-navy display tile with nothing sitting round the edges of him.

The cards. The studio that designed last year's card has closed. All we have is the file the printer ran. The layout is right, the retailers know it, and we want it kept. What changes is everything on it: the eight players, their squad numbers, their honours line, the set year. The player data is attached exactly as it comes out of our licensing database. It is contractual copy. It goes on the card as written, not tidied, not shortened, not abbreviated.

The crest. We have never held the competition mark as a file. What we have is a photograph of the embroidered patch off an official's sleeve. We need it back as artwork we can place and scale, and it has to still read as the competition mark on the card, which is where it reproduces smallest.

Alongside the cards we need the launch set for the store: a wide banner image, a square post and a tall one. Those three come back as one working file we can edit ourselves, because the on-sale date moves every year. Give us whatever it was built from as well.

On look and level: a pack is twelve dollars, a sealed box is ninety-five, and the featured cards trade well above that. The buyer knows what a licensed set looks like. Deep, saturated, high contrast, floodlit blacks. Not a community-league treatment, flat and bright and cheerful, and not a neon gaming poster either.

What we need back: the press card file, one single-card file per player named so our retail team can attach the right one without opening it, the finished photography, the recovered crest, the three launch canvases as one editable file, and a short note saying what you did to each picture, what type we are using, and anything in the player data you had to question.
price_band_and_audience: Premium licensed collector programme. Pack twelve dollars, sealed box ninety-five, featured base cards trading roughly thirty to one hundred and twenty dollars on the secondary market. Buyers are 16 to 45, they collect officially licensed cup sets and they can tell a licensed set from a fan-made one at a glance. The band is load-bearing: at this level the treatment is deep and saturated with real floodlit blacks, one dominant player per card with the stadium reduced to atmosphere, and type set large and confident. If this were a community-league set at three dollars a pack the correct answer is the opposite artefact: flat daylight, bright neutral grounds, four players to a sheet, and no isolation work at all. An agent that ships bright, flat and cheerful has misread the commission even if every field binds, and an agent that ships neon gradients and glow has misread it the other way. A posted job of this shape runs 1,800 to 3,500 dollars fixed, or 50 to 85 dollars an hour over 30 to 45 hours.

assets_supplied.name: cup26_portraits_raw/ (8 frames, 4800px long edge)

Diego Solano, Marco Ferraz, Theo Rocher, Luka Petrov, Rafael Duarte, Nikolai Ivanic, Callum Reid, Mattias Holm. They do not match and we need them to." Camera-scale, one player per frame, crowd and stand behind each.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two things the client cannot see. (1) Rafael Duarte was shot with a floodlight tower directly behind him. His white sleeve, his near shoulder and the ball at his hip are clipped to paper white with nothing left in them at all. On a screen it reads as the most dramatic frame of the eight, and the photographer flagged it as his favourite. A highlight recovery on it moves nothing whatsoever, and that readout of nothing is the only evidence that exists. (2) Luka Petrov is the keeper, in a dark navy kit, standing against a shadowed block of crowd at almost the same value as the kit. A subject knockout on him bites into the shoulder and the near arm where kit and crowd share luminance, and his raised arm encloses a genuine see-through gap between forearm and head that comes back filled with captured crowd. Both calls report full success and both defects are invisible against a light ground.

assets_supplied.name: cup26_card_2025_PRINTER.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: document
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The card file the printer ran last year. It is all we have. The layout is right, keep it." A real press PDF at trading-card trim, 63.5 x 88.9 mm, fonts embedded, produced from a genuine page layout so it converts cleanly. Carries the player name, squad number, position, honours line and set year, plus the player photograph and a small placed crest.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three properties of how the closed studio built the 2025 document, announced nowhere. First, the printed card looks like five separately labelled fields but the placed images split the flow into two text frames only, and the split falls in an unobvious place, so several of the five lines share one continuous story and can only be driven by ordered offset arithmetic inside it. Second, the mapping readout of that multi-line story silently omits the run holding the honours line while keeping its line break, so the string still reads as well-formed and every character offset after it is short by exactly that run's length. The validator returns valid on the resulting arithmetic and the placeholder step reports success, and two fields never become placeholders. Third, the crest frame is a fraction of the size the printed card suggests, so the reproduction size of the recovered crest is geometry inherited from a printer nobody can ask.

acceptance_bar: The eight portraits read as one set when laid side by side as they will sit in a retailer's row: one black point, one warmth, one crop logic. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is pulled and named to us, not shipped at eighty percent.
Every card hero is genuinely separated from the stadium: no fringe, no halo, no captured crowd left inside a gap, checked close up on the retailer's deep-navy tile and not only on a light ground.

No delivered picture is larger than the picture it came from. Where a crop would have meant inventing pixels you chose a different crop or expanded the frame, and the note lists every picture any tool resized and by how much.

The press card file has exactly one page per featured player, in roster order, with no extra page and no missing page. If the count we get is not the count we gave you, the note says which row you left out and on whose authority.

Every card carries every line the 2025 card carried: player, squad number, position, honours line, set year, that player's own photograph and the crest. A card missing a line is a failed card even if the file opened.
Nothing in the player data is reworded, shortened, re-spaced or abbreviated. It is contractual copy.
No card ships with copy clipped or truncated at true trim. Any card you cannot give us that way, name it to us in writing before it reaches the printer.
Each single-card file actually contains the player its filename claims, established by opening it rather than by the order the files came back in.
Proofs render at real print resolution at card trim.
The recovered crest is artwork we can scale and place on any ground, with no white box behind it, and it still reads as the competition mark at the size the card reproduces it.
In the launch file the crest is real vector artwork and the words are live text we can retype, not a picture of a layout.
All three launch canvases sit in ONE working file, each keeping its own canvas size, and we also get the self-contained source it was built from.
One type system across all three canvases, and the note names, per role, the family, its foundry or designer, and the weight actually used.
The selects board carries every finished picture with nothing silently missing from it.
The note states, per picture, what you did to it, and lists every row in the player data you questioned and what was done about it.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which half of the commission lands on which surface.
trajectory.judgement: The split is the first real decision and the brief does not state it. The cards are record per page against a layout the client wants preserved, so they belong on the merge surface. The launch set is three different canvas sizes that the client must edit next year, so it belongs on HTML authoring. Reversing this loses either the layout or the editability. The brief pins the delivery destination itself, an editable file plus the source it was built from, so there is nothing to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming deliverable to surface, and the confirmed account tier that gates the export.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each presigned URL against a role manifest.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline, but thirty artefacts later the manifest is the only thing that keeps the Petrov frame distinguishable from the Rocher frame.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Preview all eight portraits and the wide frame. Triage each: tilt, which night, what is behind the player, how tight the subject sits to the frame edge, and how much separation there is between kit and background.
trajectory.judgement: The client says the pictures do not match, which is true but is not the whole triage. The agent has to look at what is behind each player, because that is what decides whether a knockout will hold, and it has to notice which frames are too tight to survive the card cell before it fixes a crop policy for the set rather than per frame.
trajectory.produces: A per-frame triage note covering tilt, night, ground separation and subject tightness, and the crop policy chosen for the set.

trajectory.action: Straighten the frames that need it.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes the subject and eats edge pixels, so it happens before any crop is locked, not after.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix one house look on the strongest frame and correct every other frame toward it, one call per frame, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a set, not eight good pictures. Frames from the two nights need materially different corrections to arrive at the same place, and a single batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong here. The agent must hold one destination in its head rather than optimising each frame alone.
trajectory.produces: Eight corrected masters at source scale with a per-frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Masked work where a whole-frame correction is wrong: select the kit or the skin, invert where the correction belongs to the other side, apply the confined adjustment.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the whole gate. Naming the object the graphic sits on pulls the selection to the wrong thing, and naming the material's own visual properties pulls it to the right one. Floodlit skin and a saturated kit want opposite moves and cannot both be served globally.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a global move would have taken the kit muddy or the skin orange.

trajectory.action: Produce the card heroes: triage the knockout route per frame, run the one-call route where the subject is a single coherent shape against separable ground, and handle the rest by naming the ground material, inverting and filling.
trajectory.judgement: The two routes are not interchangeable and the choice is per frame, not per set. The direct route cannot punch a gap enclosed by a limb, and a knockout that reports success is not the same as a knockout that holds.
trajectory.produces: Transparent heroes and flat-ground heroes for all eight players.

trajectory.action: Place every transparent hero on the retailer's deep-navy tile ground and inspect the cut edge close up.
trajectory.judgement: This is the only place the edges can actually be judged, because a bitten shoulder and a filled gap both look clean against white. Looking is a decision the agent has to make; nothing prompts it.
trajectory.produces: The hero-on-dark composite tiles, and an edge verdict per player.

trajectory.action: Crop to the card cell ratio and to the launch ratios, reading the confidence and tradeoff metadata every crop returns rather than trusting success.
trajectory.judgement: The tradeoffs array is the only signal that a crop clipped, that detection was weak, or that an output was interpolated upward, and it is easy to ignore. Where a crop would clip, the choice between expanding the short axis and cropping looser is a craft call, and generated edge material must itself match the house look.
trajectory.produces: Card-cell heroes, launch-ratio masters, and a no-enlargement record drawn from the tradeoffs actually reported.

trajectory.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, vector recovery
trajectory.action: Recover the competition mark off the sleeve patch: an ink-level selection naming the mark's own visual properties, inverted for correct polarity, cropped to the selection's own bounds, traced, then given a viewBox with the opaque full-canvas ground path removed. Produce a colour-accurate plate as well.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions the tools do not make: how to word the selection so it takes the mark and not the fabric, which polarity to trace, and whether the card takes the two-colour trace or the colour plate. Background removal is the wrong instrument on an enclosed ring and returns a solid disc.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent crest plus a colour-accurate variant and a high-resolution plate for the card frame.

trajectory.surface: Data preparation and Creative Cloud storage
trajectory.action: Reconcile the licensing export against the client's own list of eight, normalise headers, build the prefixed image column holding bare filenames, upload the card-cell heroes and build the image map against them.
trajectory.judgement: Real reconciliation. The row count and the stated player count disagree, and the agent has to decide whether dropping a row the licensing database emitted is its call or the client's to confirm, and how to say so. The image column contract is specific and a plain header silently binds nothing.
trajectory.produces: The merge data file, uploaded heroes, the image map, and a first list of data questions for the note.

trajectory.action: Convert the printer PDF to a native document, export IDML from it, unzip it, and reconstruct each frame's true story text by concatenating its content runs. Record the real integer page-item ids, the frame count and the bounds.
trajectory.judgement: This is where the mapping strategy is actually decided and the answer is a property of the client's PDF, not of the plan. Per-frame mapping if the lines came across separately, offset arithmetic inside one story if they did not. The agent must also decide which text it will compute offsets from, and the fast answer and the reliable answer are different strings.
trajectory.produces: The converted document, its IDML, a real frame inventory, and an independently reconstructed story text.

trajectory.action: Generate the mapping prompt against the IDML and the data file, author the mapping covering every text field plus the photo frame and the crest frame, and pass it back through the validator.
trajectory.judgement: Choosing the right action for the granularity that came back, using the integer page-item id as the uid, ordering any rows sharing a uid so their positions hold against the original text, and passing the whole mapping as one stringified object.
trajectory.produces: A validated mapping covering every field on the card.

trajectory.action: Prepare the merge template, then export IDML from the result, unzip it and grep the stories for every placeholder the mapping claimed to create.
trajectory.judgement: Not accepting a success message as evidence. Nothing in the chain instructs this and nothing warns if it is skipped, and it is the only place the mapping's real yield is visible before pages exist.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholder inventory has been independently confirmed.

trajectory.action: Merge to a native InDesign document with the per-row heroes bound, then render the press file and the 300 ppi proofs from that document.
trajectory.judgement: Route matters and it is practically irreversible: merging straight to raster silently drops to screen resolution whatever resolution is requested, and merging straight to PDF forfeits per-record rendering afterwards. If the image map does not carry at this row count, the fallback is a single-record loop binding one image per call.
trajectory.produces: The press card file at card trim and the 300 ppi proofs.

trajectory.action: Produce the per-player single-card files by the route whose record identity is guaranteed, and name each by opening it rather than by its position in the returned list.
trajectory.judgement: Returned order is not trustworthy on every route, and naming eight files by position is the fast wrong answer that ends with a retailer receiving the wrong player.
trajectory.produces: Eight single-card files, named to player, identity verified by inspection.

trajectory.action: Read every card at true trim against the data file, line by line and photograph by photograph.
trajectory.judgement: Reading the output rather than the log. Overset is reported nowhere and a wrongly bound photograph is reported nowhere, and neither reads as broken on a screen-scale proxy.
trajectory.produces: A card by card reconciliation against the licensing export.

trajectory.action: Search Stock with short generic queries for the wide floodlit ground frame the banner needs, filter to photography, exclude generative results, license and download at full resolution, then grade it toward the house look and lay it beside the eight.
trajectory.judgement: Choosing a frame whose existing light can be brought to the house look rather than the best thumbnail. Two frames that look equally cold at thumbnail size can be a full grade apart at full resolution.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP-clean, camera-scale banner ground, graded and judged against the set.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit for the whole system.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is entirely the agent's and has to answer to a licensed cup set rather than a club fanzine. The numeric weight cannot be inferred from the style name, a display cut is reached by its own family slug, and the CSS must use the returned stack.
trajectory.produces: A one-kit type system with family, foundry or designer and real weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self-contained HTML with three roots at three canvas sizes, embedding every photograph as image data rather than a reference, placing the crest as inline vector inside an explicitly sized and top-left anchored wrapper, declaring family and weight on every text element and letting each root declare its own canvas size. Upload the HTML and export it, then verify canvas one by resolving the document's rendition and looking, and canvases two and three by parsing the returned per-canvas markup.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto-sized right-anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, weight is not inherited from markup semantics, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed-size set. Every one of those drops returns success. The design decisions, how much of the frame the player occupies and how large the crest sits, are the actual work.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document with all three canvases, the retained source HTML, an inspected first canvas and a markup audit of the other two.

trajectory.action: Create the selects board and add the finished pictures, batching within the per-call placement cap and treating a partial success as partial by re-sending only the entries named as failed. Then write the handover note.
trajectory.judgement: What to escalate and what to fix silently. The client asked to hear about data problems, so the note has to name every row questioned and every card that could not be delivered inside their own layout, before the file reaches a printer rather than after.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable selects board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: That one of the eight frames cannot be brought to the set at all. The Duarte frame was shot into a floodlight tower and its white sleeve, near shoulder and the ball are clipped with nothing left in them. The only way to learn this is to apply a highlight correction and read a result in which nothing moves. Every other frame in the set responds normally to the same move, this one responds by not responding, and the tool reports success either way. At preview the frame reads as the most dramatic of the eight and the photographer flagged it as his favourite, so nothing about looking at it suggests a problem.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and care cannot either. There is no readout of headroom anywhere in the connector, no histogram, no measurement of any kind, and the agent is explicitly not measuring pixels. A frame with genuinely empty highlights and a frame that is merely bright look identical until a recovery is attempted, and the attempt is the measurement. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the pictures do not match and that one is brighter than the rest, which is a client describing a mismatch, not a disclosure that a frame is unrecoverable. No asset note, no acceptance line and no deliverable names Duarte or clipping. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is not to re-grade with different numbers, it is to decide that this player's card hero has to come from somewhere else, which changes what is licensed, what is cropped and what is escalated to the client, and to say so in writing rather than shipping a card at eighty percent.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Confirm the frame is genuinely empty rather than merely under-corrected by attempting recovery from a different direction and reading the same non-response, then decide the fallback: crop into the frame away from the clipped shoulder if enough of the player survives, or hold the card and name the frame to the client under their own standing request. Re-lay the remaining seven plus whatever replaces it and re-judge the set as a set, because pulling one frame moves the set's centre and the other seven may need to move with it.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A featured card ships with the player's shoulder and sleeve as a flat white shape with no detail, in a saturated high-contrast set where every other card holds its highlights, and the retailer sees it as a printing fault in a licensed product.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the card heroes actually hold at the edge, on the ground they are going to be used on. Petrov is in dark navy against a shadowed block of crowd at nearly the same value, so the knockout bites into the shoulder and the near arm where there is no contrast to work with, and his raised arm encloses a gap that comes back filled with captured crowd rather than punched through. Whether a given photograph gives the subject detector enough separation is a property of that frame's light and that player's kit, not of the tool or the plan. The failure is completely silent: the call succeeds, the returned cutout looks correct at normal viewing size, and on the card's own light ground the missing shoulder and the filled gap are invisible. Only the deep-navy retailer tile, at close inspection, shows the pale slab inside the arm and the chewed edge.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it. Every frame must be knocked out regardless of order, and there is no property of the file, no metadata and no tool response that reports edge quality. A careful agent choosing the right route for a coherent subject still gets a bitten edge on the one frame where kit and ground share value, because the route is not the variable, the photograph is. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for each player lifted cleanly off the stadium and mentions the deep-navy tile, which is the client stating what they need, not a warning that one frame will resist. No asset note names Petrov's kit or the crowd behind him. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The fix is a different operation on a different principle: name the ground material, invert the selection and fill it, rather than ask for the subject, and for the enclosed gap the direct route can never be made to work at all. The earlier asset is replaced, not re-fed.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-cut the affected heroes by naming the material behind the player rather than the player, invert and fill to the flat ground, and handle the enclosed gap as its own selection composited into the mask rather than expecting the subject route to punch it. Re-place on the deep tile and inspect again rather than assuming the second attempt took. Check the other seven at the same close inspection, because the reason to look was found on one frame and the reason to trust the rest has not been established.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The retailer's display tile shows a keeper with a pale slab of stadium crowd sitting inside the arc of his own raised arm and a shoulder eaten into the crowd behind it, in a licensed premium set, having been signed off against a light-ground proof where none of it was visible.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's card actually becomes as editable structure, and then whether the mapping built against it landed. Two facts arrive only by running. First, granularity: whether the five printed lines come across as five addressable frames or collapse into a continuous story, and whether the photograph and the crest arrived as real graphic frames with integer ids, is a property of how the closed studio built the 2025 document and is under nobody's control. Second, yield: the mapping tool's convenience readout of the story silently omits the run holding the honours line while keeping its line break, so the string still parses as well-formed prose and every offset past it is short by exactly that run's length. The validator returns valid on internally consistent wrong arithmetic, the preparation step reports success, and two fields never become placeholders. Only an independent reconstruction of the story from the exported IDML's content runs, followed by a round trip and a grep of the prepared file, makes either fact visible.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Neither ordering nor diligence dodges it. Granularity is not a parameter and has no read-ahead. Yield is worse, because the failure is produced by a readout that presents as complete, so an agent that reads carefully and computes offsets diligently from the string it was handed produces arithmetic that is internally consistent and wrong, and every downstream tool agrees with it. The defence is a second reconstruction of the same text from a different channel, which nothing in any tool description prompts. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the layout is right and should be kept, and mentions no frames, offsets or mappings. The acceptance bar states an output requirement, that every card carries every line, which is the client's standing requirement and not a description of a cause. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. What changes is the mapping strategy and its source of truth, from placeholder replacement against a tool readout to offset arithmetic computed against a reconstructed story with same-frame rows re-ordered. The mapping is re-authored from a different text, not re-fed.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story by concatenating the IDML content runs, recompute every offset against that string, re-order rows sharing a uid so their positions hold against the original text, rebuild and re-validate the mapping, re-run the preparation, and re-verify by round-tripping IDML and grepping for every placeholder before any page is merged. If the photograph or the crest did not come across as a mappable frame, the binding has to be re-planned before the merge rather than discovered after it.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A press card file that binds the player, the number and the set year correctly on all eight cards while the honours line is simply absent from every one of them, silently, with every tool in the chain having reported success, going to a printer against a contractual copy requirement.

decision_gates: The surface split: cards to the merge surface because they are record per page against a layout the client wants preserved, launch set to HTML authoring because it needs three canvas sizes and must stay editable.
Whether one house look can be reached from both nights, and how far each frame is pushed before it stops being worth saving.
What to do with the frame that will not come back, given the client called it the best of the eight.
Knockout route per frame rather than per set, and how to treat a gap enclosed by a limb that the direct route cannot punch.
On which ground the cut edges are judged, given that the ground the client will use is the only one that shows them.
Crop policy for the set as a whole versus per frame, and on the tight frames whether to expand generated edge material or crop looser, knowing the generated edge must itself match the house look.
The row-count discrepancy in the licensing export: whether dropping a row the database emitted is the agent's call or the client's to confirm, and how to say so.

Whether to trust the mapping tool's own readout of the client's text or to reconstruct the story from the document. One route is fast and produces confidently wrong arithmetic that every downstream tool blesses.
Whether a success message counts as verification of the prepared template.
How to honour contractual copy when one record cannot be set inside a frame the connector gives no way to change.
Whether to name eight per-record files by returned order or by opening each one.

Selection wording on the sleeve patch, where naming the fabric takes the fabric and naming the mark's own visual properties takes the mark, and which crest variant carries the card at its real reproduction size.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a licensed collector band, and the real numeric weight per family.
Whether the licensed banner frame joins the set or reads as bought, and if bought, whether to push it further or search again on the light rather than the subject.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a picture of a trading card. IDENTITY: these are eight specific photographs of eight specific players under this tournament's floodlights, and the crest is a specific embroidered mark that has to be recovered from a photograph, not reinvented. A regenerated player is a different person and a regenerated crest is a different competition, which is the one thing a licensed programme cannot survive. SPEC: the client needs one page per featured player at card trim with contractual copy bound verbatim from a licensing database, eight separately named single-card files each containing the player its filename claims, and print-resolution proofs. A generated image satisfies none of that and cannot be checked against a roster. EDITABILITY: two deliverables are defined by being editable, a live merge template so next season is a data change rather than a re-commission, and a document with live text and real vector geometry so the on-sale date changes without a redo. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: does this highlight recover, does this cut edge hold on navy, did this placeholder actually get created, is this record clipped at trim, does this trace still read at card size. None of that is a generation problem.
doability_proof: Five surfaces, honestly counted, all verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account). MERGE SPINE: convert_pdf_to_indd to export_idml to generate_indd_mapping_prompt to prepare_indd_merge_template is verified end to end from a bare press PDF, one record per page is confirmed for PDF output, per-record files are confirmed by two order-safe routes (createSeparateFiles and a recordRange loop) while multi-record raster order is documented as reversed and is therefore avoided, and true 300 ppi comes from document_render_layout because outputSpecs.resolution on the merge itself is silently ignored. The card PDF is specified as a real font-embedding press PDF produced from a genuine layout, because a thin hand-authored PDF fails conversion opaquely. Frame granularity behaviour is taken from the verified observation that interleaved images split a flow into two text frames plus graphic frames, and the trajectory degrades gracefully whichever way it lands. The lossy textContent readout is a documented, reproduced live finding, including the validator returning valid and the preparation step reporting success on wrong offsets. IMAGE BINDING: the prefixed CSV column plus additionalImageFiles is verified visually at three rows, so the eight-row run carries an explicit fallback of a recordRange loop binding one image per call, which also guarantees per-record identity. IMAGING: auto_straighten, masked and unmasked adjustments, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, fill_area, remove_background in both transparent and backgroundColor forms, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs array, generative_expand and vectorize are all verified headless. The enclosed-void failure of remove_background is a documented live finding (a solid opaque disc where a knockout was expected), as are the substrate versus ink prompt asymmetry, vectorize's missing viewBox and opaque first path, and the fact that crop_and_resize interpolates to a hard cap and reports it only in tradeoffs. Highlight recovery on genuinely empty highlights returning no visible change is a property of the material, not a tool claim, and the acceptance bar scores the decision and the disclosure rather than any measurement. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, photographs must be embedded as data because every external URL renders as an empty placeholder, and the HTML is routed through the upload path with media_type text/html because three canvases of embedded photography exceed the inline threshold. Verification is split to match the two channels that exist: the rendition preview shows the first canvas only, so canvases two and three are audited from the returned markup. Persistence is not assumed, so the deliverable is the editable document plus the self-contained source. FONTS: font_recommend to font_styles to find_fonts to get_fontkit_embed_url is verified end to end, and the non-standard numeric weights, the slug-not-PostScript CSS rule and the all-or-nothing kit call are live findings the task leans on. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only (long queries return zero), the orientation filter is broken and never passed, licensing returns genuine camera-scale imagery, and boards persist with a hard cap of twelve placements per call where a 201 means partial success with a failed-items list. IMAGE VOLUME: ten client image files in, roughly thirty image artefacts moved in total, every multi-image call at or under the ten-item cap and no batch above twenty. AVOIDED: no video or audio (all async with no poll tool in this host), no document_render_vector or document_merge_data_vector, no variable QR, no bleed gate, no pdfPreset, no fill_text, no animate_design, no replace_image, no download_design, no upscaling, no OCR, no compositing, no from-scratch image generation, and no photograph reaching Express as a URL.

engagement_title: Fernwell & Rowe, season post-production partner: prove a walk-away house pass on the Hartley wedding across three lighting regimes, recover the studio seal, rebuild the printer's thank-you card into a live run, and hand back the venue-partner set editable
vertical: Media and personal: a two-person wedding and event photography studio in the Cotswolds, England, shooting twenty-two weddings a season for couples booking full-day coverage
real_brief_anchor: The ledger entry for PHOTO-18 carries no quoted posted brief and no absorbed task, so this is stated plainly rather than dressed up: the engagement is built to the posted-job archetype the ledger records, a wedding and event photographer needing a fast, consistent first-pass polish across a very large set so the gallery reads finished and even before client review, at a full-day coverage band of 3,200 to 5,500 dollars. That archetype is a standing category on the freelance marketplaces (walk-away batch retouching for wedding photographers, priced per event or per season) and it is the same shape the connector's own retouch-portraits routing describes: a folder of frames from one event, polished and returned ready to review. The rebuild verdict applies because the ledger concept as it stood was a single-surface batch operation whose deliverable list was one gallery at several sizes. Here the batch pass is the pilot half of a season partnership, and it is joined by the couple-facing print run and the studio's own venue-partner collateral, which is what a studio actually buys when it takes on a post-production partner. The studio, the couple, the households and the venue are all invented: Fernwell & Rowe, the Hartley wedding, the Orangery at Ashcombe Park.
client_one_liner: We shoot six to nine hundred frames a wedding across ceremony, golden hour and a dark reception, we cannot hand-edit every one, and before we hand you the season we want to see you hold one look across the Hartley set and take the couple's cards and our venue pitch off our hands with it.
client_brief:
Fernwell & Rowe, Cotswolds. There are two of us and we shoot twenty-two weddings a season.

We are looking for someone to take our post-production for the season, and this is the trial. The Hartley wedding is the set we are giving you: sixteen frames the couple shortlisted, taken across three completely different situations. The ceremony was inside with window light, the portraits were the last hour of sun in the walled garden, and the reception ran until one in the morning under the venue's own coloured uplighters. What we need is one house pass that holds across all of it, run the same way every time, so that when the season starts we hand you nine hundred frames and get back a gallery that already looks finished and even. Warm, natural, true skin. Never orange, never crunchy, never that filtered look. If a frame will not take the house pass, we would rather you pull it out and tell us than force it.

Out of that same set the couple have starred six for full-resolution prints, and one of the six is going on the cover of their album and on their thank-you cards.

The cards are the second piece. The couple are sending a thank-you card to each household that came. Our card artwork was made for us two years ago and the designer is not around any more, so all we have is the file our printer ran. Each card carries the household's name and the couple's message. The guest list is attached the way the RSVP tool exported it. Please do not tidy the household names, they are how people asked to be addressed.

The third piece is for us rather than the couple. We are pitching three venues for their winter dates and we need a leave-behind: an A4 sheet plus a square post and a tall one, all three in one file we can edit ourselves, because the venue name and the dates change with every pitch. Our look on that sheet is the tinted vellum treatment we use, warm ink over the photograph rather than a photograph sitting flat on a page. We do not have a picture of the venue in winter light, only a phone snap from the June wedding, so if you think we need one, get one.

Our seal is the last thing. It is a wax seal we press on every envelope, and it has never existed as a file. We are attaching a photograph of one. We want it on the card, on the sheet and on the posts, and it has to still look like our seal.

On level: full-day coverage is three and a half to five thousand and our couples are around thirty. It should feel like a real day, warm and honest, not a magazine shoot and not a phone filter.

What we need back: the sixteen at review size, the six keepers at full resolution, the cards ready for the printer plus one file per household, the leave-behind set as one editable file with its source, the seal as usable artwork, a shared board the four of us can look at, and a note telling us exactly what your house pass is, so we can hold you to it for the rest of the season.
price_band_and_audience: Full-day wedding coverage 3,200 to 5,500 pounds, couples aged 27 to 38, booking a Cotswolds country-house venue eighteen months out. The band is load-bearing on every decision. At this level the expected finish is warm, natural and true to skin, delivered fast and even across an entire day, because the couple's parents will look at these prints for thirty years. Push it toward a heavy stylised grade, crushed blacks, teal shadows and a strong preset signature, and it reads as a cheaper filtered package that the couple will regret; leave it flat and uncorrected and it reads as unfinished at the price. The venue leave-behind sits at the same band: warm paper, generous white space, one photograph doing the work, prices and dates set plainly. A glossy dark luxury treatment would misprice the studio to a venue that books at this level, and a bright busy collage would undersell it. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. The fuller engagement of this shape runs 1,200 to 2,600 pounds for the pilot plus a per-event season rate.

assets_supplied.name: hartley_selects/ (16 frames, camera scale)
assets_supplied.kind: image
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The sixteen the couple shortlisted. Ceremony inside with window light, portraits in the last hour of sun, reception under the venue's uplighters. Six of them are starred for full-resolution prints."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The reception is not one lighting situation. The venue's uplighters were switched from amber to magenta at the first dance, so within the reception block two illuminants sit side by side, and the frames after the switch carry a magenta cast that a warm house pass pushes further rather than correcting. Each of those frames looks plausible on its own, which is why the studio has never named it, and the break only declares itself when the block is laid out as a run in gallery order. Separately, two of the six starred keepers were shot by the second shooter on a different body with a flatter, cooler profile, so they arrive at a different starting point from the fourteen and need a different correction to reach the same place.

assets_supplied.name: fernwell_card_2025_PRINTER.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: document
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The thank-you card artwork our printer ran. We do not have the working file and the designer is not around any more." A real press PDF at A6 landscape, fonts embedded, produced from a genuine page layout. Carries the household line, the couple's message, the date line, a photograph and the studio seal on a pale panel.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The photograph on the card is not a placed image. The designer flattened it into the page artwork, so the conversion exposes no addressable graphic frame for it at all, and per-household picture variation is structurally impossible inside the client's own artwork no matter how the data is shaped. Nothing in the printed card suggests this and nothing in the conversion reports it. On the text side the household line and the message share one continuous story while the date line sits alone, so the fields cannot be addressed uniformly and same-story insertions have to be ordered against the original text.

assets_supplied.name: guest_households.csv
assets_supplied.kind: data
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The guest list as the RSVP tool exported it. Do not tidy the household names, they are how people asked to be addressed."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Fourteen rows for twelve households: two households replied twice through the RSVP tool and appear with slightly different spellings, so a straight run prints two duplicate cards and the file count stops matching the household count. Headers are mixed-case with trailing spaces. And one household line is far longer than the rest, a double-barrelled family name with a village appended, which oversets the fixed card frame at true trim while every other record sits comfortably. Nothing reports overset anywhere.

assets_supplied.name: fernwell_seal.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: image
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our wax seal, pressed on an envelope. It has never existed as a file." A close phone frame of a dark red wax seal on a cream envelope, shot under a window.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Wax is not ink. The impression carries a specular sheen across the raised areas and a small bubble at one edge, so a trace breaks the strokes wherever a highlight crossed them and picks up the torn flash around the rim as if it were part of the mark. The monogram's counters are partly filled with wax flash, which reads as detail at full canvas and as a solid blob at the size the card's seal panel reproduces it. There is no option on the tracing step to tune any of this, so the only lever is the raster preparation, and which preparation is needed cannot be known until the result is seen at size.

assets_supplied.name: venue_snap.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: image
assets_supplied.visible_description: "A phone snap of the Orangery from the June wedding, if it is any use for the leave-behind."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: 1600px on the long edge and shot at midday in flat overhead June light with the sky washed out. It is comfortably large enough for a square or tall social canvas and nowhere near large enough for the A4 sheet's hero, and it shows the venue in exactly the season the pitch is not about. It looks usable as a thumbnail.

assets_supplied.name: house_look_notes.txt
assets_supplied.kind: document
assets_supplied.visible_description: A paragraph from Rowe on the house look in plain language: warm, natural, true skin, never orange, never crunchy, black point held open, and the standing rule that a frame that will not take the pass gets pulled and named rather than forced.

acceptance_bar: The sixteen read as one day when laid out in gallery order, not as three separate edits joined together, and no frame in the run jumps against its neighbours.

The house pass is a stated recipe we can hold you to for the season, named in the note, not a set of sixteen individual rescues. Where a frame needed something outside the recipe, the note says which frame and why in one line.
Skin is true across the whole run under all three lighting situations. Nothing orange, nothing plum, nothing plastic.
Any frame that will not take the house pass is pulled and named to us, not forced and shipped.

The six keepers are delivered at full resolution with no invented pixels anywhere in the package. No delivered file is larger than its source, and the note lists every picture any tool resized and by how much.

The thank-you cards run exactly one card per household, with the household name printed exactly as the guest wrote it, and the file count matches the household count. If the count we get is not the count we gave you, the note says which rows you merged or dropped and on what basis.
No card ships with a household name or the message clipped at true trim. Any card you cannot give us that way, name it before it goes to the printer.
Each per-household file contains the household its filename claims, established by opening it.
Printer proofs render at real print resolution at card trim.
The leave-behind carries our tinted vellum treatment as it actually looks, warm ink over the photograph, and the photograph is visible in the finished file rather than buried or missing.
All three leave-behind canvases sit in ONE editable file, each keeping its own canvas size, and we get the self-contained source it was built from.
The seal is placeable artwork with no white box behind it, and it still reads as our seal at the size the card and the sheet reproduce it, including on the warm ink panel.
One type system across the sheet and both posts, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the weight actually used.
The board carries the finished set with nothing silently missing from it.
