trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and split the commission: the card run to the merge surface, the leave-behind to HTML authoring, the gallery to imaging.
trajectory.judgement: The brief does not state the split. The cards are record per page against artwork the studio wants kept, the leave-behind needs three canvas sizes and must stay editable per pitch. Reversing them loses either the artwork or the editability.
trajectory.produces: A plan naming deliverable to surface, and the confirmed tier.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset and hold a role manifest of presigned URLs.
trajectory.judgement: Handoff discipline, and the only thing that keeps sixteen event frames distinguishable once crops and renditions multiply.
trajectory.produces: A manifest keyed by role and by lighting block.

trajectory.action: Preview all sixteen and group them by what is actually in them: which are window light, which are late sun, which are under the uplighters, and which came off a different body.
trajectory.judgement: The brief gives three situations and the agent has to decide whether three is the right number of treatment groups by looking rather than by accepting the client's own description of their day. Two frames from the second shooter start somewhere else entirely, and grouping by the story of the day rather than by the light in the frame is the fast wrong answer.
trajectory.produces: A grouping of the sixteen by illuminant and starting point, with a note per group.

trajectory.action: Read the preset catalogue, choose a candidate house recipe against the stated look, apply it across the set, and record exactly what the recipe is.
trajectory.judgement: The catalogue gives names, not behaviour, and the preset tool is whole-frame with no mask, so what a named recipe does to a face under window light versus under coloured uplight cannot be read off the list. The deliverable is a recipe the studio can be held to for a season, not sixteen bespoke edits, so the temptation to rescue each frame individually is the wrong instinct even though it produces a better-looking sixteen.
trajectory.produces: A first pass across all sixteen under one named recipe, with the recipe written down.

trajectory.action: Lay the first pass out in gallery order and read it as a run rather than frame by frame.
trajectory.judgement: Judging the set as a set at the only moment the comparison exists. A frame that is acceptable alone can be unacceptable between its neighbours, and gallery order is how the couple will see it.
trajectory.produces: A run-level verdict on the first pass, naming any frame or block that jumps.

trajectory.action: Deliver the review renditions for all sixteen and the full-resolution keepers for the six starred frames, holding crop discipline and reading the tradeoff metadata each crop returns.
trajectory.judgement: Review size and full resolution are two different products from one master, and the keepers must not pass through any step that quietly interpolates. The tradeoffs array is the only signal that one did.
trajectory.produces: Sixteen review renditions, six full-resolution keepers, and a resize record.

trajectory.action: Prepare the album-cover frame at the card's hero ratio and at the leave-behind hero ratio.
trajectory.judgement: One frame serving a printed card and an A4 sheet needs two different crops with the same intent, and the card's ratio is inherited from artwork nobody can change.
trajectory.produces: Two ratio masters from the couple's chosen frame.

trajectory.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, vector recovery
trajectory.action: Recover the studio seal: a selection naming the wax's own visual properties rather than the envelope, inverted for polarity, cropped to the selection's bounds, traced, then given a viewBox with the opaque ground path removed.
trajectory.judgement: Naming the object the mark sits on takes the envelope; naming the mark's own colour and material takes the wax. Polarity decides whether the trace is a mark or a filled box, and background removal is the wrong instrument on an impression with enclosed counters.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent seal plus a colour-accurate variant.

trajectory.action: Reconcile the RSVP export against the stated household count, normalise the headers, and prepare the merge data file.
trajectory.judgement: Two households appear twice with different spellings and the client has forbidden tidying the names, so merging duplicates and preserving the address form pull against each other. Whether a merge is the agent's call or the couple's to confirm is a judgement that has to be made and stated.
trajectory.produces: The merge data file and a first list of data questions for the note.

trajectory.action: Convert the printer's card PDF, export IDML, unzip it, and read the real inventory: how many text frames, how many graphic frames, which object styles, the true integer page-item ids, and the true story text reconstructed from the content runs.
trajectory.judgement: This is where the binding strategy is decided and the answer belongs to the client's artwork rather than the plan. The agent has to establish what is actually addressable before promising any field or picture will vary, and it has to decide which text it computes offsets from.
trajectory.produces: The converted document, its IDML, a real frame inventory and a reconstructed story text.

trajectory.action: Author the mapping against what the conversion exposed, covering every variable field, and pass it back through the validator.
trajectory.judgement: Choosing the right action for the granularity that came back, using integer page-item ids, and ordering same-story rows so their positions hold against the original text.
trajectory.produces: A validated mapping.

trajectory.action: Prepare the merge template, then export IDML from the result and grep the stories for every placeholder the mapping claimed to create.
trajectory.judgement: A success message is not evidence. Nothing instructs this check and nothing warns if it is skipped.
trajectory.produces: A template whose placeholder inventory has been independently confirmed.

trajectory.action: Merge to a native document, render the press file and the print-resolution proofs, produce the per-household files by the identity-guaranteed route, and read every card at true trim against the guest list.
trajectory.judgement: Merging to the native document first keeps both the press branch and the per-record branch open, and resolution asked for at merge time is not honoured. Reading at trim rather than at proof scale is the only way clipped copy shows.
trajectory.produces: The press card file, one file per household named and identity verified, and the proofs, with a card by card reconciliation.

trajectory.action: Search Stock with short generic queries for a winter country-house frame, filter to photography, exclude generative results, license and download at full resolution, then bring it toward the house look and lay it beside the graded set.
trajectory.judgement: Choosing a frame whose light can be brought to the studio's look rather than the prettiest thumbnail, and judging it against the studio's own photography rather than on its own terms.
trajectory.produces: One licensed camera-scale winter frame, graded and judged against the set.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, read the family style inventories for real numeric weights, launder every name, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own and has to land on warm and honest rather than glossy luxury. Weight cannot be inferred from the style name and the CSS must use the returned stack or it falls back silently.
trajectory.produces: A one-kit type system with family, foundry or designer and real weight per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self-contained HTML with an A4 root and a square and a tall root, carrying the studio's tinted treatment over the hero, the seal as inline vector inside an explicitly sized wrapper, and every photograph embedded as image data. Upload the HTML and export it.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto-sized right-anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed-size set. The design work is how much air the sheet carries and how the treatment sits over the picture at this band.
trajectory.produces: An exported native Express document plus the retained source HTML.

trajectory.action: Verify the export through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at the first canvas, and parse the returned per-canvas markup for the other two, asserting per canvas that every photograph resolved to real image data, that the seal arrived as vector shapes, and that nothing resolves past its declared canvas width.
trajectory.judgement: Treating a successful export as unverified. Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition only ever shows the first canvas, so looking at page one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: An inspected first canvas and a markup audit of the other two.

trajectory.action: Create the shared board and add the finished set, treating a partial success as partial by re-sending only the entries named as failed. Then write the note: the house recipe as a recipe, the frames that needed something outside it and why, the type system, the data rows questioned, and anything the client's own card artwork could not do.
trajectory.judgement: The note is the actual season contract. It has to be specific enough that the studio can hold the freelancer to the same pass across nine hundred frames, and honest enough that a structural limit in their own artwork is named rather than quietly worked around.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: That no single named recipe holds the whole day, and specifically where it breaks. The preset catalogue gives names and nothing else, the preset tool is whole-frame with no mask, and what a given recipe does to a face is a function of the illuminant in that frame. The reception block is not one illuminant: the uplighters were switched from amber to magenta partway through, so a warm recipe that is correct everywhere else pushes the post-switch frames to plum skin. Every call succeeds, every frame looks like a plausible photograph on its own, and the studio itself has never named the switch. The break exists only as a discontinuity in the run, so it can only be seen by applying the recipe to the whole set and then laying the result out in gallery order and looking at it as a sequence.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and diligence alone cannot either. There is no way to interrogate a preset except by applying it, no mask to confine it, and no measurement anywhere. An agent that previews the sixteen first sees sixteen plausible frames from a long day; the fact that two of them are lit by a different colour of light than the frames on either side of them in the same block is not visible as a defect until a single treatment has been applied to both and the two sit adjacent. (b) Nothing states it. The brief names three situations, which is the client's own account of their day and is what makes the trap work, and it says nothing about the uplighters changing. No asset note, no acceptance line and no deliverable names the switch or the frames. The acceptance bar asks for skin to be true across the run, which is the studio's standing quality requirement, not a disclosure. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to change what the deliverable IS: the house pass stops being one recipe and becomes a recipe plus a named pre-correction for an identified group, which is the thing the studio will be held to for the rest of the season, and it has to be written up as such.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Split the reception block into two treatment groups by illuminant rather than by moment, apply a correction toward the house neutral to the post-switch group before the recipe rather than after it, re-run the recipe across the whole set so the pass stays one pass, and re-lay the run in gallery order and judge it again as a sequence rather than spot-checking the frames that were changed. Then rewrite the recipe in the note as what it actually is, because a recipe with an unnamed exception is not a recipe the studio can hold anyone to.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A gallery handed to a couple in which the first dance and everything after it has plum skin, sitting immediately after frames that are warm and true, delivered as the studio's proven house pass and about to be applied unchanged to nine hundred frames of the next wedding.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the studio's own card artwork actually exposes as editable structure. The printed card shows a photograph, so a per-household picture is a reasonable thing to plan for, and the guest data supports it. But the designer flattened the photograph into the page artwork rather than placing it, so the conversion exposes no addressable graphic frame for it at all, and per-household picture variation is structurally impossible inside the client's own file no matter how the data is shaped. On the text side the household line and the message share one continuous story while the date line sits alone, so the fields cannot be addressed uniformly. Both facts are properties of how a designer who is no longer reachable built a document two years ago, they are reported by nothing, and the conversion itself returns success either way.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it and care cannot substitute for it. Granularity is not a parameter, is not declared in the PDF, and has no read-ahead: the only route to the answer is to convert, export the document structure and look. A careful agent that plans the binding from the printed card plans a picture frame that does not exist. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the artwork came from the printer and that nobody knows how it was built, which is a client explaining why they have no working file, not a description of its internals. No asset note in the client's hands, no acceptance line and no earlier step says the photograph is baked in. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to re-plan the deliverable: one static hero shared by every household with variable text only, or a decision to escalate and ask whether the couple want the card rebuilt rather than merged, and either way a written statement to a client who believes their artwork can do something it cannot.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-plan the card as variable text against a single shared hero, drop the per-household image column from the data file so it does not silently bind nothing, re-author the mapping as ordered offset arithmetic inside the shared story with the standalone field handled separately, re-validate, re-prepare and re-verify the placeholders by round-tripping the document rather than trusting the success message, and put the structural limit in the note in plain language so the studio knows what their own artwork can and cannot do before they commission the next one.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A card run that reports success at every step and prints twelve identical cards where the couple expected each household's card to carry the picture, or worse, an image mapping that binds nothing and is never noticed because a photograph is present on every card anyway, so the failure is only discovered by the couple when the cards arrive.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the two constructs the leave-behind is actually built on. The studio's signature treatment is warm ink laid over the photograph, which is a compositing behaviour in the authored source, and the seal is a trace of a wax impression. What comes back is only visible in the returned per-canvas markup and the first canvas's rendition: the treatment is normalised to a plain opaque panel that covers the photograph rather than tinting it, so the hero is buried under a solid warm rectangle, and the traced seal arrives as loose ungrouped geometry with its own opaque ground riding along, so editable and usable turn out not to be the same claim. The export reports success with no warning of any kind, the sheet's structure is intact, and only looking at the rendition and reading the markup shows that the picture the whole sheet is built around is not visible.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it. The normalisation is a property of the importer, is not documented anywhere the agent can read at run time, and is not reported in the response; the only channel that carries the answer is the markup the export returns, which exists only after exporting. Nor can the agent design around an unknown: the treatment is the studio's stated house look and has to be attempted. (b) Nothing states it. The brief describes the tinted vellum treatment as the studio's own look and asks for the photograph to be visible in the finished file, which is a client describing what they want, not a warning about an importer. No asset note and no earlier step says the construct will not survive. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The fix crosses back to a different surface and produces a different asset: the treatment has to be baked into the raster hero by a tinting or overlay operation at a strength chosen by eye, which is an imaging decision with its own judgement, and the seal has to be re-prepared with its ground stripped and possibly re-traced. The source is then re-authored around a picture that already carries the look, which changes the sheet's composition as well.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Return to the imaging surface and bake the studio's treatment into the hero raster at a strength judged against the house look rather than relying on the authoring layer to composite it, re-prepare the seal so it arrives as clean transparent geometry, re-author the HTML around the pre-treated hero, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and verify again through both channels rather than assuming the second export took.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A leave-behind handed to three venues in which the A4 hero is a solid warm rectangle where the photograph should be and the seal is a smear of loose shapes on a white box, delivered as the studio's own signature look, with the export having reported success.

deliverables.name: Hartley wedding house pass: sixteen review renditions and six full-resolution keepers
deliverables.spec: All sixteen shortlisted frames carried through one stated house recipe to a single warm, natural, true-skin finish that holds across window light, late sun and coloured uplight when read in gallery order, delivered at review size, plus the six starred frames at full resolution with no interpolation anywhere and every tool-reported resize transcribed. Any frame that would not take the pass is pulled and named rather than forced. This is one pass with one recipe, not sixteen individual rescues and not one picture at several sizes.

deliverables.name: Hartley thank-you card run: press file plus per-household files
deliverables.spec: One card per household at the card's trim, household names printed exactly as the guests wrote them, file count equal to the reconciled household count, produced by reverse-engineering the printer's flat card into a live merge template with no working file supplied. Accompanied by one single-card file per household, named and identity verified by opening it, and by print-resolution proofs rendered from the merged document. The template and the record of what the client's artwork could and could not carry are part of the handover.

deliverables.name: Recovered Fernwell & Rowe seal
deliverables.spec: The studio's wax seal recovered from a photograph of an envelope as placeable, scalable vector geometry with a real viewBox and no opaque full-canvas ground path, delivered as a clean mark and a colour-accurate variant, holding legibly at the size the card's seal panel and the leave-behind reproduce it, including over the warm ink panel.

deliverables.name: Venue-partner leave-behind set as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: A single native editable Express document carrying an A4 sheet plus a square and a tall canvas, each keeping its own canvas size, with live editable text in one licensed type system, the seal as real vector shapes, and every photograph carried as embedded image data and visible in the finished file. The studio's tinted treatment must be present as it actually looks rather than as a panel over a hidden picture. Delivered with the self-contained source it was authored from, since the venue name and dates change with every pitch.

deliverables.name: House pass note and shared board
deliverables.spec: A written note stating the house recipe as a recipe the studio can be held to for the season, naming every frame that needed something outside it and why in one line, the type system by role with foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight, the data rows questioned and how they were resolved, anything the client's own card artwork structurally could not do, and every resize any tool reported. Paired with a persistent shareable board carrying the finished set for the two photographers and their two coordinators to brief from, with nothing silently dropped.

verifiers_auto.text: The card run produces exactly one page per reconciled household row.
verifiers_auto.how: Count pages of the merged press file and per-household files against the delivered merge data file.

verifiers_auto.text: Proofs render at real print resolution at card trim.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the rendered proof's pixel dimensions against the card trim and the requested resolution.

verifiers_auto.text: No delivered file exceeds its source pixel dimensions and no crop reports an upscale entry.
verifiers_auto.how: Compare delivered dimensions with named sources and scan the run for tradeoffs entries of type upscaled.

verifiers_auto.text: The prepared template contains a placeholder for every variable field.
verifiers_auto.how: Round-trip IDML from the prepared template and grep the stories for each expected token.

verifiers_auto.text: The seal carries a viewBox and no full-canvas opaque background path.
verifiers_auto.how: Inspect the delivered SVG source.

verifiers_auto.text: Every photograph in the exported document resolved to real image data on all three canvases.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse the returned per-canvas markup for image elements carrying the importer's placeholder.

verifiers_auto.text: The three canvases each keep their own declared size in one document.
verifiers_auto.how: Read per-canvas width and height in the export response against the three declared sizes.

verifiers_auto.text: Text elements carry the licensed faces rather than the importer's default sans.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse resolved font-family values in the returned markup.

verifiers_auto.text: The board carries the full finished set with no failed placements.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the board response for added entity count and an empty failed-items list.

verifiers_auto.text: The sixteen review renditions and the six keepers are two distinct products from the same masters, not one set resaved.
verifiers_auto.how: Compare dimensions and file inventory of the two sets against the stated recipe and source frames.

verifiers_human.text: The sixteen read as one day in gallery order with no frame or block jumping against its neighbours.
verifiers_human.how: View the run in gallery order end to end rather than frame by frame.

verifiers_human.text: Skin is true across all three lighting situations, with nothing orange, plum or plastic.
verifiers_human.how: Inspect faces across the ceremony, portrait and reception blocks side by side.

verifiers_human.text: The note states a real recipe that could be applied to nine hundred frames, with exceptions named.
verifiers_human.how: Read the note and check it against what was actually applied in the run.

verifiers_human.text: The leave-behind carries the studio's treatment with the photograph visible and working.
verifiers_human.how: View the first canvas rendition and judge the treatment against the studio's description.

verifiers_human.text: The seal reads as the studio's seal at card and sheet reproduction size, including over the ink panel.
verifiers_human.how: View the rendered card proof at trim and the sheet at its canvas size.

verifiers_human.text: No card shows a household name or message clipped at trim, on any record.
verifiers_human.how: Read all cards on the proofs at trim against the guest list.

verifiers_human.text: The package reads as warm honest country-house work rather than a filtered package or a glossy luxury one.
verifiers_human.how: Judge the gallery, the card and the leave-behind together against the stated band.

decision_gates: The surface split: card run to the merge surface, leave-behind to HTML authoring, gallery to imaging.
How many treatment groups the day actually has, judged by looking at illuminants rather than by accepting the client's three-part description of their day.
Whether to deliver a recipe or sixteen rescues. The better-looking sixteen is the wrong deliverable if it cannot be repeated across nine hundred frames.
Which named preset to build the house pass on, given that the catalogue gives names and the tool works whole-frame with no mask.
What to do with the two frames that came off a different body and start somewhere else.
The duplicate households: whether merging two near-identical rows is the agent's call or the couple's, when the client has forbidden tidying the names.
Whether to trust the mapping readout of the client's text or reconstruct the story from the document.
Whether a success message counts as verification of the prepared template.
What to tell a client whose own artwork structurally cannot do the thing they assumed it could, and when to tell them.
Selection wording on the wax seal, where naming the envelope takes the envelope and naming the wax's own properties takes the wax, and which preparation gets the counters open at reproduction size.
Whether the studio's treatment is composited in the authored source or baked into the raster, and at what strength.
Whether the licensed winter frame joins the studio's own photography or reads as bought.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a warm country-house band rather than a luxury one.
How much air the A4 sheet carries. At this band restraint reads as confidence and a busy sheet reads as a cheaper studio.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a pretty wedding picture. IDENTITY: these are the Hartley wedding, this couple, these guests and this studio's own wax seal, and the deliverable is those exact frames finished, not new frames invented. A regenerated face on a thank-you card is the single worst possible failure in this vertical. SPEC: the studio needs one card per household with names printed exactly as the guests wrote them, per-household files named and verified, print-resolution proofs, and full-resolution keepers with no invented pixels. None of that is checkable against a generated image. EDITABILITY AND REPEATABILITY: the actual product being bought is a recipe the studio can be held to across nine hundred frames next month, plus a merge template and an editable document they change per venue pitch. A one-shot render is not a recipe, cannot be applied to a set it has never seen, and gives the studio nothing to hold anyone to. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: does this pass hold in gallery order, does this artwork actually expose a picture frame, does this record clip at trim, does this trace still read at seal size, does the treatment survive the import. None of that is a generation problem.
doability_proof: Five surfaces, honestly counted, every link verified in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account). IMAGING: image_list_presets and image_apply_preset are live, and the doc records explicitly that image_apply_preset accepts no mask and is single-image whole-frame, which is what makes the recipe question real rather than decorative. Masked and unmasked image_apply_adjustments, select_by_prompt, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs array, monochromatic tint and colour overlay, and vectorize are all verified headless; colour overlay takes no mask and no opacity and the doc points at fill_area for percentage work, which is exactly the constraint the baked treatment has to be designed around. Vectorize takes no options at all, emits no viewBox and always emits an opaque first path, all verified, which is the hygiene the seal deliverable gates on. crop_and_resize interpolates to a hard cap and signals it only in tradeoffs, so the no-invented-pixels bar is scored as a decision plus a disclosure rather than a measurement. MERGE: convert_pdf_to_indd to export_idml to generate_indd_mapping_prompt to prepare_indd_merge_template is verified end to end from a bare press PDF, and the card PDF is specified as a real font-embedding press PDF because thin synthetic PDFs fail conversion opaquely. The baked-photograph case is grounded in the verified observation that a converted PDF exposes graphic frames only when the source PDF actually places images, and that a continuous flow can collapse to a single mappable text frame; the trajectory reads the inventory before promising any binding and degrades gracefully whichever way it lands. One record per page for PDF output is confirmed, per-record files come from the two order-safe routes, multi-record raster order is documented as reversed and is avoided, and 300 ppi comes from document_render_layout because resolution asked for at merge time is silently ignored. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, external image URLs render as empty placeholders so every photograph is embedded, and the HTML is routed through the text/html upload path because embedded photography exceeds the inline threshold. The importer's silent normalisations are documented findings (mix-blend-mode dropped, filter dropped, multi-layer shadows truncated to the first, every drop returning success with no warning), and the rendition preview shows the first canvas only, so canvases two and three are audited from the returned markup. Persistence is not assumed, so the deliverable is the editable document plus the source. FONTS: the recommend, styles, find, kit chain is verified end to end, with the non-standard numeric weights, the slug-not-PostScript rule and the all-or-nothing kit call all leaned on. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation filter never passed, licensing returns camera-scale imagery, boards persist with a twelve-placement cap where 201 means partial success. VOLUME: eighteen client image files in, roughly thirty-four image artefacts moved in total, every multi-image call at or under ten and no batch above twenty. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no bleed gate, no pdfPreset, no fill_text, no animate_design, no replace_image, no download_design, no upscaling, no OCR, no compositing, no generated imagery, and no photograph reaching Express as a URL.

engagement_title: Cascadia Founders Summit: eighteen self-submitted portraits brought to one credible house treatment, cut to the crops the programme and the stage need, bound into the venue printer's badge artwork as a live run, and carried into the programme and announcement set
vertical: Party, events and promotion: a paid professional founders summit in Portland, Oregon, with delegate passes at 600 to 1,200 dollars and an audience of founders, operators and institutional investors
real_brief_anchor: Two ledger anchors, both Freelancer.com. The first, 'Traditional Corporate Headshot Session Needed', whose grounding_note describes 'classic/formal corporate head-shots, neutral light-grey backdrop, colour + clean black-and-white versions, deliverables for social-profile/company website/print, one-week turnaround'. The second, a corporate-website retouch open call quoted verbatim in its grounding_note: 'professionally enhance a complete set of images for our corporate website', 'correct lighting imbalances and exposure issues', 'create a consistent visual style across all website images', 'showcase our facilities, operations, equipment and people', 'maintain a natural and realistic appearance'. Absorbs AO-104 and AO-20. The rebuild is needed because both absorbed tasks sat on a single surface and both ended in a set of crops, which is one deliverable, not four. The fuller commission an events client of this shape actually posts is the one here: the portraits are only useful once they are bound into the badge run the venue printer will actually print and into the programme and announcement collateral, and it is in the binding that a badly prepared crop stops being invisible. All names in the legacy grounding notes are discarded and replaced: the summit, its fourteen speakers and its four staff are invented and Western or European throughout (Marguerite Halloran, Peter Vance, Ines Moreau, Anders Lindqvist, Colm Byrne, Dana Whitfield, Estelle Rioux, Grant Mackey, Sofia Bellini, Nils Haugen, Robin Tate, Bernadette Cruz, Hugo Almeida, Karin Voss, plus staff Laurel Beckett, Owen Faraday, Mireille Dufort and Jonah Pryce).
client_one_liner: Every speaker sent a headshot taken somewhere different, our own team's photos are worse, and the badges have to be at the printer in nine days.
client_brief:
Cascadia Founders Summit, Portland, second edition.

We run a two-day summit for founders and the people who fund them. Passes are six hundred to twelve hundred dollars and the room is about four hundred people. We are nine days from the badge deadline and we have a problem with pictures.

We have fourteen speakers and four of our own team. Every speaker sent whatever headshot they had. One is from a magazine shoot, two came from their PR agency and look it, several were taken in an office with whatever light was in the room, and a couple are cropped so tightly you can barely get a square out of them. Our own four are worse. Put them next to each other and it looks like eighteen different events.

What we need is for all eighteen to look like they belong to the same summit. Understated and credible, the way a serious professional event looks. Not glamour retouching, not that flat direct-flash look, and please do not make anyone look like a different person. Our audience pays to be in the room and they read the calibre of the event off things like this.

We need the pictures at the shapes we actually use: the portrait shape that runs in the printed programme, a tight square for badges and avatars, and a wide one for the lower third of the stage screens. Each person needs to sit on our house ground rather than whatever room they were photographed in, and for the stage screens we need them without any ground at all so our AV team can drop them over the session video.

The badges are the urgent piece. Our venue printer ran our badges last year and we are using the same artwork, but we only have the file they sent us, not whatever it was made from. Each badge carries the person's name, their role line and their affiliation, plus their picture. The speaker list is attached the way our registration system exported it. The role lines are how the speakers wrote them and how their contracts say they print, so they go on as written.

We build our own website, so we do not need pages. What we do need is the printed programme's opening page, a title slide the stage team can restyle per session, and a square announcement we post when each speaker is confirmed. Those three in one file we can edit ourselves, please, because we confirm speakers weekly.

One more thing. The venue has not opened yet so nobody has a photograph of it. We have the architect's render but it looks like a render. If you think the programme opener needs a real picture, get one.

What we need back: the eighteen at all three shapes plus the no-ground versions, the badges ready for the printer and one file per person named so registration can reprint a single badge without opening it, the three canvases as one editable file with its source, a board our team can review from, and a note on what you did to each portrait and what type we are now using.
price_band_and_audience: Delegate passes 600 to 1,200 dollars, two days, roughly four hundred attendees, speakers who are founders, operators and institutional investors, audience aged 28 to 55 who expense the ticket. The band is load-bearing. At this level the portraiture has to be understated, even and credible: neutral house ground, natural skin, no visible retouching signature, one consistent scale of head in frame across eighteen people so the programme grid reads as one event. Push it toward glamour retouching, smoothed skin, bright eyes and a warm glossy finish, and it reads as a consumer conference selling to the wrong buyer. Leave it flat and hard-lit and it reads as a free meetup. The programme and the announcement set follow the same rule: generous white space, restrained type, one strong photograph, and the summit's mark used quietly. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every crop is dimensionally correct. A posted job of this shape runs 1,500 to 3,000 dollars fixed on a nine-day turnaround.

assets_supplied.name: speaker_portraits/ (14 files) and staff_portraits/ (4 files)
assets_supplied.kind: image
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everything we were sent. Fourteen speakers, four of our own team. Different rooms, different light, different everything." Mixed dimensions from roughly 1,100px to 5,600px on the long edge, all head-and-shoulders, Western and European sitters, no two grounds alike.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two things nobody at the summit can see. First, three of the fourteen speaker frames are cropped so tightly at the top that the wide stage-screen shape cannot be derived from them without either clipping the crown of the head or inventing pixels, and the crop tool answers that with a tradeoff rather than a refusal and will interpolate toward its cap while reporting it only in a metadata entry. The only route that does not invent pixels is to add material at the edges first, and whether the added band actually matches that sitter's own ground and the house treatment is a property of that frame that cannot be known before it is done. Second, two of the frames arrived already heavily retouched by an agency, with skin smoothed and eyes lifted, so bringing them to the house treatment makes them read plastic beside the sixteen untouched ones rather than bringing them into line.

assets_supplied.name: summit_badge_2025_PRINTER.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: document
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The badge artwork our venue printer ran last year. We only have what they sent us." A real press PDF at 100 x 70 mm portrait, fonts embedded, produced from a genuine page layout. Carries the name, the role line, the affiliation, the summit mark and the person's picture.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The printed badge reads as a square picture chip, but the graphic frame behind it is a tall portrait rectangle at roughly three to four, and the frame fits whatever is bound into it on its own terms. A square badge crop bound into it is fitted to the frame's proportion and the crown of the head is cut on every single record, silently, with the merge reporting success and every badge looking deliberate in isolation. The frame's proportion is geometry inherited from a printer nobody at the summit can ask. On the text side the name and the role line share one continuous story while the affiliation sits alone, so the fields cannot be addressed uniformly.

assets_supplied.name: speakers.csv
assets_supplied.kind: data
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The speaker list as our registration system exported it. Role lines print as written, that is in the contracts." Columns for name, role line, affiliation, session and a photo filename.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Twenty rows for eighteen people: two speakers registered twice, once through the speaker portal and once through the general registration, with different affiliations on each row. Headers are mixed-case with trailing spaces and the photo column is a plain header holding bare filenames, which does not satisfy the merge image-column contract, so a naive run binds nothing while every badge still shows a picture. And the longest role line runs to more than sixty characters where the median is under thirty, which oversets the badge's fixed role frame at true trim while every other record sits comfortably. Nothing anywhere reports overset.

assets_supplied.name: venue_render.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: image
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The architect's render of the new venue. It is all anyone has because the building has not opened."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a CGI render with a synthetic sky and impossible interior light, and it will never sit beside photographic portraits on the same page, which is only obvious once the two are actually adjacent. It is also 1,400px on the long edge, so it could not carry a programme opener even if it belonged there.

assets_supplied.name: summit_brand_notes.txt
assets_supplied.kind: document
assets_supplied.visible_description: The summit's house ground description in plain language, the tone words (understated, credible, quiet, professional), the three shapes actually used, and the standing rule that speaker role lines print as contracted.

assets_supplied.name: programme_copy.txt
assets_supplied.kind: document
assets_supplied.visible_description: The programme opener copy, the session track names and the announcement wording the summit posts when a speaker is confirmed.

acceptance_bar: The eighteen read as one event when laid out in the programme grid: one house ground, one treatment, one scale of head in frame. A portrait that cannot be brought to the set is named to us, not shipped at eighty percent.
Nobody is made to look like a different person, and no portrait carries a visible retouching signature. Anything that arrived already heavily worked is named in the note with what you did about it.
All three shapes are delivered for every person, plus a no-ground version for the stage screens whose edge holds when placed over dark video and not only over white.
No invented pixels anywhere. No delivered file exceeds its source, no crop reports an upscale, and where material had to be added at an edge the note says which portraits and why.
Where material was added at an edge, the added band matches that portrait's own ground and the house treatment, judged with the wide shapes laid out together rather than one at a time.
The badge run produces exactly one badge per confirmed person, with the picture on each badge being that person's picture and the head sitting in the frame the way it does on every other badge.
Every field is present on every badge, and no name, role line or affiliation is clipped at true trim. Any badge you cannot give us that way, name it before the file goes to the printer.
Role lines print exactly as the speakers wrote them, not shortened, re-spaced or abbreviated.
Each per-person badge file contains the person its filename claims, established by opening it.
Printer proofs render at real print resolution at badge trim.
All three canvases sit in ONE editable file, each keeping its own canvas size, and we get the self-contained source it was built from.
Any diagram on the programme opener is real editable artwork in that file, not a picture of a diagram.
One type system across all three canvases, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the weight actually used.
The board carries every finished portrait with nothing silently missing from it.
The note states, per portrait, what you did to it, and lists every row in the speaker export you questioned and what was done about it.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and split the commission: badges to the merge surface, the three canvases to HTML authoring, portraits to imaging.
trajectory.judgement: The brief does not state the split, and it explicitly rules out web pages, which is a constraint on scope rather than on surface. Badges are record per page against artwork the summit wants kept; the three canvases need three sizes and weekly edits.
trajectory.produces: A plan naming deliverable to surface, and the confirmed tier.

trajectory.action: Upload all eighteen portraits, the badge PDF, the export and the render, holding a role manifest.
trajectory.judgement: Handoff discipline. Source dimensions are recorded here because they are the reference every no-upscale claim is made against later.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs with source dimensions per portrait.

trajectory.action: Preview all eighteen and triage: light, ground, tilt, how much room there is above the head, how large the head sits in frame, and which frames arrived already worked on.
trajectory.judgement: Three things have to be decided by looking, not by reading a filename: which frames are too tight for the wide shape before any crop policy is fixed, which frames arrived retouched and therefore need a different destination from the rest, and what one scale of head in frame means across sitters photographed at wildly different distances.
trajectory.produces: A per-portrait triage note and the house treatment target chosen from the strongest frame.

trajectory.action: Straighten what needs it, then correct every portrait toward the house treatment one call per frame, recording parameters.
trajectory.judgement: A batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong across eighteen rooms. The target is a set, and the two already-retouched frames need a decision rather than a correction: pushing them toward the house treatment is the move that makes them worse.
trajectory.produces: Eighteen corrected masters with a per-portrait parameter log and a stated decision on the retouched pair.

trajectory.action: Put every sitter on the summit's house ground, triaging the route per portrait, and produce the ground-free versions for the stage screens.
trajectory.judgement: The one-call ground route and the select-invert-fill route are not interchangeable and the choice is per portrait. Hair against a busy or similar-valued room is where the difference shows, and it shows on dark video rather than on the house ground.
trajectory.produces: House-ground portraits and ground-free portraits for all eighteen.

trajectory.action: Derive the programme shape, the tight square and the wide stage shape for every person, reading each crop's confidence and tradeoff metadata rather than trusting success.
trajectory.judgement: The tradeoffs array is the only signal that a crop clipped, that detection was weak, or that an output was interpolated, and a subject-aware crop on a sparse frame can mis-detect and still report success.
trajectory.produces: Three shapes per person, with a resize and confidence record.

trajectory.action: On the frames too tight for the wide shape, add material at the short edges first and then crop, bringing the added band into the house treatment.
trajectory.judgement: Adding edge material is the only route that does not invent pixels inside the picture, but it introduces synthesised ground that has to match that sitter's own ground and the house treatment, and it is the single sanctioned generative call so it must not be reached for casually.
trajectory.produces: Wide-shape masters for the tight frames without interpolation.

trajectory.action: Lay all eighteen wide shapes out together and look at them as the stage set they will be.
trajectory.judgement: Judging the set as a set at the only moment the comparison exists. Grounds and treatments that agree in isolation can disagree in a row.
trajectory.produces: A set-level verdict on the wide shapes.

trajectory.surface: Data preparation and Creative Cloud storage
trajectory.action: Reconcile the registration export against the confirmed eighteen, normalise headers, build the prefixed image column holding bare filenames, upload the badge-shape portraits and build the image map against them.
trajectory.judgement: Two people appear twice with different affiliations, and choosing which affiliation prints is a decision about somebody's professional identity, not a data-cleaning detail. The image column contract is specific and a plain header binds nothing while every badge still shows a picture.
trajectory.produces: The merge data file, uploaded badge portraits, the image map, and a first list of data questions.

trajectory.action: Convert the badge PDF, export IDML, unzip it, and read the real inventory: frame counts, bounds, object styles, integer page-item ids, and the true story text reconstructed from the content runs.
trajectory.judgement: The binding strategy belongs to the printer's artwork rather than to the plan, and the agent has to establish what is addressable, and at what proportion, before promising anything. It also has to decide which text it computes offsets from.
trajectory.produces: The converted document, its IDML, a real frame inventory with bounds, and a reconstructed story text.

trajectory.action: Author the mapping covering the name, role line, affiliation and the picture frame, and pass it back through the validator.
trajectory.judgement: Choosing the right action for the granularity that came back, using integer page-item ids, ordering same-story rows against the original text, and passing the whole mapping as one stringified object.
trajectory.produces: A validated mapping.

trajectory.action: Prepare the merge template, then round-trip IDML from the result and grep for every placeholder the mapping claimed to create.
trajectory.judgement: A success message is not evidence, and nothing in the chain instructs this check.
trajectory.produces: A template whose placeholder inventory has been independently confirmed.

trajectory.action: Merge to a native document with the per-row portraits bound, render the print-resolution proofs, and look at the proofs.
trajectory.judgement: Merging to the native document first keeps the press branch and the per-record branch open and is the only route to real resolution. Looking at what came out, rather than at the success message, is the whole point of this step.
trajectory.produces: The merged document and the first print-resolution proofs, inspected.

trajectory.action: Produce the press file and the per-person badge files by the route whose record identity is guaranteed, naming each by opening it.
trajectory.judgement: Returned order is not trustworthy on every route, and naming eighteen files by position ends with registration reprinting the wrong person's badge.
trajectory.produces: The press badge file and eighteen per-person files, named and identity verified.

trajectory.action: Read every badge at true trim against the speaker export, field by field.
trajectory.judgement: Reading the output rather than the log. Clipped copy is reported nowhere and does not read as clipped at proof scale.
trajectory.produces: A badge by badge reconciliation against the export.

trajectory.action: Search Stock with short generic queries for a real photograph for the programme opener, filter to photography, exclude generative results, license and download at full resolution, then bring it toward the house treatment and lay it beside the portraits.
trajectory.judgement: The architect's render is the obvious free answer and it is the wrong one, which is a judgement about how a render sits beside photography rather than about the render's quality. The licensed frame then has to sit with eighteen portraits rather than merely be good.
trajectory.produces: One licensed camera-scale frame, graded and judged against the set.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, read the family style inventories for real numeric weights, launder every name, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own and has to read as a serious professional summit. Weight cannot be inferred from the style name and the CSS must use the returned stack.
trajectory.produces: A one-kit type system with family, foundry or designer and real weight per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self-contained HTML with three roots at three canvas sizes, embedding every photograph as image data, authoring the session track diagram as inline vector inside an explicitly sized wrapper, and declaring family and weight on every text element. Upload and export, then verify the first canvas by rendition and the other two by parsing the returned markup.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto-sized right-anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, weight is not inherited from markup semantics, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed-size set. Every one of those drops returns success, and the rendition only shows the first canvas.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document with three canvases, the retained source, an inspected first canvas and a markup audit of the other two.

trajectory.action: Create the review board and add the finished portraits, batching within the per-call cap and re-sending only entries named as failed. Then write the note.
trajectory.judgement: What to escalate and what to fix silently. The summit asked to be told about the portraits and the data, and the note also has to say plainly that badge typography is the printer's and not the agent's, because the summit will otherwise assume the type system covers it.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: That the badge's picture frame is not the shape the printed badge implies, and that everything bound into it is being re-fitted on the frame's terms. The 2025 badge reads as a square picture chip, so a square badge crop is the reasonable thing to prepare, and the summit's own brief asks for a tight square. The graphic frame behind it is a tall portrait rectangle, and the merge fits whatever is bound into it to that proportion, so the crown of the head is cut on every record. The frame's proportion is geometry inherited from a printer nobody at the summit can ask, it is not visible in the printed artefact, the merge reports success, and each badge looks like a deliberate tight crop when viewed alone. It only declares itself as a fault when the rendered proofs are actually looked at and the same cut appears on all eighteen heads.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it and care cannot substitute for it. The frame's proportion is not stated in the PDF, is not visible in the printed card, and is not reported by the merge; the only way to it is to convert, read the frame bounds and then bind something and look at what came out. An agent that reads the bounds carefully before binding can catch it one step earlier, which is exactly the competent path this trajectory takes at step 10, and it still cannot know whether the frame fits or fills what is bound into it until a record is actually rendered. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for a tight square for badges and avatars, which is the summit describing the shape they use, and the acceptance bar asks that heads sit in the frame the same way on every badge, which is an ordinary client quality requirement. Neither is a disclosure about the artwork's internals. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to go back to the imaging surface and prepare a different asset: a badge crop at the frame's real proportion with the head placed for that proportion, which is a fresh composition decision per sitter, not the same crop re-fed. The square crop the summit asked for still ships as an avatar deliverable, so the two now diverge.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-derive a badge-specific crop at the picture frame's real proportion for all eighteen, composed for that shape rather than cropped down from the square, re-upload them and rebuild the image map against the new filenames, re-merge and re-render, then read the proofs again on all eighteen rather than on the ones that were changed. Keep the square crop as the avatar deliverable and say in the note that badge and avatar are now two different crops and why, so the summit does not later swap one for the other.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Eighteen badges go to the printer with the top of every speaker's head cut off, on a run that reported success at every step and looked deliberate on any single badge, for an event whose paying audience reads calibre off exactly this.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the material added at the edges of the three too-tight frames actually belongs to those pictures. Adding edge material is the only route to the wide stage shape that does not invent pixels inside the picture, but what gets built at the edge is generated from that specific frame's own content: on one sitter it continues the office wall convincingly, on another it invents a lighting falloff that does not match the sitter's own ground, and on a third it produces a band that is plausible in isolation and a full step off the house treatment. None of that is knowable before the operation is run, nothing in the response reports it, and each result looks like a normal photograph on its own. It shows only when the eighteen wide shapes are laid out together as the stage set, where three of them carry a band along one edge that the other fifteen do not.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it. The expand has to happen after the house treatment is established, since the band has to match that treatment, and it has to happen before the wide crops are final. There is no parameter that guarantees a match and no readout that reports one; the seed parameter makes a result reproducible, not correct. A careful agent doing it right the first time is still handing an outcome to a generative step whose output it has not seen. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says a couple of frames are cropped tightly, which is the client noticing that some pictures are tight, and the acceptance bar requires added material to match, which is the client's standard for the work rather than a warning that it will not. No asset note names which frames or what the band will do. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is a different decision on a different axis: re-run the expand with different amounts or from a different side, correct the band as its own masked region, or abandon expansion for that sitter and accept a looser wide crop that loses the head scale the set is built on, which then changes what one scale of head in frame means for the whole set.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-run the edge material on the frames whose band does not sit, from a different side or at a different extent, and bring the band into the house treatment as a confined correction rather than re-grading the whole frame, which would move the sitter. Where it will not come, choose the looser crop and re-check what that does to the head scale across all eighteen wide shapes, then lay the eighteen out and judge them together again rather than checking only the three that were touched.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Three of eighteen lower thirds carry a visible band of invented wall along one edge in a different light from the rest, projected at stage scale in front of four hundred people who paid to be there.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether every badge actually holds at true trim. The role lines are the speakers' own contracted titles, supplied by a registration system, and the longest of them is more than twice the median. The role frame's depth is fixed inside a printer's artwork that nobody at the summit can change and that the connector offers no way to resize, reflow or releaded. The two only meet on a typeset badge at real trim size. The failure is silent in every channel: nothing in the merge reports overset, the merge's own raster route renders at screen resolution where a clip does not read as a clip, and the badge looks finished at proof scale.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Neither ordering nor competence produces a fit. The agent cannot shorten the role line, because the summit has said it prints as contracted, and it cannot deepen or reflow the frame, because the mapping surface exposes only text, image and code mappings and no typographic or geometric control whatsoever. Both the constraint and the frame are fixed client property. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says role lines print as written, which is a standard contractual copy clause of the same kind the client already applies to their speakers, and the acceptance bar carries an ordinary quality line about nothing being clipped at trim. Neither says any record is long, and no asset note names the speaker. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the input the agent would want to change is the one it is forbidden to touch and the artefact it would want to alter cannot be altered. The checkpoint resolves into a judgement that has to be taken and then made consistent with the earlier decision about the duplicate registrations: either this is a freelancer who quietly edits a client's contractual copy, or one who names in writing what cannot be done inside the client's own artwork.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-render the affected record alone at true trim to confirm the clip is real rather than a proof artefact, then read all eighteen at trim rather than only the flagged one. Go back to the duplicate-registration decision and make the two consistent: name the over-length role line and the frame it will not fit, name the rows merged and the affiliation chosen and on whose authority, and put both to the client as questions with no copy shortened in either case. State whether the affected badge ships as it stands or is held, and carry the same decision into that person's single badge file.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A speaker who negotiated their title into a contract wears a badge for two days with it cut off mid-word, in front of the investors the summit sold the room to, discovered at the registration desk rather than before the file went to the printer.

deliverables.name: Cascadia Founders Summit portrait set, eighteen people at one house treatment

One set with one treatment, not eighteen separately optimised pictures and not one picture at three sizes.

decision_gates: The surface split, and reading the client's no-website instruction as a scope limit rather than as a limit on which surfaces may be used.
What one scale of head in frame means across sitters photographed at different distances, and holding it across eighteen files.
What to do with the two frames that arrived already heavily retouched, where the house correction makes them worse rather than better.
Ground route per portrait rather than per set, and on which ground the ground-free edges are judged.
Whether to interpolate a tight frame or add material at its edges, and whether the added material can be brought into the house treatment or the crop has to loosen instead.
The duplicate registrations: which affiliation prints, and whether that is the agent's call or the summit's to confirm.
Whether to trust the mapping readout of the client's text or reconstruct the story from the document.
Whether a success message counts as verification of the prepared template.
Reading the picture frame's real proportion before promising a crop shape, and what to do when the shape the client asked for and the shape the frame takes are not the same.
How to honour contractual role lines when one will not fit a frame the connector gives no way to change.
Whether to name eighteen per-record files by returned order or by opening each one.
Whether an architect's render can sit beside photographic portraits, and if not, what a real photograph has to look like to join them.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a paid professional summit, and saying plainly that it cannot reach the printer's badge.
How much restraint the programme opener carries. At this band quiet reads as calibre and busy reads as a cheaper event.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns eighteen new faces. IDENTITY is the whole point and the whole prohibition: these are eighteen real speakers whose actual likeness has to survive, and the client says explicitly that nobody may be made to look like a different person. A regenerated headshot on a conference badge is not a design failure, it is a fraud. SPEC: the summit needs one badge per confirmed person at badge trim with contractual role lines bound verbatim, each person's own picture bound per row, eighteen separately named badge files each containing the person its filename claims, print-resolution proofs, and three named crop shapes plus a ground-free version per person. None of that is producible or checkable from a generated image. EDITABILITY: two deliverables are defined by being editable, a live merge template so next year's badges are a data change, and a document the summit restyles weekly as speakers confirm. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: does this frame fit or fill what is bound into it, does this added band match this sitter's ground, does this role line clip at trim, does this edge hold over dark video. None of that is a generation problem.
doability_proof: Five surfaces, honestly counted, every link verified in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account). MERGE: the convert, export, generate, prepare, merge, render chain is verified end to end from a bare press PDF, and the badge PDF is specified as a real font-embedding press PDF because thin synthetic PDFs fail conversion opaquely. Per-row image binding is verified visually through a prefixed CSV column plus an image map whose keys match the bare filenames, at three rows, so the eighteen-row run carries an explicit fallback of a recordRange loop binding one image per call, which also guarantees per-record identity. PDF-derived templates are confirmed to contain real image frames when the source PDF places images, and the mapping prompt returns frame bounds, which is the channel the frame-proportion question is answered through. One record per page for PDF output is confirmed, per-record files come from the two order-safe routes, multi-record raster order is documented as reversed and avoided, and 300 ppi comes from document_render_layout because resolution asked for at merge time is silently ignored. The mapping surface exposes only text, image and code mappings with no typographic or geometric control, which is what makes the overset constraint real rather than rhetorical. IMAGING: auto_straighten, auto_tone, masked and unmasked adjustments, select_by_prompt and select_subject with returnBbox, invert_selection, fill_area, remove_background in both transparent and backgroundColor forms, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and detection-confidence metadata, and generative_expand are all verified headless. generative_expand is the single sanctioned generative call and is documented as adding pixels only at the edges with AI-generated content and an optional seed, which is exactly how it is used here. crop_and_resize is documented as interpolating to a hard cap and reporting it only in tradeoffs, and subject-aware extraction is documented as silently mis-cropping on sparse art with a low confidence value, so both are scored as decision plus disclosure rather than measurement. Alpha survives crops at png output, which is what the ground-free deliverable depends on. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector so the track diagram is a real deliverable, external image URLs render as empty placeholders so every photograph is embedded, and the HTML is routed through the text/html upload path because embedded photography exceeds the inline threshold. The rendition preview shows the first canvas only, so canvases two and three are audited from the returned markup. Persistence is not assumed, so the deliverable is the document plus the source. FONTS: the recommend, styles, find, kit chain is verified end to end, and the documented absence of any font file download is why the note must state that badge typography stays the printer's. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation filter never passed, licensing returns camera-scale imagery, boards persist with a twelve-placement cap where 201 means partial success with a failed-items list, so the eighteen-portrait board is sent in two batches. VOLUME: twenty client image files in, roughly forty-eight image artefacts moved in total across three shapes plus ground-free versions, every multi-image call at or under ten and no batch above twenty. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no bleed gate, no pdfPreset, no fill_text, no animate_design, no replace_image, no download_design, no upscaling, no OCR, no compositing, no generated faces, and no photograph reaching Express as a URL.

engagement_title: Astrid Vellacourt founder brand kit: one look across nine session frames, a monogram recovered from a blind-debossed card, cut-outs that hold on the deep ground, and the speaker and announcement canvases handed back editable
vertical: Personal branding for a founder: the co-founder and managing director of a six-person industrial design studio, raising a seed round and speaking on a European conference circuit
real_brief_anchor: Ledger anchor for PHOTO-20 (Freelancer.com, reference null). Its grounding_note, quoted as far as the ledger carries it: 'Adapted from a real Freelancer.com creative-headshot brief (a founder wanting a creative and dynamic headshot for my professional business profile, shot in a studio with studio lighting and creative and dynamic compositions). The live studio shoot itself is out of connector scope, so the task is faithfully scoped to the POST-PRODUCTION + personal-brand delivery a creative-headshot retoucher hands over once the raw studio frames exist. The client is laundered to a FICTIONAL unnamed founder with a generic two-letter personal monogram (AV); no real person, company, product, platform or trademark is named.' Absorbs AO-21. The rebuild is needed because the ledger concept ended in a set of crops of one sitter, which is one deliverable rather than four, and sat on one surface. The fuller commission a founder on a raise actually buys is the one here: the session frames finished to one look, the cut-outs that have to hold on the deep ground her deck and press kit use, her monogram recovered from the only artefact that carries it, and the speaker and announcement canvases she edits herself between events. The founder is named Astrid Vellacourt, the studio is Vellacourt & Sund, and no real person, firm or platform is referenced.
client_one_liner: I got a mix of frames out of a half-day session and they do not match, my monogram only exists as a blind deboss on an old card, and I need one look that works everywhere from a tiny profile picture to a conference banner.
client_brief:
I co-founded and run a six-person industrial design studio. We are raising a seed round and I am speaking at three conferences between February and May, so this is the season my picture is in front of people who do not know me yet.

I had a half-day session with a photographer and I have nine frames I like. They do not match. The light moved during the afternoon, some are warmer, one is much cooler than the rest, and put together they look like three different sittings. I want one look across all of them. Composed, credible, understated. I am asking people for money and asking conferences for stage time, so it should look like someone who runs a company, not someone who runs an account. No heavy filter, nothing that looks like a preset, and please do not smooth me into somebody else.

Here is what I actually need the pictures for. A profile picture, which is the smallest place any of this appears and where I care most. A press headshot I send to conference organisers. A wide banner for my profile pages. And a speaker photo for the programmes, which those organisers always ask for on a plain background so they can put it on their own colour.

That plain background is the thing I keep failing to solve myself. The session was shot on grey paper and I do not want grey. I want a warm neutral behind me. And for the press kit and my deck I need a version with nothing behind me at all, because both of those sit on a very dark ground and every version I have tried has a pale outline round my hair on it.

My monogram. When we started the studio we had cards made with the two letters pressed into the paper with no ink, just the impression. I love it and it is the only version that exists. I do not have a file and the printer that made them has closed. I want it back as artwork I can use, and it has to survive on a profile picture, which is where it is smallest, and reversed on the dark ground, which is where it is hardest.

The last piece is a speaker one-pager for the conferences, a wide banner canvas and a square announcement I post when a talk is confirmed. Those three in one file I can edit myself, because the event name and the date change every time and I am not paying for this four times.

One more thing. The banner wants something with more room than a studio frame, my studio or a workshop, and we have nothing usable. If that is what it needs, source one and bill me for it.

What I need back: the nine finished, all four crops, the version on the warm neutral and the version with nothing behind me, my monogram as artwork with a note on where it will and will not hold, the three canvases as one editable file plus whatever it was built from, a board I can send my co-founder, and a note on what you did.
price_band_and_audience: Founder personal-brand package. The client is 30 to 50, raising a seed round at institutional level and pitching a European speaking circuit, and her audience is investors, conference programme committees and prospective senior hires. The band is load-bearing on every decision. At this level the look is composed, credible and understated: neutral warm ground, natural skin, restrained contrast, one consistent framing logic, and the monogram used quietly rather than as a badge. An over-filtered influencer treatment, high clarity, bright teeth and eyes, a strong colour cast, misprices her to exactly the people she is asking for money, and a stiff corporate flash-on-white treatment makes a design studio founder look like an accountant. The collateral follows the same rule: air, one photograph doing the work, type that does not shout. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every crop is dimensionally correct. The ledger records the base concept at 400 to 900 dollars; this fuller commission, with the mark recovery and the editable canvases, runs 900 to 1,800 dollars fixed.

assets_supplied.name: vellacourt_session/ (9 frames, 5200px long edge)
assets_supplied.kind: image
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Nine frames I like out of the half-day. Shot on grey paper in a studio. The light moved during the afternoon and they do not match." Seated and standing, three-quarter and straight on, no other people.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two things she cannot see. First, she has thick curly hair and the studio grey sits close in value to it in the frames shot after the key light was moved, so the knockout on those frames returns an edge that is either cut hard into the curl or carries a soft pale rim of captured grey. On white and on the warm neutral both look perfectly clean, which is why every version she has tried looked fine until it went on her deck. Second, the frame she has already decided is the press headshot, the one she calls her favourite, is the coolest of the nine and the furthest from where the other eight can reasonably be brought, so bringing the set to one look and honouring her choice of hero pull against each other, and nothing in the frame announces this until the nine are laid out together after correction.

assets_supplied.name: vellacourt_deboss_card.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: image
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our original card. The two letters are pressed into the paper with no ink at all, just the impression. It is the only version of the monogram that exists and the printer has closed." A 4,000px phone frame of a white cotton card on a pale desk, shot under a window at a raking angle.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: A blind deboss carries no ink and no colour, so the mark exists only as the shadow the raking light throws in the relief, and it exists only on the side the light came from. On the lit side the letterforms have almost no edge at all. What a selection returns is therefore a property of that one photograph's light rather than of the mark, and what the trace yields is a set of soft shadow shapes that read convincingly as the monogram at full canvas and break into fragments at the size a profile picture reproduces it. There is no option on the tracing step to tune this, so the only lever is the raster preparation, and which preparation is needed cannot be known until the result is placed at its real delivered size.
