trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface.
trajectory.judgement: The sheets are record per page against a layout the client has told you to keep, so they belong on the merge surface. The line card, poster and slides do not exist yet, need three canvas sizes and must stay editable, so they belong on HTML authoring. Authoring the sheets from scratch throws away the layout the customers recognise; trying to merge the poster discovers record per page cannot produce three canvas sizes.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier.

trajectory.action: Upload the twelve frames, the 2025 sheet PDF, the stock-system export and the reference material, holding each presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Manifest discipline: thirty artefacts later the mapping between URL and SKU has to still be trustworthy.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by SKU and role.

trajectory.action: Preview all twelve frames and triage: which session, which finish, how level, how much contrast each part actually has against the bench it is lying on, and whether the part in each frame is the part the export row claims.
trajectory.judgement: The client says same bench, same camera. Half the range disagrees. The agent also has to notice which parts are the same value as their background before it decides how to derive anything from those frames, and to read the export against the pictures rather than assuming a thirteen-row export describes twelve parts.
trajectory.produces: A per-frame triage note covering session, finish, level, subject contrast and identity.

trajectory.action: Level the frames that are off level.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels, so it precedes any crop decision.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed.

trajectory.action: Fix one technical white from the better-lit session and correct each SKU toward it with its own parameter set, recording what was dialled per frame.
trajectory.judgement: One destination held across twelve frames, not twelve locally optimised pictures. Six frames need a materially different correction to arrive at the same neutral. A single batched call would apply one identical parameter set and ship half the range green.
trajectory.produces: Twelve graded masters at source scale with a per-frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Masked corrections to protect the finishes: hold the galvanised spangle out of brass, keep clear anodised from collapsing into powder coat, keep zinc plate bright without going blue.
trajectory.judgement: This is the client's actual commercial requirement rather than a cosmetic one. Prompt wording is the gate, and a material selection on a brushed steel part lying on a brushed steel bench may leak into the bench, which has to be recognised as leakage rather than accepted because the call succeeded.
trajectory.produces: Finish-protected masters with the masked parameters recorded per SKU.

trajectory.action: Derive the catalogue grid tile and the in-context bench crop for every SKU, reading the detection confidence and the tradeoffs each crop returns rather than trusting success, then lay the twelve tiles out as the index grid they are for.
trajectory.judgement: A subject-aware crop is a guess with a confidence attached, and the confidence lives in the response rather than in the picture. Consistent subject scale across twelve tiles is a set-level decision that cannot be made one tile at a time.
trajectory.produces: Twelve grid tiles and twelve bench crops, laid out as the index, with the crop metadata transcribed.

trajectory.action: Propose two neutral grounds for the data-sheet cutouts, a paper white and a light technical grey, and pick one against an engineering readership.
trajectory.judgement: A taste decision with a defence attached, and one that has to hold for four different finishes: a ground that flatters powder coat can bury clear anodised.
trajectory.produces: Two proposed grounds and a written pick.

trajectory.action: Isolate each SKU onto the chosen ground, routing per part: coherent solid bodies through the one-call knockout, parts with through-bores, open frames and enclosed handles through a material-named selection, inverted and filled to the ground.
trajectory.judgement: A knockout fills an enclosed bore with captured bench and reports success, and a sheave with a filled bore is a part the buyer does not recognise. The route is a per-part decision made by looking at the part.
trajectory.produces: Twelve neutral-ground cutouts with the route recorded per SKU.

trajectory.surface: Data preparation and Creative Cloud storage
trajectory.action: Reconcile the stock export against the pictures and the finishes note, normalise it into a merge-shaped data file with the image column in the form the merge contract requires and bare filenames in the cells, upload the sheet masters and build the image map against them.
trajectory.judgement: Real data-prep work: a superseded row the system still emits, part numbers carrying a spreadsheet artefact, and an image column that does not satisfy the contract. The agent decides which of those are its call and which the client's, and how to say so.
trajectory.produces: The merge data file, uploaded masters, the image map, and a first list of export questions.

trajectory.action: Convert the 2025 sheet to a native document, export IDML, unzip it, and read the true frame inventory and the true story text reconstructed by concatenating the content runs.
trajectory.judgement: The mapping strategy is decided by what the client's own system happened to produce, not by the plan. Two graphic frames come back distinguishable only by bounds and link, and deciding which one holds the part photograph rather than the drawing is a judgement made against the printed reference, not a name in the response.
trajectory.produces: The converted document, its IDML, a frame inventory with real ids and bounds, and the reconstructed story text.

trajectory.action: Author the mapping covering every spec field plus the photograph, ordering any rows that share a uid against the original text, and pass it through the validator.
trajectory.judgement: Choosing the right action for the granularity that came back, computing offsets from a source of truth the agent has chosen deliberately, and passing the whole mapping across as one stringified object with integer page-item ids.
trajectory.produces: A validated mapping covering the spec fields and the image frame.

trajectory.action: Prepare the merge template, then export IDML from the RESULT, unzip it and grep the story for every placeholder the mapping claimed to create.
trajectory.judgement: Not accepting a success message as evidence. Nothing instructs this and nothing warns if it is skipped, and it is the only place the mapping's real yield is visible before pages exist.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholder inventory has been independently confirmed.

trajectory.action: Merge to a native document with the per-row photographs bound, render the press file and the proofs at 300 ppi, and produce per-part sheets named to part number, identity-verified by opening each file.
trajectory.judgement: Merging straight to raster silently drops to screen resolution whatever is asked for, and merging straight to PDF forfeits the per-record branch, so the route is chosen deliberately. Naming twelve sheets by the order they came back is the fast wrong answer and it is the one a road rep discovers in front of a customer.
trajectory.produces: The press sheet file, 300 ppi proofs and twelve identity-verified named sheets.

trajectory.action: Read every rendered sheet against the export and against the 2025 printed reference, line by line and photograph by photograph, at true trim rather than at proof scale.
trajectory.judgement: Reading the output rather than the log. A field that never became a placeholder, a compliance string that does not fit, and a photograph in the drawing's frame all look like success at the API boundary and all look plausible at proof scale.
trajectory.produces: A page-by-page reconciliation of the rendered sheets against the export.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for one service or machine-room context frame, filter to photography, exclude generative-tech results, license and download at full resolution, then grade it toward the technical neutral and judge it beside the range.
trajectory.judgement: An atmosphere frame at this band has to be flat and plausible rather than dramatic. A dark cinematic machine room is the wrong answer for a parts catalogue no matter how good it looks at thumbnail size.
trajectory.produces: One licensed camera-scale context frame, graded, judged in or out.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, read the real numeric weights from the style inventories, launder every name, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own and has to read technical rather than consumer. Numeric weight cannot be inferred from a style name, a display cut is reached by its own slug, and one bad name kills the whole kit including the valid faces beside it.
trajectory.produces: One kit with family, foundry or designer and the actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self-contained HTML with roots at three canvas sizes (A4 line card, A1 counter poster at true physical dimensions, meeting slides), the spec comparison as a real table, the dimensional drawing as inline vector inside an explicitly sized and top-left anchored wrapper, every photograph base64 inlined, family and weight declared on every text element, each root declaring its own canvas size. Upload by the allowed-host route, run the readiness check, export, then verify canvas one through its rendition and the remaining canvases through the returned markup.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, so the export is unverified until it is inspected, and the preview only shows the first canvas. The design decisions, how much of the A1 is table and how much is photograph, whether the line card leads with the range or the service promise, are the actual work.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document with all three canvas sizes, its durable source HTML, and a per-canvas markup audit.

trajectory.action: Create the approval board with the graded range and the licensed frame, within the placement cap and re-sending only the entries named as failed. Then write the handover.
trajectory.judgement: What to escalate versus what to fix silently. The note has to let the next freelancer rebuild the sheet from the same PDF without repeating the archaeology, and it has to name the compliance strings that will not fit and the export row that was excluded, before a printer sees the file.
trajectory.produces: A persistent approval board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether a subject-aware crop found the part. Three SKUs are long, thin and made of the same brushed steel as the bench beneath them, so the crop has almost no contrast to work with and latches onto the one high-contrast feature in the frame, returning a tight, sharp, well-composed crop of a painted end fitting or a yellow cable jacket, at a detection confidence well under any level worth trusting, while reporting complete success. Which frames behave that way is a property of these particular photographs (this part on this bench under this light) and cannot be predicted from the SKU list, the finishes note or the frame previews. The tile looks like a competent product tile. It is a picture of a fragment.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and care alone does not either. The failure is produced by a detection step whose only honest signal is a confidence value and a bounds rectangle buried in a response that otherwise reads as success, and the crop that comes back is genuinely well composed, so there is no visual alarm in the artefact itself. An agent can only learn which frames are affected by running the crop on each of them and either reading the confidence or laying the twelve tiles out together and noticing that three of them are showing the wrong thing. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for a grid tile per part that shows the whole part rather than a corner of it, which is an ordinary client quality requirement, and says nothing about contrast, detection or which parts are at risk. No asset description names the three SKUs, and no earlier step reports subject contrast as a number. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to abandon the subject-aware route for those frames and drive the crop from an explicit selection's own bounds instead, which is a different operation on a different input, and then to re-take the scale policy for the whole grid, because three tiles derived a different way will not sit at the same subject scale as the other nine unless the policy is re-decided across all twelve.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-derive the affected tiles by making an explicit selection of the part, taking its bounds, and cropping to those bounds with padding, rather than asking the crop to find the subject. Then re-lay all twelve tiles and re-decide the subject scale policy so the re-derived three sit with the nine, which in practice means re-cropping some of the nine as well. Transcribe every crop's reported metadata into the handover so the client can see which tiles were produced by which route.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A catalogue index in which three of twelve parts are represented by a sharp, confident photograph of the wrong end of the part, sent to buyers who order by looking at the picture and then reading the number beside it, from a supplier whose entire pitch is that the picture and the number agree.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's sheet actually exposes, and then whether the mapping built against it landed. Two things arrive only by running. First, the granularity: the fourteen-row spec table came out of the distributor's system as ONE continuous story with tab characters between parameter and value, so there are no per-parameter frames to map and everything must be driven by ordered offsets inside a single story, and the two graphic frames are distinguishable only by bounds and link. Second, the yield: the mapping readout of that story omits the run holding the compliance footnote while keeping its line break, so the string still parses as well-formed and every offset past it is short by exactly that run's length. The validator returns valid on internally consistent wrong arithmetic, the placeholder step reports success, and the two fields past the omission never become placeholders.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and diligence alone cannot either. Granularity is not a parameter, is not reported before the conversion, and has no read-ahead: the only route to the answer is to convert, export and read. The yield failure is worse, because it is produced by a convenience readout that presents as complete, so an agent that reads carefully and computes offsets diligently from the readout it was handed produces arithmetic that is internally consistent and wrong, and every downstream tool agrees with it. The only defence is an independent reconstruction of the same text from a different channel, which nothing in any tool description prompts and whose necessity is invisible until the two disagree. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says keep the sheet exactly as it is and put this year's specs through it, and mentions no frames, fields, stories or offsets. The acceptance bar states an output requirement, that every field the 2025 sheet carried is present on every page, which is the client's standing requirement rather than a warning. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The source of truth behind the mapping changes, from a tool readout to a reconstructed story, and with it the whole mapping is re-authored with re-ordered same-uid rows. If the photograph turns out to have been mapped into the drawing's frame, the image binding is re-planned before the merge rather than after.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story by concatenating the IDML content runs, recompute every offset against that string, re-order rows sharing a uid so their positions hold against the original text, rebuild and re-validate the mapping, re-run the template preparation, and re-verify by round-tripping IDML and grepping for every placeholder before a single page is merged. Settle which of the two graphic frames holds the photograph by rendering a page and reading it against the 2025 printed reference rather than by assuming the larger frame is the photograph.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Twelve data sheets that bind part number, description and most of the spec table correctly while the compliance line and the field after it are silently absent from every page, printed and put on a counter for technicians who order to those exact values, with every tool in the chain having reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the importer actually did with the two constructs the collateral depends on: the dimensional line drawing carried in as vector, and the spec comparison carried in as a real table. Neither the drawing's leader lines and dash treatment nor the table's per-cell strokes and cell backgrounds can be confirmed to have survived by any means other than reading the markup the import returns, and every drop this importer performs comes back as a success with no warning at all. The A1 poster and the slides compound it: the rendition preview shows the first canvas only, so whatever happened on the poster and the slides is reported by the returned markup and by nothing else.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it. How this importer normalises a given construct is not documented anywhere the agent can read ahead, is not a parameter, and is not signalled by the response status. Authoring the drawing more carefully does not tell you what happened to it, and the one visual channel available shows only the canvas that is least likely to be affected. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for live text and a drawing that is real artwork rather than a picture of a page, which is the client's requirement for an editable file, and it names no construct, no importer and no failure. No earlier step claims to have solved it, because no earlier step has exported anything. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to re-author the construct itself, which means redrawing the dimensional artwork in a form that survives, or rebuilding the comparison in a different structure, and then re-running the readiness check and re-exporting, and the layout around the changed construct changes with it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Parse the returned markup per canvas and check, for each canvas rather than only the first: that every photograph resolved to real image data rather than the importer's placeholder, that the drawing arrived as path shapes rather than one flattened element or nothing at all, that the table arrived as real cells rather than a stack of loose text, that every text element carries the intended face and weight rather than a silent fallback, and that no element's resolved position runs past its declared canvas width. Then re-author whichever constructs did not survive, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and inspect again rather than assuming the second export took.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A counter poster and a slide set delivered as the client's editable file in which the dimensional drawing is gone or flattened, the spec comparison is a heap of loose text, and nobody notices because the only page anyone looked at was the line card.

deliverables.name: Girdermark range photography, twelve SKUs at one technical white
deliverables.spec: Twelve in-house frames from two sessions brought to one technical neutral with the four finishes still distinguishable from one another, delivered as a catalogue grid tile and an in-context bench crop per SKU at consistent subject scale, plus one licensed context frame graded into the same neutral. Every output at or below its source pixel dimensions, with a per-frame parameter log and one line per frame on why it differs from its neighbours, and every crop's reported detection and tradeoff metadata transcribed.

deliverables.name: Neutral-ground SKU cutouts for the data sheets
deliverables.spec: Twelve parts isolated onto the agreed neutral ground for the sheets, with through-bores, open frames and enclosed handles genuinely open rather than filled with captured bench, and the isolation route recorded per SKU because parts that are single coherent solids and parts that enclose voids cannot be produced the same way. True finish colour preserved through the isolation, since a buyer specifies from these pictures.

deliverables.name: Girdermark 2027 data sheets, press file plus per-part named sheets
deliverables.spec: US Letter portrait, one part per page in export order, page count equal to the current part count, rendered at 300 ppi at trim. Every page binds the fourteen spec parameters, the description, the compliance line and both prices verbatim from the stock export, plus that part's own photograph in the correct graphic frame. Accompanied by one single-page sheet per part named to the part number and identity-verified by opening it, and by 300 ppi proofs. Produced by reverse-engineering the printer's flat PDF into a live merge template, which is handed back with the record of how it was derived.

deliverables.name: Counter and road set: line card, A1 counter poster and March slides
deliverables.spec: One native editable Express document holding roots at three canvas sizes: an A4 line card, an A1 trade-counter poster at true physical dimensions, and the distributor meeting slides. Live editable text throughout in one licensed type system, the spec comparison as a genuine table, the dimensional drawing as real vector artwork, every photograph carried as embedded image data. Delivered with the self-contained source it was authored from, so prices can be changed without a re-commission and the design survives the document's own retention.

deliverables.name: Handover note and approval board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording per frame what was applied and why it differs from its neighbours, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and actual numeric weight, the explicit statement that the sheet's typography remains the printer's because no font can reach that surface, what the conversion exposed and the mapping decisions taken against it, every export row questioned and its resolution, the compliance strings that will not fit inside the sheet as it stands, and every resize any tool reported. Paired with a persistent approval board carrying the graded range and the licensed frame with nothing silently dropped.

verifiers_auto.text: The press sheet file has exactly one page per current part in export order and renders at 300 ppi at US Letter trim (2550 x 3300 px).
verifiers_auto.how: Count pages in the rendered PDF against the reconciled part count and check the render call's resolution and the output raster dimensions.

verifiers_auto.text: Every spec field, the description, the compliance line and both prices appear on every page of the merged output.
verifiers_auto.how: Round-trip the prepared template to IDML and grep for every expected placeholder, then read text off each rendered page and compare against its export row.

verifiers_auto.text: Every grid tile contains the whole part, and every crop's reported detection confidence and tradeoffs are transcribed in the handover.
verifiers_auto.how: Compare each tile's coverage against its source frame and against an explicit selection's bounds for that SKU; check the handover for the transcribed metadata per crop.

verifiers_auto.text: No delivered file exceeds its source frame on either axis and no crop response carried an upscale entry.
verifiers_auto.how: Compare delivered dimensions against source dimensions and inspect every tradeoffs array.

verifiers_auto.text: The exported Express document holds three canvases at three distinct declared sizes, with the A1 poster at true physical dimensions, every photograph resolved to real image data, the drawing present as path shapes and the comparison present as real table cells.
verifiers_auto.how: Read slide_count and per-slide dimensions from the export response and parse each canvas's returned markup for placeholder images, path-type shapes, table cell structure and out-of-canvas resolved positions.

verifiers_auto.text: Twelve per-part sheet files exist, each named to a part number, each containing the part its name claims.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the part number off each single-page file and compare with its filename, never with its position in the returned list.

verifiers_auto.text: Every text element in the exported document carries a resolved licensed face and the intended numeric weight rather than a fallback.
verifiers_auto.how: Compare the resolved font families and weights in the returned markup against the kit's families and the weights read from the style inventory.

verifiers_human.text: Laid out as the catalogue index, the twelve parts read as one range shot the same way on the same day.
verifiers_human.how: View the twelve grid tiles together and judge neutral, white point, black point and subject scale as a set rather than one at a time.

verifiers_human.text: The four finishes remain distinguishable and none has been pushed toward a colour the part is not.
verifiers_human.how: Compare the delivered pictures of galvanised, zinc-plated, clear-anodised and powder-coated parts against the finishes note and against each other.

verifiers_human.text: Through-bores, open frames and enclosed handles are genuinely open in the cutouts.
verifiers_human.how: Place each cutout on a contrasting ground and look through the voids.

verifiers_human.text: The collateral reads flat, accurate and technical rather than consumer or cinematic, appropriate to a 400 to 9,000 dollar part and a twenty-year buyer.
verifiers_human.how: Review the line card, poster and slides against the price band and audience description and reject styled, warm or shallow-depth treatments.

verifiers_human.text: The handover escalates rather than conceals, naming the excluded export row, the compliance strings that will not fit, and the fact that the sheet's typography could not be changed.
verifiers_human.how: Read the handover against the triage, conversion and render findings and check each is disclosed with the decision taken.

decision_gates: The surface split: sheets to the merge surface because the layout is fixed client property and the run is record per page, counter set to HTML authoring because it needs three canvas sizes and must stay editable.
Which session sets the technical white, knowing a warm reference makes plated steel look brassy across the whole catalogue.
How far to correct the second session before the correction itself becomes a finish change the buyer can see.
Whether a subject-aware crop found the part, on frames where the part and the bench are the same metal and the response says success either way.
Subject scale policy across twelve tiles, decided as a set rather than per tile, and re-decided once any tile is derived a different way.
Isolation route per SKU: the one-call knockout is right for a solid body and wrong for a sheave with a bore, and the wrong route returns a filled bore that reports success.
Which of two indistinguishable graphic frames holds the part photograph rather than the dimensional drawing.
Whether to trust the mapping readout of the client's own spec table or to reconstruct the story independently from the document.
Whether a success message counts as verification of the prepared template.
How to honour 'nothing shortened or reworded' when three compliance strings do not fit the sheet as it stands, given no way to change a frame.
Whether to name twelve sheets by the order they came back or by opening each one.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a technical readership, plus the disclosure that no chosen face can reach the printed sheet at all.
Whether the licensed context frame reads as a plausible service environment or as marketing photography, which is the wrong register for a parts catalogue.
why_not_vlm: Paste this brief and these frames into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of machinery. IDENTITY: these are twelve specific parts with specific finishes that a technician orders and installs, and a generated part fabricates a finish, which on a page that also carries load and duty values is effectively a false spec claim. SPEC: the client needs one sheet per current part at US Letter and 300 ppi with fourteen spec values bound verbatim from their own stock export, twelve separately named sheet files each containing the part their filename claims, a grid tile per part showing the whole part, and no delivered file larger than its source. None of that can be produced or checked by generation. EDITABILITY: two deliverables are defined by being editable, a live merge template so next season's specs are a data change, and a native document with live text, a real table and real vector artwork so prices can move in March. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did this placeholder get created, did this crop find the part, is this photograph in the photograph's frame, do these four finishes still read as four finishes. That is not a generation problem.
doability_proof: Every link is verified in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account); the surface count is five and honestly declared, and image_vectorize is not claimed as an Illustrator surface (the genuine Illustrator tools are never called because document_render_vector and document_merge_data_vector sit on a polling helper that does not exist in this host). MERGE SPINE: building a merge template from a bare PDF end to end headlessly is verified, one record per page is confirmed for PDF output, per-record named files are confirmed by two order-verified routes while multi-record raster order is documented as reversed and is therefore never used for identity, and true 300 ppi at US Letter (2550 x 3300) comes from document_render_layout because outputSpecs.resolution on the merge is documented as silently ignored. THE SHEET PDF IS BUILT TO A VERIFIED SHAPE: v3 observed that placed images interleaved with text split the flow into multiple text frames plus graphic frames, and that a continuous flow collapses to a single frame; this asset carries a continuous tab-delimited spec story plus two placed images, so the expected yield is a small number of text frames plus two graphic frames whose only differentiators are bounds and link, exactly as v3 describes them. The PDF must be a real font-embedding press PDF from a full engine, since a thin hand-authored PDF fails conversion opaquely. The lossy-readout defect is verify-then-ship: before admission, run the conversion and the mapping generator and confirm the returned textContent is short by exactly one run against the IDML-reconstructed story; if it will not reproduce, the checkpoint still stands on the granularity fact, which is verified and controllable. THE CROP CHECKPOINT IS A DOCUMENTED LIVE FINDING, NOT AN ASSUMPTION: v3 records that fit extract with a prompt focus silently mis-cropped sparse art to a fragment at detection_confidence 0.459 with detection_source image_select_by_prompt while reporting success, and advises falling back to crop_to_bounds driven by an explicit selection's returnBbox below about 0.6, which is exactly the rework this task encodes. IMAGE BINDING: per-row binding through an at-prefixed column plus additionalImageFiles keyed to bare filenames is verified at three keys; this task binds twelve, so the verified recordRange loop is carried as an explicit fallback and also guarantees per-record identity. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, single_color_saturation, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, select_subject, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs array, remove_background with backgroundColor and fill_area are all verified headless; the enclosed-aperture failure of remove_background, the binary non-anti-aliased mask and the substrate-versus-material prompt asymmetry are documented findings. No upscaling is asserted: crop_and_resize interpolates to a hard 2x cap signalled only in tradeoffs and remove_background silently downscales oversized inputs, so the bar scores the decision and the disclosure separately. EXPRESS: multi-root export with mixed canvas sizes is verified, mm canvases resolve at exactly 96 dpi so A1 and A4 are true physical canvases, tables survive as real tables with per-cell backgrounds and strokes, and inline SVG becomes native editable vector; transport is routed through the text/html upload because inlined photography passes the 70 KB inline threshold, and verification is split because the rendition preview shows page one only. FONTS: the recommend, styles, find, embed chain is verified end to end, and the task leans on the non-standard numeric weights, the slug-not-PostScript rule and the all-or-nothing kit call; the impossibility of getting a font file onto the InDesign surface is stated as a client-facing constraint rather than silently ignored. STOCK AND BOARDS: short generic queries only, licensing returns genuine camera-scale files, board placements are capped at twelve per call with partial success signalled by failedItems. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no bleed gate, no pdfPreset, no fill_text, no animate_design or create_firefly_board, no replace_image, no download_design, no upscaling, no OCR, no compositing, no generated imagery, no photo reaching Express as a URL, and no batch above twenty files.
